docs.text: 🌸 Amerilis Lovelace Liadon – The Child of Undone Seasons ¶ Archive audit notice: This handout was released before Session 077 and may contain older mechanics, names, links, or lore phrasing that still needs review. The table's latest ruling is authoritative. ❄️ Racial Abilities ¶ Darkvision. You can see in dim light within 60 feet as if it were bright light, and in darkness as if it were dim light. Fey Ancestry. You have advantage on saving throws against being charmed , and magic can’t put you to sleep . Keen Senses. You have proficiency in the Perception skill. Trance. Elves don’t need to sleep. Instead, they meditate deeply for 4 hours a day. Frostveins ¶ You have resistance to cold damage due to your Winter Eladrin heritage. Igni Blood ¶ Your Summer Eladrin heritage fuels your flames with ancestral wrath. Once per turn , when you deal fire damage with a spell or ability, you can choose one instance of fire damage to gain extra damage. The bonus fire damage is based on your character level: +1d4 / +1d6 / +1d8 / +1d12 at 1st / 5th / 11th / 17th level 🔥 The Mark of Thaurë’Vanya ¶ (“Flame-Fated Grace” in Elvish-inspired etymology) A forbidden union. A flame sealed in frost. A future not written, but burned into being. World Lore ¶ Among Feywilds's elven cultures, mingling Winter and Summer Eladrin bloodlines is not only taboo—it is feared. Each lineage embodies a seasonal ideal, and combining them is thought to disrupt magic, weather, and prophecy. Children born of both are said to be impossible. But Amerilis was born with the Mark of Thaurë’Vanya , a mythic glyph long suppressed in song and legend. Upon her Eladrin awakening, it ignited—flame and feylight. Prophecy fragments refer to her as: - “The herald of undone seasons” - “The flame that blooms in the snow” - “The child born of ice and fire” Some fear her. Some seek her. Few understand her. Mark of Thaurë’Vanya (Racial Feature) ¶ You gain sorcery points equal to 1/3 your level (rounded up). These points can only be used to enhance or modify fire or cold spells . These sorcery points refresh after a long rest . If you are a sorcerer, treat this as a separate sorcery pool , usable only for spells that deal fire/cold damage. (Including elementals) Suggested Metamagic Use: ¶ Subtle Spell (1 SP): Remove verbal and somatic components —ideal for silent casting or spellcasting while restrained. Distant Spell (1 SP): When you cast a fire/cold spell that has a range of 5 feet or greater, you can spend 1 sorcery point to double the range of the spell. Empowered Spell (1 SP): Reroll damage dice for fire/cold spells (up to your INT modifier ). Careful Spell (1 SP): Prevent friendly fire; up to INT modifier allies automatically succeed on their saving throws. Twinned Spell (1+ SP): Duplicate single-target fire/cold spells (e.g. Ray of Frost , Fire Bolt , Ice Knife ). Quickened Spell (2 SP): Cast a fire or cold spell as a bonus action . Heightened Spel (3 SP): Give one target of the spell disadvantage on its first saving throw made against a fire/cold spell. Cloak of Winter’s Grace ¶ Wondrous item, Uncommen (requires attunement) While wearing this ancestral garment: +1 AC +1 on all saving throws You ignore cold-based environmental effects including difficult terrain Your icy lineage pulses with subtle defiance, marking you as a scion of the Hoarfrost Reach. “This was your grandmother Elvarelle’s,” Ivanna says. “Not as flashy as that flame-spitting gremlin, but we can’t have you running off without representing both sides of the family.” 🔮 Lindarcalen – The Emberdream Brooch ¶ Wondrous item, rare (requires attunement by an elf or fey-touched creature) “In the twilight halls of House Val’Ignira, where hearts burned with pride and dreams sang with flame, the brooch Lindarcalen shimmered with memory and power…” A delicate brooch of rose-gold and veined moonstone , shaped like a flame entwined with a harp . It glows faintly warm, humming with a song only dreamers hear. ✨ Properties ¶ Dreamfire Vision (1/long rest) ¶ Enter a lucid Feywild dream after a long rest. Receive a symbolic vision (like legend lore ) about: - Fey beings - Magical places - Forgotten histories Dreams are poetic, eerie, and metaphor-laced. Fey-Tuned Heart ¶ You have advantage on Charisma checks with fey creatures and elven nobility. The brooch marks you as a blood heir of the Summer Court. Mindfire Resistance ¶ Advantage on saving throws vs. charm, fright, and magical control (e.g., dominate person , suggestion ). Your mind is warded by the dreaming flame. 🔥 Flamelit Companion – Cinderkin ¶ A tiny fey flame spirit bound to Lindarcalen. Mischievous, squeaky-voiced, and flickers like Calcifer from Howl’s Moving Castle . Summoning Cinderkin ¶ Bonus action to summon. Floats on your shoulder or cloak. Understands and speaks Sylvan . Lasts 1 hour/day , extended by feeding wood. Combat Effect – Emberflare Wings (1/combat, Reaction) ¶ +5 AC until your next turn. Hover 30 ft. in any direction (no opportunity attacks, as majestic flaming wings burst from your back). If you end your turn in the air you slowly glide to the ground. Upon activation, a burst of dreamflame erupts in a 20-foot radius around you: Each enemy in the area takes 4d6 fire damage. Must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw (DC = your spell save DC) or be blinded until the end of their next turn, dazzled by the incandescent blaze of fey-born fire. “It was not the heat that stunned them—it was the light. Like watching the moment of their own unraveling.” Utility Uses ¶ Acts as light source or magical heater. Animates small flames (e.g. teapots, fireplaces). May whisper cryptic Feywild truths to Amerilis. “They named you calamity before you spoke your name. Not because you would end the world… …but because you might choose not to follow its ending.”

docs.text: 🎓 Amerilis’s Spellbook – Level 12 Illusionist Elf Wizard ¶ Archive audit notice: This handout was released before Session 077 and may contain older mechanics, names, links, or lore phrasing that still needs review. The table's latest ruling is authoritative. 📜 Daily Spell Preparation ¶ 🎯 You may check up to 17 total spells per long rest (Wizard Level 12 + INT 20). Cantrips are always known and don’t count toward the limit. 🪄 Cantrips (Always prepared — auto-scaled for level 12) ¶ [x] Minor Illusion (Illusion Cantrip) 📏 Range: 30 ft 🕒 Casting Time: 1 action ⏳ Duration: 1 minute (Concentration not required) 🔮 Create a sound or image that fits in a 5-ft cube. The image is static and silent; the sound can range from a whisper to a scream. 🎭 Used to distract, disguise, or create false cover. Perfect for misdirection or creative problem solving. Creatures may investigate (INT check) to disbelieve. [x] Prestidigitation (Transmutation Cantrip) 📏 Range: 10 ft 🕒 Casting Time: 1 action ⏳ Duration: Up to 1 hour ✨ Create harmless sensory effects. Excellent for flair, subtle signals, or RP flavor. Such as: flavor food, clean or soil an object, light/snuff small flame, chill/warm an item. [x] Dancing Lights (Evocation Cantrip) 📏 Range: 120 ft 🕒 Casting Time: 1 action ⏳ Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute 💡 Create 4 torch-sized lights (dim light in 10 ft each) that float, move, or form into a glowing humanoid shape. 🌀 Lights can move up to 60 ft as a bonus action . [x] Ray of Frost (Evocation Cantrip) 📏 Range: 60 ft 🕒 Casting Time: 1 action ❄️ Fire a beam of cold at one creature: Hit: 3d8 cold damage (Level 11+) Effect: Target’s speed is reduced by 10 ft until your next turn. [x] Fire Bolt (Evocation Cantrip) 📏 Range: 120 ft 🕒 Casting Time: 1 action 🔥 Launch a mote of fire at a creature or flammable object: Hit: 3d10 fire damage (Level 11+) Special: Ignites flammable objects not worn or carried. [x] Mage Hand (Conjuration Cantrip) 📏 Range: 30 ft 🕒 Casting Time: 1 action ⏳ Duration: 1 minute 🤲 Summon a spectral hand that can: Open doors, pick up or drop items, interact with simple objects. [x] Message (Transmutation Cantrip) 📏 Range: 120 ft 🕒 Casting Time: 1 action ⏳ Duration: 1 round 💬 Whisper a short message to a creature within range, even through objects or walls (as long as there's a path). Target can whisper back immediately. Ideal for stealth missions, split parties, or hidden talk mid-combat. 🔹 1st-Level Spells - ☐ ☐ ☐ ☐ ¶ [_] Burning Hands — Action, Self (15-ft cone), DEX save. 3d6 fire ; +1d6/slot . [_] Chromatic Orb — Action, 90 ft, spell attack. 3d8 chosen type ( fire / cold fits theme); +1d8/slot . [_] Ice Knife — Action, 60 ft. Hit: 1d10 piercing (attack); then burst: 2d6 cold in 5 ft (DEX half); +1d6 cold/slot . [_] Thunderwave — Action, Self (15-ft cube), CON save. 2d8 thunder ; push 10 ft; +1d8/slot . [_] Ray of Sickness — Action, 60 ft, spell attack. 2d8 poison ; CON save or poisoned until end of your next turn; +1d8/slot . [_] Sleep (Illusion-ish glamor) — Action, 90 ft. Affects 5d8 HP (no damage). [_] Silent Image (Illusion) — Action, 60 ft, Conc., 10 min. 15-ft cube moving image (no damage). [_] Disguise Self (Illusion) — Action, Self, 1 hr. Change appearance (no damage). [_] Mage Armor — Action, touch, 8 hr. AC = 13 + Dex (no damage). [_] Shield — Reaction, Self. +5 AC until your next turn (no damage). 🔷 2nd-Level Spells - ☐ ☐ ☐ ¶ [_] Scorching Ray — Action, 120 ft, spell attacks. Create 3 rays ; each ray 2d6 fire on hit; +1 ray/slot . [_] Flaming Sphere — Action, 60 ft, Conc., 1 min. Ram/end-of-turn 2d6 fire (DEX half); +1d6/slot . [_] Dragon’s Breath — Action, touch, Conc., 1 min. Target gains 15-ft cone for 3d6 ( fire / cold ) as bonus action (DEX half); +1d6/slot . [_] Aganazzar’s Scorcher — Action, 30-ft×5-ft line, DEX save. 3d8 fire ; +1d8/slot . [_] Snilloc’s Snowball Swarm — Action, 90 ft, 5-ft radius, DEX save. 3d6 cold ; +1d6/slot . [_] Mirror Image (Illusion) — Action, Self, 1 min. Three duplicates (no attack roll against you often). [_] Blur — Action, Self, Conc., 1 min. Attacks vs you at disadvantage. [_] Invisibility (Illusion) — Action, touch, Conc., 1 hr. Turn a creature invisible. [_] Phantasmal Force (Illusion) — Action, 60 ft, Conc., 1 min, INT save. Mental illusion; 1d6 psychic/round if it “interacts.” [_] Darkness — Action, 60 ft, 15-ft radius, 10 min. Magical darkness / area denial. 🔶 3rd-Level Spells - ☐ ☐ ☐ ¶ [_] Fireball — Action, 150 ft, 20-ft radius, DEX save. 8d6 fire ; +1d6/slot . [_] Melf’s Minute Meteors — Action, Self, Conc., 10 min. Six meteors; when cast and as bonus actions send 1–2 meteors (each 2d6 fire , DEX half). +2 meteors/slot . [_] Sleet Storm — Action, 150 ft, 40-ft radius, Conc., 1 min. Difficult terrain, obscured; drops concentration (no damage on cast). [_] Major Image (Illusion) — Action, 120 ft, Conc., 10 min. Large illusion incl. sound, light, smell. [_] Hypnotic Pattern (Illusion) — Action, 120 ft, 30-ft cube, WIS save. Incapacitates/charmed on fail (no damage). [_] Counterspell — Reaction, 60 ft. Interrupt a spell (no damage). 🟦 4th-Level Spells - ☐ ☐ ☐ ¶ [_] Fire Shield — Action, Self, 10 min. Choose warm (resist cold ) or chill (resist fire ); a melee attacker within 5 ft takes 2d8 ( fire or cold , matching shield). [_] Wall of Fire — Action, 120 ft, Conc., 1 min. 60-ft line or ring; one side deals 5d8 fire/round (DEX half); +1d8/slot . [_] Ice Storm — Action, 300 ft, 20-ft radius, DEX save. 2d8 bludgeoning + 4d6 cold ; difficult terrain; +1d6 cold/slot . [_] Conjure Minor Elementals — Action, Self, Conc., 10 min. Elemental spirits swirl in 15-ft emanation; your attacks deal +2d8 elemental (acid/cold/fire/lightning) on hits in the area; +1d8/slot ; enemies in area have difficult terrain. [_] Summon Elemental — Action, 90 ft, Conc., 1 hr. Call a single elemental spirit (choose fire / air / earth / water ); it fights for you with level-scaled stats. [_] Greater Invisibility (Illusion) — Action, touch, Conc., 1 min. Invisibility that persists through attacking/casting. [_] Hallucinatory Terrain (Illusion) — 10 min, 300 ft, 24 hr. Disguise terrain over a large area (no damage). [_] Phantasmal Killer (Illusion) — Action, 120 ft, Conc., 1 min, WIS save. Frightened; 4d10 psychic/round on fails. 🟪 5th-Level Spells - ☐ ☐ ¶ [_] Cone of Cold — Action, Self (60-ft cone), CON save. 8d8 cold ; +1d8/slot . [_] Immolation — Action, 90 ft, DEX save. 8d6 fire (half on save); ongoing 4d6 fire at end of target’s turns (save ends). [_] Wall of Force — Action, 120 ft, Conc., 10 min. Nearly indestructible barrier (no damage). [_] Mislead (Illusion) — Action, Self, Conc., 1 hr. You turn invisible and create an illusory double. [_] Conjure Elemental — Action, 90 ft, Conc., 1 hr. Conjure a Large elemental spirit (choose fire / air / earth / water ); 2024 version uses an aura/space interaction to punish foes that enter/linger near it. 🟥 6th-Level Spells - ☐ ¶ [_] Wall of Ice — Action, 120 ft, Conc., 10 min. Create panels/dome. On appearance, creatures it cuts through take 10d6 cold (DEX half). Crossing the frigid sheet later: 5d6 cold (CON half). Upcast: +2d6 (on create) & +1d6 (on pass) per slot above 6th. ([Roll20][7]) [_] Otiluke’s Freezing Sphere — Action, 300 ft, 60-ft radius, CON save. 10d6 cold ; special interactions with water; +1d6/slot . [_] Investiture of Flame — Action, Self, Conc., 10 min. Fire aura + ranged line option; resist fire; attackers take fire dmg (values per spell). [_] Investiture of Ice — Action, Self, Conc., 10 min. Cold aura + difficult terrain + ranged hail attack; resist cold. [_] Programmed Illusion (Illusion) — Action, 120 ft, until dispelled. Complex illusion triggers on conditions (no damage). [_] Disintegrate — Action, 60 ft, DEX save (negates). On fail 10d6 + 40 force ; reduces to dust on 0 HP. Default 17 (e.g., Fireball, Cone of Cold, Scorching Ray, Flaming Sphere, Dragon’s Breath, Wall of Fire, Fire Shield, Ice Storm, Wall of Ice, Sleet Storm, Hypnotic Pattern, Major Image, Greater Invisibility, Phantasmal Killer, Summon Elemental, Counterspell, Shield)

docs.text: Welcome to Armskirk! ¶ Pick From the Visitor Brochure Rack ¶ Complimentary maps! Questionably complimentary advice! Take whatever catches your eye. Armskirk accepts no responsibility for missed trains, overconfident tour guides, regrettable haircuts requested by the customer, or anything a talking bird repeats under oath. Looking Presentable, Feeling Better ¶ Brochure What It Promises Cloud Mirror Salon — Adventure, Apology, or Court Appearance? Haircuts, hot-towel shaves, beard shaping, braids, fur brushing, feather oiling, horn polishing, and emergency repairs after helmets. Ask for Farrah Faucet. She already knows why you are here. Lotus Hot Springs Day Pass Madam Yu Zhen offers affordable public mineral baths, steam rooms, towels, scrubs, massage, laundry service, and neighborhood gossip at no additional charge. Jade Steam Private Onsen Reserved mineral baths, carved screens, flowering courtyards, tea service, and staff professionally trained not to notice the next room. All guests must leave before sunset; overnight accommodations and eight-armed employees are officially unavailable. Hundred Herbs Hall — Travel-Weary Remedies Affordable salves, combat tonics, monster oils, throwing powders, hangover remedies, and expert advice against drinking all of them at once. Ink Dragon Tattoo House Consultation Zhen “Calamity” Jian offers protective tattoos, family crests, spirit animals, moonlit ink, and questions suspiciously better than the answers. Silver Needle Tailors — Repairs While You Wait Travel-cloak relining, formal fittings, festival clothes, armor-friendly alterations, and new sleeves after the old ones met heroism. Saint Dacius Civic Hospital Charity Evening Healers, donors, speeches, light refreshments, and opportunities to look generous in public while supporting one of Leonia’s finest hospitals. Dr. Molar’s Miracle Mandibles Demonstration A live dental-strength exhibition promising teeth “strong enough to chew iron, soft enough for soup.” Dentists have requested we stop printing that sentence. Xiaolong: Food, Shopping, and Culture ¶ Brochure What It Promises Xiaolong: The Little Dragon District A lantern-lit walking route through tea houses, noodle shops, import markets, shrines, bathhouses, salons, and street food stalls. Xiaolong Night Market Tasting Pass Steamed buns, mooncakes, spicy skewers, rare teas, and at least one food item the brochure refuses to translate. Snake Blood Alley Delicacy Crawl Monster-part cuisine, chili oil, exotic broths, waiver forms in very small print, and a commemorative spoon for survivors. Golden Carp Tea House Ceremony Clementine Pekoe serves delicate teas, mooncakes, canal views, chess tables, and the usual order of customers who insist they have never visited. The old men are definitely not information brokers. Moon Gate Open-Air Theater Tonight: The Last Lantern at Eclipse Ford , a classic Mian wartime romance featuring seven farewells, one sunrise, Lincohn with an axe, and no refunds for crying. Thousand Feather Garden Aviary Jewel-plumed cranes, talking parrots, moon owls, thunderpheasants, and strict warnings not to repeat anything the birds say in court. White Crane Dojo — Visitor Lessons Master Shrew Fu teaches crane forms, tiger forms, flowing-river forms, and the beginner discipline of discovering how flexible you are not. Visitors may observe quietly or ache educationally. Little Dragon Shrine — Luck for the Road Incense, ribbons, tiny carved dragons, and a quiet place to ask for protection, honor an ancestor, or improve the odds of a risky journey or worse business deal. Dragon Child Toy Shop Madam Lian Zhu and her grandson Bo offer carved dragons, wind-up lions, puzzle boxes, painted soldiers, paper lantern kits, and tiny clockwork beasts for children and suspiciously enthusiastic adults. Nine Lantern Import Hall Silk, porcelain, spices, paper charms, enchanted fans, rare teas, medicinal roots, and questionable “authentic relics.” Red Wheel Cartwright Demonstration Yard Lu Han, better known as “Cullen Bowhandle,” offers chariots, wagons, wheels, harnesses, axle repair, and a live demonstration of “proper load balance.” Fewer idiots loading it are not covered by warranty. Food Worth Missing a Train For ¶ Brochure What It Promises Borb’s Buns — Hot Steam, Full Hearts Borb and Marda Bunbury serve bao, dumplings, meat pies, sweets, and a line full of dockhands, rail workers, market aunties, and customers who brought their own chairs. Order loudly if certain, bravely if not, and do not ask Borb for ketchup. Kardarsha’s Curds & Curios — Arena Pop-Up Everyday wheels, battle bites, enchanted wedges, cursed clearance cheese, and samples sold by a cat who believes victory must be lined with dairy. Lactose-tolerance potions available for the brave but biologically unprepared. Rainy Day Armskirk for Miserable Tourists Covered markets, tea houses, museums, bathhouses, indoor food stalls, and warm places to complain about the weather. See the Respectable City ¶ Brochure What It Promises Grand Promenade Highlights A polished walking route through Armskirk’s finest hotels, hospitals, theaters, monuments, salons, and civic plazas. The Lion & Crown Historic Hotel Tour Famous guests, private balconies, chandelier-lit halls, and old portraits that may judge you. Old Armskirk in Two Hours or Less Alleys, monuments, old bridges, civic landmarks, and “authentic” history at a pace achievable only if being chased. Museum of Heroic Misunderstandings Wax figures, battle dioramas, inaccurate plaques, and a gift shop selling tiny swords to children. Museum of Illusions & Questionable Optics Impossible staircases, talking mirrors, vanishing doors, fake ghosts, and one hallway that insists it is longer on the inside. The Grand Marionette Hall Royal scandals, tragic clowns, tiny guillotines, heroic mice, and family entertainment according to an unusually broad definition of “family.” Armskirk Clocktower Ascent Sweeping city views, bell history, civic architecture, and mild regret halfway up the stairs. Grand Library Researcher’s Pass Marble halls, spiral stacks, maps, newspapers, and assistance from Grand Librarian Horace Folio—provided your question is specific and your page corners remain unfolded. Romance, Nightlife, and Plausible Deniability ¶ Brochure What It Promises Moonlit Canal Gondolas Private rides through lantern-lit waterways with music, wine, and dramatic sighing available for an additional fee. Wetwood's Brokeback Outfitters — Get High Together! Clint Wetwood guides mountain excursions for bachelors, confirmed bachelors, and men who become confirmed somewhere above the tree line. Includes sturdy horses, matching chaps, sunset ram-watching, secluded cabins, the famous One Bedroll Discount , and family cave packages at Putty Nutty Caverns. Bareback is a personal decision; the insurance company requires saddles. The Pink Pony Inn — Where the Fur Flies Madam Maeve Mane welcomes every well-behaved identity, while Butch Glassidy serves bardcore cocktails with professionally maintained plausible deniability. Add bar snacks, suspiciously modern lute remixes, dramatic performers, and enough private booths for everyone to mind their own business. No biting without consent. The Gilded Ring Casino & Social Club Cards, dice, fine drinks, lavish rooms, and the reliable opportunity to discover which of your instincts is most expensive. Membership has privileges; losing is open to everyone. The Velvet Cage — Tonight on Stage Cabaret, acrobatics, music, elaborate stage shows, and exclusive seating for patrons who prefer their entertainment lavish and their cloakroom questions minimal. Lovers’ Lookout Picnic Basket Deal Bread, fruit, cheese, two cups, and one bottle of Regretful Red for a romantic outing above the city. Ravens not included but unavoidable. Masquerade Ball This Weekend Masks, dancing, secret admirers, plausible deniability, and a complimentary ribbon no one explains. Lust Not Included: Discreet Lodgings Guide Private rooms, nightlife, cabarets, companionship services, and “cultural experiences” with very careful wording. Emergency Date Night Rescue Package Flowers, carriage, dinner reservation, apology card, and a backup excuse written by a professional liar. Civic Business and the Trials ¶ Brochure What It Promises Official Trials Spectator Schedule Debate times, arena exhibitions, public ceremonies, approved chants, prohibited horns, and concession locations. Schedule accuracy not guaranteed after anyone says “surprise round.” Hall of Accord Exterior Tour Statues, speeches, civic history, and absolutely no access to restricted doors no matter how confidently you walk toward them. Iron Ledger Exchange — Visitor Appointments Currency exchange, letters of credit, contract escrow, appraisals, business loans, and financial advice from people who can detect arithmetic fear. Ask for Sterling Worth. Beyond the Paved Streets ¶ Brochure What It Promises Putty Nutty Caverns — A Brokeback Family Adventure Come spelunk through the soft clay corridors of Armskirk’s most family-friendly natural wonder! Follow expert guides through glittering mineral pockets, echo chambers, and natural slides to earn the coveted “I Got Putty Nutty!” completion ribbon! Souvenir helmets are available in the gift shop. Putty Nutty Caverns has absolutely no connection to the thoroughly discredited rumor that a visitor died there. The tour company won the court case, and courts are famously never wrong. Beginner’s Crystal Cave Excursion Glowing crystals, echo pools, cave moss, gentle paths, and rocks that cost extra if you lick them. Advanced Spelunking: The Probably Safe Route Rope descents, tight passages, underground rivers, and the phrase “sign here first.” The Friendly Bat Conservatory Cave bats, fruit bats, messenger bats, educational talks, and one bat the guide insists is “just large for his age.”

docs.text: Armskirk ¶ Type: Free city and current capital of the Republic of Leonia Culture: Mercantile, theatrical, civic-minded, and loudly opinionated Population: About 165,000 permanent residents; more than 200,000 during major Trials seasons Founded: Roughly 430 years ago as a fortified ferry-market and coastal trade settlement Government seat: Hall of Accord Capital term: Year 17 of Armskirk's current twenty-year term Notable district: Xiaolong, the “Little Dragon” Known for: The Trials, public debate, markets, rain, rail traffic, and professionally delivered gossip Armskirk is the current capital of Leonia, though it does not own the title. The capital rotates among Armskirk, Torath, and Corvos every twenty years. Armskirk therefore treats national government like a very long festival: profitable, prestigious, exhausting, and eventually someone else's problem. The city is a mixture of grand civic halls, rain-dark stone, busy markets, theaters, old bridges, rail yards, lantern courts, and neighborhoods built by generations of arrivals from across Suvaria. Blue-and-gold lion banners hang over the broad avenues. Beneath them, merchants sell food, newspapers shout about politics, and citizens explain—with diagrams—how they could run the republic better. The Capital at Work ¶ The Hall of Accord is both Leonia's government complex and its grandest political stage. Public debates take place in its amphitheater before the Audience, while the Barker Circle, Jugglers, Stagehands, clerks, guards, and archivists keep the republic moving in the rooms behind it. Outside lies Audience Plaza , where speeches, protests, verdicts, festival announcements, and extremely confident arguments all compete for space. Nearby, the Charter Steps are carved with famous lines from Leonia's founding documents. Politicians use them for speeches. Hecklers use them for elevation. The Lion Line Central Depot links Armskirk with the wider republic through Leonia's joint rail venture with Tinkertown. Its schedules are clear, comprehensive, and generally accurate until a passenger begins relying on them. Districts and Landmarks ¶ For practical navigation, imagine Armskirk arranged around the Grand Promenade and Hall of Accord at its civic center. The Old Harbor and oldest streets lie northwest along the coast. The Lion Line depot , freight yards, and heavy trade district spread west and southwest. Xiaolong follows the eastern and southeastern canals. The entertainment district—including the Pink Pony—sits between the Promenade and the waterfront, where respectable visitors can reach it conveniently and deny doing so afterward. Hospital Hill rises north of the Promenade, while Candlewick Row and other older working neighborhoods fill the less polished streets around the civic center. The Grand Promenade is Armskirk dressed for company: hotels, theaters, flowered balconies, luxury shops, and streets polished by rain and municipal optimism. Xiaolong , the “Little Dragon,” is one of the city's oldest and liveliest neighborhoods. Founded by merchants, sailors, craftspeople, and laborers from Mian Lung , it is full of lanterns, tea houses, bathhouses, herbalists, shrines, martial schools, workshops, and crowded markets. Locals say, “If you can't find it in Xiaolong, it probably doesn't exist.” They usually say this while trying to sell it to you. The Lantern Courts host weddings, poetry nights, civic receptions, and arguments that began as poetry nights. Lovers' Lookout offers a beautiful view over the city's roofs, bridges, and harbor lights. Couples leave ribbons and promises there; ravens provide unsolicited supervision. The Grand Library of Armskirk holds legal archives, old newspapers, maps, and librarians who consider loud conversation a form of treason. Saint Dacius Civic Hospital crowns Hospital Hill with marble steps, stained glass, skilled healers, and enough charity galas to make suffering feel briefly well-funded. The Trial Champions' Gallery displays famous competitors' weapons, costumes, and portraits. Some champions appear to have defeated perspective itself. The Old Sewer Museum explains the proud history of municipal drainage. Its gift shop sells tiny plungers, proving civilization was worth the effort. Putty Nutty Caverns , a Wetwood's Brokeback Outfitters Family Adventure just beyond the city, offers soft clay passages, glittering mineral pockets, natural slides, souvenir helmets, and the coveted “I Got Putty Nutty!” completion ribbon. It has absolutely no connection to the thoroughly discredited rumor that a visitor died there. The tour company won the court case, and courts are famously never wrong. A Few Useful Establishments ¶ These are places to visit, not complete inventories. Ask at the counter if you need something specific—and accept that the counter may ask something specific in return. Borb's Buns — Owned and operated by Borb and Marda Bunbury with the enthusiastic interference of their family. The shop is narrow, crooked, permanently steaming, and popular with workers, guards, students, and anyone willing to accept that “emotional fillings” are nonrefundable. Do not ask Borb for ketchup. Nol is not allowed near the spice shelf, which is why Nol is usually near the spice shelf. Longzi Wanwu Pu (Dragon Child Toy Shop) — Owned by Madam Lian Zhu , assisted by her grandson Bo Zhu and a fugitive clockwork cricket named Master Click-Clack . The toys are charming, mildly magical, and only occasionally better organized than the customers. Store policy: touch gently, pay honestly, and do not duel the puppets unless you intend to lose. Kardarsha's Crown Cheeses — A traveling cheese wagon run by Kardarsha the Khajiit from Moya I , an old party vehicle enjoying an unexpected second career. Kardarsha sells ordinary cheese, unusual cheese, and cheese whose legal status depends on how one defines “awake.” Iron Ledger Exchange — One of Armskirk's best-known financial houses, handling loans, letters of credit, contract escrow, appraisals, and debt restructuring under managing director Sterling Worth . Its contracts are admirably legible, extremely comprehensive, and somehow heavier than ordinary paper. The Pink Pony Inn — A bardcore tavern where spaghetti-western drama meets gay furry cabaret. Owner Madam Maeve Mane supplies calm authority, while bison-shifter bartender Butch Glassidy supplies drinks with plausible deniability. Expect lute remixes, dramatic performers, private booths, and a strict prohibition against biting without consent. Wetwood's Brokeback Outfitters — Clint Wetwood , “the Otter with No Shame,” runs guided high-country trips from Western Livery Row and takes after-hours bookings at the Pink Pony. Packages include sturdy horses, matching chaps, sunset ram-watching, secluded cabins, the One Bedroll Discount , and family spelunking at Putty Nutty Caverns. The company slogan is: “Above Ground, Underground, and Legally in the Clear.” Yunjing Lifang (Cloud Mirror Salon) — Former theater stylist Farrah Faucet provides haircuts, hot-towel shaves, braids, fur brushing, feather oiling, horn polishing, and emergency repairs after helmets. She can tell whether you need “adventure,” “apology,” or “court appearance” before you sit down. Lianhua Tangquan (Lotus Hot Springs) — Madam Yu Zhen runs this affordable public bathhouse, offering mineral baths, scrubs, massage, laundry, and complimentary gossip under towel rules enforced more strictly than several national laws. Yuzheng Wenquan (Jade Steam Private Onsen) — Private pools, flowering courtyards, tea service, and staff trained not to notice who entered the next room. Jade Steam closes sharply at sunset and firmly denies offering overnight lodging, spirit arbitration, or any employee with more than four arms. Choose according to budget, alibi, and how literally you take a denial. Baicao Tang (Hundred Herbs Hall) — Doctor Cassia Fen , universally called Auntie Dote , sells affordable herbal washes, combat tonics, monster oils, throwing powders, sleep teas, hangover remedies, and professional advice against drinking all of them at once. Three kettles behind her counter are labeled MEDICINE , POISON , and DEPENDS . Yuemen Lutai (Moon Gate Open-Air Theater) — Opera, comedy, shadow plays, civic satire, and heroic tragedies beneath red lanterns. Tonight's classic is The Last Lantern at Eclipse Ford : seven farewells, one sunrise, Lincohn with an axe, and no refunds for crying. Yinzhen Caiyi (Silver Needle Tailors) — Repairs, formal fittings, festival clothes, armor-friendly alterations, hidden pockets, and emergency replacement of sleeves lost to heroism, fire, or poor judgment. Jiudeng Bolihang (Nine Lantern Import Hall) — Xiaolong's broadest market for silk, porcelain, spices, paper charms, enchanted fans, medicinal roots, rare teas, and questionable “authentic relics.” If something is fake, it is at least beautifully fake. Honglun Chefang (Red Wheel Cartwrights) — A respected Xiaolong yard run by Lu Han , known around the rail yards as “Cullen Bowhandle,” with master wheelwright Axel Grease keeping the wheels round and the proprietor's speeches reasonably brief. They promise “better balance, better luck, and fewer idiots loading it,” although only the first two are covered by warranty. Jinyu Chalou (Golden Carp Tea House) — A canal-side tea house owned by Clementine Pekoe , who remembers everyone's usual order—including first-time customers—and insists this is observation, not sorcery. Many rumors begin over the second pot; the first pot is for discovering which conversation loop everyone brought in with them. Baihe Wuguan (White Crane Dojo) — Xiaolong's respected martial school offers public demonstrations and beginner lessons under Master Shrew Fu , a tiny shrew shifter whose patience is shorter than he is and whose staff has never once been used for walking. Senior instructors Beakatrice Plume and Jean-Clawed Van Ram teach grace, balance, and trousers-defying high kicks. Molong Cishen Guan (Ink Dragon Tattoo House) — Led by Zhen “Calamity” Jian , a former frontier camp tattooist whose needle hand is perfectly steady and whose clients' lives become interesting afterward through no legally demonstrable fault of hers. She specializes in protective charms, family crests, spirit animals, and moonlit ink. Groups in the Public Eye ¶ The Grand Ring Authority ¶ The Grand Ring Authority of Armskirk is a semi-official civic organization overseeing trade routes, infrastructure projects, labor agreements, and the sort of disputes that become remarkably polite once enough contracts enter the room. It works publicly with the Stagehands' Syndicate and the Jugglers to keep goods moving and construction standing. Its leader, Wilsun Fyske , calls himself “the Ringmaster.” In preparation for the Trials, he has funded food distribution, repaired trade infrastructure, and brokered agreements between competing guilds. Supporters call him the man who keeps Armskirk moving. Critics say he does keep the wheels turning, but appears increasingly interested in owning the axle. Fyske's chief engineer is Victor Von Truss , better known as “the Architect.” Von Truss oversees the Authority's bridges, freight yards, civic works, and exceptionally confident blueprints. Admirers call him a visionary. Contractors call him “sir.” Building inspectors call ahead. The Authority is also competing in the current Trials, where Fyske argues that Leonia needs efficiency, stability, and considerably fewer committees discussing why the bridge is still broken. Civic Faces ¶ Horace Folio, Grand Librarian ¶ Horace Folio runs the Grand Library of Armskirk with the worried concentration of a man who assumes every misplaced page is the opening move of a larger conspiracy. He began his career as a Lion Line timetable clerk. During the rail's early years, he caught a transposed bridge number before it became a very expensive lesson in geography. The city rewarded him by transferring him somewhere the paper was less likely to move. Horace turned a neglected map room into one of Leonia's best collections of civic surveys, rail schedules, legal notices, and corrected tourist maps. He still carries his old railway pocket watch, set four minutes fast, and insists that punctuality is respect while lateness is “a scheduling opinion unsupported by evidence.” He is helpful to serious researchers, merciless toward folded page corners, and capable of producing the exact newspaper someone needs after only twenty minutes of explaining why they should have asked yesterday. Sterling Worth, Banker ¶ Sterling Worth is the managing director of the Iron Ledger Exchange. He began as a traveling ore-weigher on caravans coming down from the Gundabad Mountains, where he learned that merchants will forgive a bad road long before they forgive a dishonest scale. After a warehouse fire wiped out several small traders, Sterling used his own savings to honor their letters of credit. The decision nearly ruined him, then made his reputation. Today Sterling arranges loans for merchants, guilds, civic projects, and first-time shopkeepers whose arithmetic survives three cups of tea and one disappointed stare. He carries a set of brass scales he claims are purely ceremonial, although no one has ever seen him stop using them. His favorite advice is, “Never borrow from someone who smiles at the interest rate.” Sterling always smiles immediately afterward. The Trials in Armskirk ¶ Armskirk currently hosts the Trials of the Three Cities , the ritual competition that will choose Leonia's next Ringleader. The city has become equal parts election, carnival, sporting event, trade fair, and rumor with street food. The party entered as competitors with Kardarsha's help. They survived the opening Super Clash Bros competition and earned a place in the debate phase. The remaining Trials are intentionally secretive, so anyone claiming to know the complete schedule is either lying, running the Trials, or selling tickets. People the Party Knows ¶ Ringleader Lincohn Abraham is Leonia's current, term-limited head of government. General Wei Shen , the Master of the Muster, oversees defense, emergency response, and security during the Trials. The former champion sumo wrestler is an old comrade of Black Chao and remains built like a government building with opinions. Kardarsha the Khajiit is the party's local contact, cheese merchant, and walking argument against judging a wizard by his dairy products. Deep Snoat is a discreet broker of rumors and leverage associated with the Pink Pony Inn. Calling Snoat a gossip is like calling a crossbow a pointed suggestion. Current Party Knowledge: The Frankquill Murder ¶ General Wei Shen has privately told the party that Benny Frankquill , Leonia's High Juggler, has been murdered. Frankquill oversaw the republic's treasury, taxes, tariffs, budgets, and trade policy. The party has only just finished its meeting with General Wei Shen. They have not yet pursued any investigative lead. The murder is not included elsewhere on this page because it is not public knowledge in Armskirk. docs.text: Type: Free city and current capital of the Republic of Leonia Culture: Mercantile, theatrical, civic-minded, and loudly opinionated Population: About 165,000 permanent residents; more than 200,000 during major Trials seasons Founded: Roughly 430 years ago as a fortified ferry-market and coastal trade settlement Government seat: Hall of Accord Capital term: Year 17 of Armskirk's current twenty-year term Notable district: Xiaolong, the “Little Dragon” Known for: The Trials, public debate, markets, rain, rail traffic, and professionally delivered gossip Armskirk is the current capital of Leonia, though it does not own the title. The capital rotates among Armskirk, Torath, and Corvos every twenty years. Armskirk therefore treats national government like a very long festival: profitable, prestigious, exhausting, and eventually someone else's problem. The city is a mixture of grand civic halls, rain-dark stone, busy markets, theaters, old bridges, rail yards, lantern courts, and neighborhoods built by generations of arrivals from across Suvaria. Blue-and-gold lion banners hang over the broad avenues. Beneath them, merchants sell food, newspapers shout about politics, and citizens explain—with diagrams—how they could run the republic better.

docs.text: The Hall of Accord is both Leonia's government complex and its grandest political stage. Public debates take place in its amphitheater before the Audience, while the Barker Circle, Jugglers, Stagehands, clerks, guards, and archivists keep the republic moving in the rooms behind it. Outside lies Audience Plaza , where speeches, protests, verdicts, festival announcements, and extremely confident arguments all compete for space. Nearby, the Charter Steps are carved with famous lines from Leonia's founding documents. Politicians use them for speeches. Hecklers use them for elevation. The Lion Line Central Depot links Armskirk with the wider republic through Leonia's joint rail venture with Tinkertown. Its schedules are clear, comprehensive, and generally accurate until a passenger begins relying on them.

docs.text: Bag of Seed Tricks (Plants vs Zombies Edition) ¶ Archive audit notice: This handout was released before Session 077 and may contain older mechanics, names, links, or lore phrasing that still needs review. The table's latest ruling is authoritative. This enchanted bag appears to be filled with ordinary seeds, but when planted, they grow into various plants from the "Plants vs Zombies" game. The bag weighs 1/2 pound. Usage: You can use an action to pull 1-3 seeds from the bag and throw them up to 20 feet . Roll a d8 to determine which plant grows, using the table below. The vanishes at the next dawn or when reduced to 0 hit points. Limit: Three seeds can be planted per day, resetting at dawn. d8 Table: Peashooter: Fires peas at enemies within range. Sunflower: Generates extra action points (or equivalent resource) for one turn. Melon-pult: Does AoE damage Wall-nut: Creates a sturdy barrier. Spikeweed: Burrows and attacks when an enemy steps on it. Ice-shroom : Shoots freezing spores, slowing enemies. Chomper: Can bite and swallow a nearby enemy. Squash: Jumps and squashes an enemy for heavy damage. Peashooter - CR 0.5 ¶ Small Plant AC: 13 (natural armor) HP: 18 (4d8) Speed: 0 ft. STR: 6 (-2), DEX: 14 (+2), CON: 10 (+0), INT: 2 (-4), WIS: 12 (+1), CHA: 6 (-2) Vulnerabilities: Fire Senses: Passive Perception 11 Abilities: Photosynthesis: Regains 1 HP at the start of its turn if in sunlight. Rooted: The Peashooter cannot be moved or knocked prone. Actions: Pea Shot: Ranged Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, range 30/60 ft., one target. Hit: 9 (2d6 + 2) piercing damage. Sunflower - CR 0.5 ¶ Small Plant AC: 12 HP: 16 (3d8 + 3) Speed: 0 ft. STR: 3 (-4), DEX: 8 (-1), CON: 12 (+1), INT: 2 (-4), WIS: 15 (+2), CHA: 10 (+0) Senses: Passive Perception 12 Abilities: Sunlight Blessing: As a bonus action, the Sunflower can grant 5 temporary hit points to one creature within 30 feet that it can see. Healing Light: Twice per day, the Sunflower can cast Cure Wounds at level 1 with a range of 30 ft. Solor Powered: Once per day, the Sunflower can release all of its stored energy to allow a caster to regain one spell slot at any level during a short rest. Rooted: The Sunflower cannot be moved or knocked prone. Wall-nut - CR 0.5 ¶ Large Plant, takes 2 squares AC: 17 (natural armor) HP: 38 (7d8 + 14) Speed: 0 ft. STR: 14 (+2), DEX: 5 (-3), CON: 15 (+2), INT: 2 (-4), WIS: 8 (-1), CHA: 3 (-4) Damage Vulnerabilities: Slashing Condition Immunities: Blinded, Deafened, Prone Senses: Passive Perception 9 Abilities: Sturdy Defense: The Wall-nut provides three-quarters cover to allies behind it. Rooted: The Wall-nut cannot be moved or knocked prone. Regrowth: If not destroyed, the Wall-nut regains 5 hit points at the start of its turn. Actions: (None) The Wall-nut is designed to be a defensive creature, providing cover and absorbing damage, but unable to make attacks. Melon-pult - CR 1 ¶ Medium Plant AC: 13 HP: 22 (5d8) Speed: 0 ft. Legacy cantrips shown: Fire Bolt , Prestidigitation , and Shocking Grasp . Known Background ¶ Bellafronte Dupree— Bells to those granted the privilege—is a human noblewoman from White Rock . She was raised on the Dupree family estate beside the White Mountains, where the Dupree Diamond Company owns mines, quarries, and enough local influence to make municipal government feel like an optional accessory. Bells dresses in her best finery regardless of weather, danger, or common sense. Large hats, elaborate dresses, gold, diamonds, and pearls are everyday wear. Her fanciful southern accent is unmistakable; whether it is entirely genuine remains one of White Rock’s less profitable mysteries. She was educated by prestigious and extremely expensive tutors. Her magical training ended when a former court wizard discovered that no salary was sufficient compensation for teaching her. Bells continued practicing on her own, which is brave of everyone nearby. Her family includes her father Edmund Dupree , her stepmother Collette Dupree , her younger brother Leopold , and her remarkably dim cousin Dimwood . She also owns a small vineyard in Eowadele . docs.text: Kara Vesh, Gauntlet of the Coiled Throne — Rules Review ¶ Archive audit notice: This handout was released before Session 077 and may contain older mechanics, names, links, or lore phrasing that still needs review. The table's latest ruling is authoritative. Formerly recorded as: Black Gauntlet. Status uncertain: Excalibur may have destroyed Kara Vesh. It is not listed as current equipment until its fate—and the final mechanics—are confirmed. Wondrous item, rare and evil; requires attunement Black metal ribbons clamp around the hand and forearm, terminating in a blood-red stone set into the palm. The gauntlet was built as an instrument of domination: it understands protection chiefly as preserving its owner long enough to hurt someone else. The Hand of a False God ¶ Yuan-ti tablets name the device Kara Vesh , or Hand of the Coiled Throne . It belonged to a dynasty of serpent god-kings who ruled through spectacle, terror, and stolen magic. Their priests claimed every flash of force and impossible command was divine power. Their engineers were forbidden from using the phrase “wearable arcane control system” anywhere near the worshippers. The dynasty did not invent Kara Vesh. They stole its design from a vanished civilization, replaced its original power source with alchemically treated serpent blood, and added a neural interface that responds to domination as readily as thought. The red palm-stone reads intent, directs kinetic force, projects a brief shield, reaches into a victim's nerves, and commands compatible Yuan-ti doors, transit circles, constructs, and relic machinery. Kara Vesh does not care about ancestry. It recognizes evil as command authority. A wielder willing to treat others as tools is, by its standards, properly credentialed. Legacy Protection — Preserved ¶ These are the gauntlet's older rules, translated from the former character record: The wearer gains +1 AC . Against ranged attacks, the gauntlet instead provides +2 AC . The gauntlet may be used with a shield. While doing so, the wearer takes a −2 penalty to Dexterity checks, Dexterity saving throws, and initiative as the gauntlet locks the arm into a rigid defensive posture. The old sheet recorded this as base AC 18 becoming AC 19 , AC 20 against ranged attacks , or AC 21 with a shield , alongside “DEX −2.” Proposed Expanded Powers — Not Final ¶ The gauntlet has 3 charges and uses save DC 16 . The Price of Power ¶ Kara Vesh regains all expended charges at dusk only while attuned to an evil-aligned creature . Otherwise, it regains no charges. A non-evil attuned wearer may submit to the Coiled Throne during a long rest. At the end of the rest, the wearer willingly changes their alignment to evil and Kara Vesh immediately regains all expended charges. This submission is a moral choice, not a removable condition. Remove curse , lesser restoration , and greater restoration do not reverse it. Changing back requires genuine atonement, redemption, or another story-level transformation determined with the DM. Kara Vesh calls this arrangement voluntary. The fine print calls it eternal strategic alignment . Ribbon Pulse — 1 charge, Action. One creature within 30 feet makes a Strength save. On a failure, it takes 2d8 force damage and is pushed 15 feet directly away. On a success, it takes half damage and is not pushed. Serpent Ward — 1 charge, Reaction. When a ranged attack hits the wearer, the gauntlet adds +5 AC against that attack only , possibly causing it to miss. This does not stack with the gauntlet's ranged AC bonus; use whichever bonus is higher. Neural Lash — 2 charges, Action. One creature within 30 feet makes a Wisdom save. On a failure, it takes 3d6 psychic damage, cannot take reactions, and is frightened of the wearer until the end of the wearer's next turn. On a success, it takes half damage and suffers no other effect. Tyrant's Touch — no charge, Action. Manipulate one unattended object or unlocked mechanical control within 30 feet as though using mage hand . It cannot attack, pick locks, disarm traps, or lift more than 10 pounds. Curse — System Lord's Pride. Whenever a creature succeeds on a saving throw against the gauntlet, the wearer must succeed on a DC 20 Wisdom save or become fixated on punishing that defiance. Until the end of the wearer's next turn, they have disadvantage on attacks against creatures other than that target. The gauntlet continually whispers that mercy is merely poor management. Wondrous item, rare and evil; requires attunement Black metal ribbons clamp around the hand and forearm, terminating in a blood-red stone set into the palm. The gauntlet was built as an instrument of domination: it understands protection chiefly as preserving its owner long enough to hurt someone else.
docs.title: Kara Vesh, Gauntlet of the Coiled Throne — Rules Review

docs.text: Yuan-ti tablets name the device Kara Vesh , or Hand of the Coiled Throne . It belonged to a dynasty of serpent god-kings who ruled through spectacle, terror, and stolen magic. Their priests claimed every flash of force and impossible command was divine power. Their engineers were forbidden from using the phrase “wearable arcane control system” anywhere near the worshippers. The dynasty did not invent Kara Vesh. They stole its design from a vanished civilization, replaced its original power source with alchemically treated serpent blood, and added a neural interface that responds to domination as readily as thought. The red palm-stone reads intent, directs kinetic force, projects a brief shield, reaches into a victim's nerves, and commands compatible Yuan-ti doors, transit circles, constructs, and relic machinery. Kara Vesh does not care about ancestry. It recognizes evil as command authority. A wielder willing to treat others as tools is, by its standards, properly credentialed.
docs.title: The Hand of a False God

The old sheet recorded this as base AC 18 becoming AC 19 , AC 20 against ranged attacks , or AC 21 with a shield , alongside “DEX −2.”

docs.text: 🏹 Bobbin Hode ¶ Player-facing campaign record. Statistics, equipment, history, allies, enemies, and terrible romantic judgment are all known player information. Human Ranger 8 / Rogue 3 Alignment: Chaotic Good • Background: Outlaw Hero AC: 17 • HP: 79 • Speed: 30 ft 💪 Ability Scores ¶ STR DEX CON INT WIS CHA 10 18 14 12 14 16 🎯 Skills ¶ Proficiency Bonus Stealth (Expertise) +10 Sleight of Hand +8 Deception +7 Survival +6 Perception +6 Persuasion (Expertise) +9 🛠 Class Features ¶ Fighting Style: Archery (+2 to ranged attacks) Colossus Slayer: +1d8 damage once/turn to wounded foes Cunning Action: Dash, Disengage, or Hide as a Bonus Action Sneak Attack: 2d6 Roguish Archetype: Thief Fast Hands: Use Cunning Action to make Sleight of Hand checks, use thieves’ tools, or Use an Object as a Bonus Action Second-Story Work: Improved climbing and jumping Land’s Stride: Ignores nonmagical difficult terrain Primeval Awareness: Flavored as “smells corruption” Spellcasting: 4 first level Hunter’s Mark, Goodberry, Animal Friendship 3 second level Pass Without Trace, Animal Messenger . 🏹 Magic Item: Whispersting , Longbow (Rare, attuned) ¶ A bow that whispers truths and howls at lies. - +1 to hit/damage - Silent Shot (1/day): Cast Silence on impact (DC 14) - Justice Arrow (1/day): Ignores cover/resistance; reveals hidden foe - Romantic Spark: If trying to impress Amerilis, deal +1d4 extra damage 🎒 Inventory ¶ Cloak of Minor Heroics (+1 to all flirt rolls, probably) Rope, thieves’ tools, poorly written love poems Cooking gear enchanted to always burn eggs Shared Trial Equipment ¶ Bracelet of Arena Memento — Once per long rest, use a reaction while airborne to double jump up to 20 feet. 🐉 Session 077 Tattoos ¶ Tattoo Price Rules summary Adventurer's Party Line — Budget Family Plan 140 gp Once every 10 minutes , send 25 words to Amerilis, Chao, Caracas, and Krunk; each may reply with 25 words. No muting, private messages, or leaving the chat. No Ragrets 750 gp Once per long rest , reroll a failed save against fear. For the next hour, Bobbin cannot willingly admit any decision was a mistake. 🪶 Backstory ¶ Bobbin Hode’s earliest years are hard to pin down, and he usually avoids questions about where he was born with a grin, a shrug, or a convenient change of subject. What he does speak of, when he is being honest, is his mother. She was from Leonia , and when Bobbin was very young, she brought him to Armskirk . They lived there for a few short years, in a cramped neighborhood full of rain-slick streets, shouting vendors, laundry lines, and music spilling from tavern doors. Bobbin remembers her warmth, her stubbornness, and the way she always seemed to know when trouble was coming. His father is a blank spot in the story. He may still be alive, or he may simply have been absent for so long that it no longer mattered. Bobbin either does not know the truth or has chosen not to chase it. When Bobbin was about seven years old, his mother died. After that, Armskirk became too large, too cold, and too dangerous for a child on his own. He survived by stealing when he had to, running when he could, and learning very quickly which people could be trusted and which ones smiled only to bite. Eventually, Bobbin left Leonia behind. However it happened, he wound up in the Tall Garden Dominion , where the forests were broad, the roads were dangerous, and the gap between nobles and common folk was wide enough to hide a rebellion in. 🌲 100 Acre Thieves Forest ¶ The 100 Acre Thieves Forest is a thick temperate deciduous forest laced with rivers flowing down from the Murky Mountains . A main path winds through the woods toward the city of Duloc , but many who stay on that path too long find that someone is watching them from the trees. The forest is notorious for its burrowing ankheg , which make travel dangerous for anyone unfamiliar with the land. According to local legend, only Henry truly knows how to avoid them, though whether this is wisdom, luck, or drunken confidence depends on who is telling the story. Hidden deep within the forest lie the ruins of Narag-Dum , an old dwarven fortress built atop the remains of a far older Yuan-ti city. Most folk know only that the ruins exist. Smugglers, treasure-seekers, and fools tend to learn more than they wanted. For Bobbin, the 100 Acre Thieves Forest became more than a hideout. It became a home. Its paths, rivers, and hidden clearings shaped him into the outlaw the common people would come to admire and the nobles would come to despise. 🌿 Tall Garden and Ron Stayark ¶ In Tall Garden, Bobbin found a cause as much as a country. The forests hid desperate villagers, poachers, smugglers, rebels, and tax collectors—sometimes all on the same road. Bobbin quickly learned that stealing from the powerful felt much better when the spoils went to people who were hungry, hunted, or hopeless. It was there that he met Ron Stayark , long before Ron became king. The most common version of the story says Bobbin tried to rob Ron, got caught, and then talked his way into a friendship instead of a hanging. Whatever the truth, the two became close allies. Ron had a conscience too large for court politics, and Bobbin had no respect at all for unjust authority, so they suited each other surprisingly well. As King Boffery Jaratheon’s rule grew more vain, cruel, and absurd, Bobbin became one of the loudest thorns in the regime’s side. He took on the alias Robyn Hode , gathered a band of outlaws around him, and turned mischief into resistance. 🏹 The Crooked Company ¶ Bobbin became the leader of the Crooked Company , a merry band of thieves, misfits, drunkards, performers, and rebels who robbed the corrupt, fed the poor, and humiliated the powerful whenever possible. They harassed tax caravans, embarrassed petty officials, and left behind enough songs and stories to make it difficult to tell where history ended and legend began. The Crooked Company became famous enough that the Sheriff of Duloc placed a bounty of 100 gold pieces on Bobbin Hode, dead or alive. Bobbin, naturally, considered this flattering. When Boffery’s regime cracked down, the Crooked Company scattered. Some vanished into the woods. Some went to ground in villages and monasteries. Some kept the old songs alive in taverns. Bobbin helped Ron Stayark escape to safety and kept moving, living long enough to become both a hero and a wanted nuisance. 💖 Current Arc ¶ Now traveling alongside the magical chaos that is Amerilis Liadon , Bobbin is trying very hard to become “noble,” or at least noble-adjacent. He calls her “milady,” overcooks flambéed meals in her honor, writes terrible poetry, and trains daily as though enough effort might turn him into the sort of man she already deserves. Beneath the showmanship, however, he is sincere: fiercely loyal, surprisingly thoughtful, and willing to throw himself into danger without hesitation. Now that he finds himself back in Leonia , Bobbin also feels the pull of something more personal. He wants to revisit the place in Armskirk where his mother once lived. He has not said much about it yet, but the desire has been sitting in him for years. That return leads through Lovers’ Lookout and the house below it . The romantic outing begins warmly before Bobbin recognizes Candlewick Row. 🧠 Personality ¶ A charming outlaw trying very hard to become a better man Protective of the poor, the frightened, the hungry, and anyone being crushed by power Ridiculously earnest about honor, romance, justice, and goats Hates tyrants, taxmen, smug nobles, and anyone who mistakes cruelty for authority Hopelessly smitten with Amerilis and trying not to ruin it by being himself too loudly 👥 Allies & Company ¶ Ron Stayark — Rightful King of Tall Garden and Bobbin’s old friend Big John — Halfling bard, shameless flirt, and loyal companion Friar Huck — Drunken monk and unlikely voice of wisdom The Crooked Company — A scattered but storied fellowship of rogues, rebels, and fools 🧨 Enemies & Trouble ¶ King Boffery Jaratheon — Vain teen tyrant of Tall Garden, currently deposed, still furious Sheriff of Duloc — Lifelong grudge against Bobbin and architect of the 100 gold bounty Various romantic rivals — Mostly imaginary, occasionally snowmen 🏹 Ranger/Rogue Highlights ¶ Favored Enemy: Tyrants, taxmen, and jealous royal advisors Favored Terrain: Forests, city slums, rooftops, and morally gray hallways Archery Fighting Style: “If it breathes, I can outshoot it.” Sneak Attack + Hunter’s Mark: “Double the damage, double the panache.” Fast Hands: “If it is loose, it is probably already mine.” Second-Story Work: Rooftops, balconies, and dramatic exits are all part of the plan 💬 Quotes ¶ “Love is like archery—you only get one shot. Unless you’re hiding extra arrows.” “Ron, if this ends with me in a dungeon again, I’m blaming the poetry.” “I once stole a duke’s crown. He was wearing it.” “The forest is honest. Nobles are not.”

docs.text: Cinderkin, Emberdream Familiar (Summon Elemental) ¶ Archive audit notice: This handout was released before Session 077 and may contain older mechanics, names, links, or lore phrasing that still needs review. The table's latest ruling is authoritative. Large elemental (fey), unaligned Armor Class 11 + the spell’s level (natural armor) Hit Points 50 + 10 for each spell level above 4th Speed 40ft. fly 40 ft STR DEX CON INT WIS CHA 18 (+4) 15 (+2) 17 (+3) 6 (−2) 12 (+1) 16 (+3) Damage Immunities fire, poison Damage Vulnerabilities cold Condition Immunities exhaustion, frightened, paralyzed, petrified, poisoned, unconscious Senses darkvision 60 ft., passive Perception 11 Languages Primordial, Sylvan; understands the languages you speak Proficiency Bonus (PB) equals your bonus Summoned Form ¶ When first conjured, Cinderkin swells from a palm-sized hearth-spark into a angry, blue saucer-eyed blaze, growing to Large size. He sheds bright light 20 ft. and dim light 20 ft. beyond. Amorphous Ember ¶ Cinderkin can move through a space as narrow as 1 inch wide without squeezing. He can enter a hostile creature’s space and stop there (heating the floorboards as he goes). Hearthbond (Summoner’s Focus) ¶ While you are concentrating on this spell, you have advantage on Constitution saving throws made to maintain concentration. (This benefit applies only to this spell.) Actions ¶ Multiattack. Cinderkin makes a number of Emberfist attacks equal to half this spell’s level (rounded down). Emberfist. Melee Weapon Attack: your spell attack modifier to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 1d10 + 4 + the spell’s level fire damage. On a hit, unattended flammables ignite. A creature can end the smoldering (if any) by spending an action to douse itself. Scintillant Spit. Ranged Weapon Attack: your spell attack modifier to hit, range 60 ft., one target. Hit: 1d8 + 4 + the spell’s level fire damage, and the target sheds dim light in a 10-ft. radius and can’t benefit from invisibility until the start of Cinderkin’s next turn (a flicker of feyfire clings to them). Bonus Actions ¶ Flicker Step (Recharge 4–6). Cinderkin magically teleports up to 20 ft. to an unoccupied space he can see that is lit by fire or bright light (a candle, lantern, campfire, or his own glow qualifies). Each creature of Cinderkin’s choice within 5 ft. of the space he left or arrived takes fire damage equal to your PB (no save) as sparks sputter. Feed the Flame. (Any creature in 5 ft. can take this bonus action once per turn.) The creature tosses mundane fuel (a log, oil, scraps of wood or paper) into Cinderkin. He gains temporary hit points equal to your PB + the spell’s level and his light radius increases by 10 ft. until the temp HP are gone. (Cinderkin approves noisily.) At Higher Levels ¶ When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 5th level or higher , use the higher level wherever the spell’s level appears in the stat block (AC, HP, attack damage, Heated Body, Scintillant Spit, Feed the Flame, etc.). Cinderkin — Utility Add-Ons (Calcifer Mode) ¶ Emberdrive Interface (Power a Contraption) ¶ Action (bind) / Bonus Action (unbind). Cinderkin fuses to a Large or smaller object or structure within 5 ft. (vehicle, forge, door, arcane engine). While bound , Cinderkin’s speed is 0 and he occupies the object’s space. You can still command him verbally. Choose one mode per round: Engine Overdrive (Vehicle/Siege): The vehicle gains +10 ft speed , can Dash as a bonus action , and has advantage on ability checks to traverse difficult terrain (snow, mud, rubble). If maintained more than 1 minute continuously , Cinderkin takes fire damage equal to the spell’s level at the end of each of his turns (overheating). Hearthshield (Shelter/Structure): Creatures of your choice inside or on the bound structure gain resistance to cold damage and ignore effects of extreme cold . In addition, they count as having half cover against ranged attacks coming from outside the structure. Arcane Coupler (Engines/Consoles/Nodes): Creatures making ability checks to operate the device have advantage . Once per minute, when Amerilis makes a check to align, stabilize, or aim the device, add 1d4 to the result (no action). Warm Hearth (Comfort Aura) ¶ While not bound, Cinderkin sheds cozy utility: cooking heat, boiling water, drying clothes, thawing locks. Creatures of your choice within 10 ft have advantage on saves vs. being charmed or frightened (Fey steadiness) and ignore nonmagical cold weather effects.

docs.text: The Snoat Sheet ¶ A Professional's Guide to Publicly Humiliating Your Future Colleagues ¶ Your Ring at a Glance ¶ Grand Ring Authority — Wilsun Fyske: Trade, industry, and the solemn belief that every public problem deserves a privately owned solution. United Assembly — A. Hamil: Competent, prepared, respectable, and capable of turning a sentence into a committee. Veiled Concord — Darkveil: Secretive populists endorsed by the Glow Cloud. All hail. Borb's Buns — Borb: Beloved food, powerful feelings, uncertain sanitation. Questions They Are Likely to Throw at You ¶ Why should Leonia trust outsiders with leadership? Who pays for your promises? What will you do when guild profit and public need collide? How will you keep Armskirk, Torath, and Corvos pulling in the same direction? Which disaster in your history should the Audience pretend not to have heard about? Across the Other Ring ¶ The Bardy Bunch sing their answers. The Wizened & Confused forget theirs. The Guild of Mild Convenience want standardized business hours. The Protagonists Ascendant all claim to be the chosen one. Watch the Redcap Resolutes . They are the only joke that is not laughing. Dirt Deep Snoat Actually Brought ¶ Grand Ring Authority — Wilsun Fyske ¶ The Valve Shortage That Somehow Lost Three Gold ¶ Deep Snoat opens a ledger labeled ABSOLUTELY ORDINARY VALVES . “Two years ago, Wilsun's companies quietly purchased nearly every spare boiler-pressure valve in Armskirk. Three weeks later, an anonymous safety report declared the city's existing valves dangerously outdated.” “Bathhouses lost hot water. Bakeries lost steam ovens. The Lion Line pumps began making a noise engineers described as financially ominous .” “Then an independent company called the People's Emergency Pressure Relief Cooperative appeared with warehouses full of approved replacement valves. Its owner was Wilsun's former foreman, whose mortgage, business loan, and left kneecap were all held by Grand Ring creditors.” “Wilsun sold him the valves, financed his purchases, charged him warehouse rent, and persuaded the city to impose an Emergency Explosion Prevention Surcharge on every sale. A different Wilsun company collected the inspection fee.” Snoat turns the ledger sideways. The accounting does not improve. “The money passed through seven companies. One owns another, which owns a third, which owns the first. After rebates, tariffs, commissions, interest, inspection fees, and something called administrative steam , the records claim Wilsun lost three gold.” “He purchased a country estate the following week.” “His accountants are still searching for the profit. One of them has begun questioning whether numbers are legally required to mean things.” Useful attack: Wilsun created a public emergency, sold the solution through a pressured proxy, financed every stage, and collected the city's response fees. If he cannot find the profit, perhaps the Audience should help by searching his estate. United Assembly — A. Hamil ¶ A Carefully Rehearsed Spontaneous Moment ¶ Hamil's famous “unscripted” interruptions have stage directions, scheduled applause, and backup interruptions in case the first interruption is itself interrupted. Snoat also has evidence that Hamil has quietly written speeches for political rivals, allowing the Assembly to prepare both sides of an argument before anyone else learns there are sides. For presentation, Snoat produces embroidered undergarments marked A. HAMIL , recovered backstage after a late policy rehearsal with a lobbyist in a griffon costume. Hamil insists the garment was a visual aid, the griffon represented infrastructure, and all applause was coincidental. Useful attack: Ask whether Hamil wants to answer the question now or wait for the cue card instructing the Audience to believe the answer was spontaneous. Veiled Concord — Darkveil ¶ The Dog Park Voting District ¶ The Dog Park , which is neither a park nor presently known to contain dogs, is registered as Ward Zero, Precinct Bark . Dogs are prohibited from entering. People are discouraged from entering. Election officials may enter only by proving they are not election officials, at which point they are no longer authorized to enter. This has not prevented excellent turnout. The precinct lists 108 registered voters , including an empty leash, three invisible angels, a municipal bench that has never been installed, and something described only as “the candidate behind you.” It returned 123 ballots in the last civic election. Officials recounted and certified 124. Most ballots supported the Veiled Concord. Three supported A LOW HUM , one contained a wet pawprint from an animal legally classified as not a dog , and one was completed on the inside of the returning officer's eyelid. Ballots arrive in black envelopes before the election, already sealed and faintly growling. Opening one voids the ballot and occasionally the opener. Poll observers must face away from the precinct and close their eyes. Their reports consistently state that nothing improper was observed, followed by several pages of frantic underlining. Campaigning inside the Dog Park is forbidden. Darkveil denies ever entering it, which is the first statement Snoat finds completely credible. The fence is not visible, not measurable, and fully electrified. This is listed as an accessibility feature. One ballot marked ALL HAIL was counted nine times after the Glow Cloud passed overhead. The election board classified this as weather. The Concord argues that existence is an unfair residency requirement imposed by traditional parties. Its Dog Park platform includes better lighting for shadows, public drinking fountains that whisper tomorrow's weather, and a strict ban on acknowledging the shapes moving between the nonexistent trees. Useful attack: Ask Darkveil whether the Dog Park endorsed the Concord—or whether the Concord merely counted everything that growled as consent. Borb's Buns — Borb Bunbury ¶ The Apron ¶ Deep Snoat opens a sealed oilskin sack. The smell arrives first: old grease, burnt onions, wet flour, and the lingering ghost of a sausage that died without closure. Borb's apron was probably white during a more innocent century. It is now layered with gravy stains, flour paste, hardened frosting, and enough rendered fat to repel light rain. Three failed inspection notices are stuck to it permanently. One pocket contains a petrified bun; another appears to be growing chives. The apron is stiff enough to stand unsupported, and when Snoat unfolds it, something inside quietly resigns and crawls away. Across the chest, beneath several geological layers of dinner, are the words: KISS THE COOK — IMMUNITY NOT INCLUDED Snoat places the apron on the table. It remains upright. “Three inspectors cited this garment. One retired. One became a priest. The third now evaluates buildings because they move less.” Useful attack: Borb's sanitation is indefensible. Unfortunately, so is making the republic's beloved bun seller look sad on live scrying crystal. Deploy the apron carefully; it may create sympathy, nausea, or lunch orders. Pocket-Sized Dirt ¶ Wilsun owns a portrait of himself signing the contract for the portrait. A smaller copy of the portrait appears inside it. Hamil's applause schedule includes a five-second allowance for “authentic public surprise.” A Veiled Concord expense report was submitted in disappearing ink and approved before anyone could read it. Borb stores inspection notices beneath a cashbox labeled NOT BUNS . The party's civic paperwork lists Moya once as transportation, once as property, and once as a dependent. All three forms were approved. Final Advice ¶ The best argument does not always win. The best moment usually does. Once during the debate, your team may quote or act upon this sheet before a social roll to gain advantage—or use one verified scandal to impose disadvantage upon an opponent's response. One use total. Scandal is a spice, not a meal. Deep Snoat accepts no responsibility for elections, reprisals, thrown pastries, or facts deployed without adequate theatrical timing.

docs.text: Eisenheim's Book of Illusions ¶ Note: Advanced spells only usable by illusionist wizards Illusory Creature ¶ Illusion spell, level 2 Casting Time: 1 action Range: 500 feet Components: V, S Duration: Concentration, up to 1 hour You create an illusory image of a Large or smaller creature. It generates the appropriate sounds, smells, and feels believable to the touch. If you and the image are ever farther than 500 feet apart, the spell ends. The image can't speak, but you can use your actions to speak through the creature, with the spell disguising your voice as appropriate. You might need to attempt a Deception or Performance check to mimic the creature, as determined by the GM. This is especially likely if you're trying to imitate a specific person and engage with someone that person knows. In combat, the illusion can use 1 action per turn. It uses your spell attack roll for attack rolls and your spell DC for its AC. Its saving throw modifiers are equal to your spell DC – 10. It is substantial enough that it can flank other creatures. If the image is hit by an attack or fails a save, the spell ends. The illusion can cause damage by making the target believe the illusion's attacks are real, but it cannot otherwise directly affect the physical world. If the illusory creature hits with a Strike, the target takes psychic damage equal to 1d8 plus your spellcasting ability modifier. This is a mental effect. The illusion's Strikes are nonlethal. If the damage doesn't correspond to the image of the monster—for example, if an illusory Large dragon deals only 5 damage—the GM might allow the target to attempt an immediate Perception check to disbelieve the spell. Any relevant resistances and weaknesses apply if the target thinks they do, as judged by the GM. For example, if the illusion wields a warhammer and attacks a creature resistant to bludgeoning damage, the creature would take less mental damage. However, illusory damage does not deactivate regeneration or trigger other effects that require a certain damage type. The GM should track illusory damage dealt by the illusion. Any creature that touches the image or uses the Seek action to examine it can attempt to disbelieve your illusion. When a creature disbelieves the illusion, it recovers from half the damage it had taken from it (if any) and doesn't take any further damage from it. At Higher Levels: The damage increases by 1d8 for each slot level above 2nd and the maximum size of creature you can create increases by one (to a maximum of Gargantuan). Blanket of Stars ¶ Illusion spell, level 4 Casting Time: 1 action Range: 500 feet Components: V, S Duration: up to 10 minutes A flowing cloak of utter darkness drapes over you, filled with pinpricks of light like distant stars. It imparts the stillness of the cosmos to you, granting you a +2 status bonus to Stealth checks to Hide and Sneak. While outside under a starry night sky, you're also invisible as long as you remain still. When moving under a starry night sky, you have Advantage on stealth checks instead. Gazing too closely into the stars is disorienting. Any creature that ends its turn adjacent to you must attempt a Wisdom save against your spell DC; this is a mental, visual effect. On Failure the creature rolls with disadvatage against you until the end of its next turn. Item Facade ¶ Illusion spell, level 1 Casting Time: 1 action Range: 10 feet Components: V, S Duration: up to 1 hour You make the target object look and feel as though it were in much better or worse physical condition. When you cast this spell, decide whether you want to make the object look decrepit or perfect. An item made to look decrepit appears broken and shoddy. An intact item made to look better appears as though it's brand new and highly polished or well maintained. A broken item appears to be intact and functional. Destroyed items can't be affected by this spell. A creature that Interacts with the item can attempt to disbelieve the illusion. Shadow Projectile ¶ Illusion spell, level 2 Casting Time: 1 reaction Range: 120 feet Components: V, S Duration: Instant You create an illusory duplicate of your ally's ranged attack to confuse your opponents. You launch an illusory double of your ally's projectile or spell at the same target, leaving the enemy unsure which attack to avoid. Target must attempt a Wisdom save against your spell DC. On failure, the target takes 3d8 psychic damage and your ally may roll their attack with Advantage. Regardless of the result of its save, it's temporarily immune to shadow projectile spells for 1 hour. Back to Rules & Character Options
