It uses your spell attack roll for attack rolls and your spell DC for its AC. Its saving throw modifiers are equal to your spell DC – 10. It is substantial enough that it can flank other creatures. If the image is hit by an attack or fails a save, the spell ends. The illusion can cause damage by making the target believe the illusion's attacks are real, but it cannot otherwise directly affect the physical world. If the illusory creature hits with a Strike, the target takes psychic damage equal to 1d8 plus your spellcasting ability modifier. This is a mental effect. The illusion's Strikes are nonlethal. If the damage doesn't correspond to the image of the monster—for example, if an illusory Large dragon deals only 5 damage—the GM might allow the target to attempt an immediate Perception check to disbelieve the spell. Any relevant resistances and weaknesses apply if the target thinks they do, as judged by the GM. For example, if the illusion wields a warhammer and attacks a creature resistant to bludgeoning damage, the creature would take less mental damage. However, illusory damage does not deactivate regeneration or trigger other effects that require a certain damage type. The GM should track illusory damage dealt by the illusion. Any creature that touches the image or uses the Seek action to examine it can attempt to disbelieve your illusion. When a creature disbelieves the illusion, it recovers from half the damage it had taken from it (if any) and doesn't take any further damage from it. At Higher Levels: The damage increases by 1d8 for each slot level above 2nd and the maximum size of creature you can create increases by one (to a maximum of Gargantuan).
docs.title: Illusory Creature

docs.text: Illusion spell, level 4 Casting Time: 1 action Range: 500 feet Components: V, S Duration: up to 10 minutes A flowing cloak of utter darkness drapes over you, filled with pinpricks of light like distant stars. It imparts the stillness of the cosmos to you, granting you a +2 status bonus to Stealth checks to Hide and Sneak. While outside under a starry night sky, you're also invisible as long as you remain still. When moving under a starry night sky, you have Advantage on stealth checks instead. Gazing too closely into the stars is disorienting. Any creature that ends its turn adjacent to you must attempt a Wisdom save against your spell DC; this is a mental, visual effect. On Failure the creature rolls with disadvatage against you until the end of its next turn.
docs.title: Blanket of Stars

docs.text: Illusion spell, level 1 Casting Time: 1 action Range: 10 feet Components: V, S Duration: up to 1 hour You make the target object look and feel as though it were in much better or worse physical condition. When you cast this spell, decide whether you want to make the object look decrepit or perfect. An item made to look decrepit appears broken and shoddy. An intact item made to look better appears as though it's brand new and highly polished or well maintained. A broken item appears to be intact and functional. Destroyed items can't be affected by this spell. A creature that Interacts with the item can attempt to disbelieve the illusion.
docs.title: Item Facade

docs.text: Illusion spell, level 2 Casting Time: 1 reaction Range: 120 feet Components: V, S Duration: Instant You create an illusory duplicate of your ally's ranged attack to confuse your opponents. You launch an illusory double of your ally's projectile or spell at the same target, leaving the enemy unsure which attack to avoid. Target must attempt a Wisdom save against your spell DC. On failure, the target takes 3d8 psychic damage and your ally may roll their attack with Advantage. Regardless of the result of its save, it's temporarily immune to shadow projectile spells for 1 hour. Back to Rules & Character Options

docs.text: Excalibur, the Promised Dawn ¶ Archive audit notice: This handout was released before Session 077 and may contain older mechanics, names, links, or lore phrasing that still needs review. The table's latest ruling is authoritative. Legendary (scaling), requires attunement by a good-aligned creature blessed by an Ancient Dragon How you got it: When a Ringwraith descended on Tinkertown, Saskia the Golden hurled this blade to Krunk as she took wing to battle her corrupted child above. After the fight she vowed to return “on the eve of the last battle”… and, yes, admitted she has the hots for you. Very Arthurian. Very epic. 📜 Description ¶ A lean, unadorned longsword of pale-gold steel that hums like a held breath before dawn. Its fuller glows with a tiny script—an Integrity % that flickers like starlight. When drawn, light folds around the edge like a sunrise caught in glass; when sheathed, the light settles into a quiet halo at the throat of the scabbard. The sword’s voice is bright and earnest, a knightly cheer in your head: “Stand tall, Sir Krunkulous. I am Excalibur, the Promised Dawn—forged in Avalon by six great fairies as a weapon for the world itself. Draw me when the many must be saved, and together we’ll cut the night and bring the morning.” 📊 Solo-Leveling-Style UI (seen only by Krunk) ¶ [WEAPON INDENTIFICATION] Name: EXCALIBUR — THE PROMISED DAWN Rank: Legendary (Scaling) Integrity: 67% Invisible Air: OFFLINE Attuned: YES (Krunk) Alignment Gate: PASS Enhancement: +2 (Level 10–14) Radiant Edge: READY Noble Phantasm: Promised Victory — READY (1/Long Rest) Companion Item: AVALON - THE EVERDISTANT UTOPIA [SYSTEM NOTICE] Wielder Added: Sir Krunkulous — AUTHORIZED Calibration: Power Output locked to Level 12 (60%) — Safety Limiters ENGAGED Quick Facts ¶ Type: +2 magic longsword; versatile ( 1d8 one-handed or 1d10 two-handed) Light: Sheds bright light 20 ft. / dim 20 ft. (unless muted by the scabbard) Languages while attuned: Celestial & Draconic Sentience: Lawful good; INT 8, WIS 14, CHA 16; telepathy with wielder (60 ft.) Personality : Noble knight, with some quirks. Enthusiastically pro-smite. Favorite title for you: “Sir Krunkulous the Unclonklable.” Self-Limiting Radiance: The blade throttles its own output to avoid killing a mortal bearer; higher unlocks gently loosen the limiters. Krunk's Current Attack — Level 12 ¶ Krunk has Strength +4 , proficiency +4 , and Excalibur's current +2 enhancement . Grip Attack roll Slashing damage One-handed +10 to hit 1d8 + 6 Two-handed +10 to hit 1d10 + 6 Once on each of Krunk's turns, a hit against a creature Excalibur deems evil deals another +4 radiant damage from Radiant Edge . This is separate from Krunk's Improved Divine Smite , which adds 1d8 radiant damage to every melee weapon hit. Excalibur's Spellcasting Enhancement ¶ Excalibur's spellcasting enhancement is active while its attuned bearer either wields the drawn sword or keeps at least one hand touching its hilt while it is sheathed , provided the bearer is not wielding another weapon . A shield does not count as another weapon. For Krunk, meeting this condition raises his spell save DC from 16 to 18 and his spell attack modifier from +8 to +10 . The bonuses end immediately if he releases the hilt, cannot reach the sword, or begins wielding a different weapon. Merely wearing or carrying Excalibur without touching its hilt is not enough. Scaling Enhancement ¶ The enhancement applies to Excalibur's attack and damage rolls. It also increases the wielder's spell save DC and spell attack modifier while Excalibur's spellcasting enhancement above is active. +1 to attack, damage, spell attacks, and spell save DCs Level 5–8 +2 to attack, damage, spell attacks, and spell save DCs Level 9–14 (you are here) +3 to attack, damage, spell attacks, and spell save DCs Level 15+ Core Features ¶ Radiant Edge ¶ Once on each of your turns when you hit with Excalibur, you may deal extra radiant damage equal to your proficiency bonus — but only to creatures that the sword deems evil. Once per turn, when you use any Smite , add +1d8 radiant damage. Oathbound Light ¶ If you commit a vile act (e.g., betray a sacred oath), Excalibur’s abilites are suppressed for an indefinite period and it becomes a regular longsword. Expect a lecture about abusing your powers. Anti-Theft Protocol ¶ If a non-authorized creature grasps the hilt: “UNAUTHORIZED WIELDER!” booms in Common/Draconic/Celestial within 300 ft. The sword counts as a mundane longsword for them and forces a DC 25 CON save or they take 2d6 radiant and drop it. Noble Phantasm — Promised Victory (Anti-Fortress Class) ¶ 1/long rest. As an Action , expend a 3rd-level spell slot or higher to fire a daybreak beam: a 120-ft-long line that is 5, 10, or 15 ft. wide (your choice when fired). Creatures in the line make a DEX save vs your spell DC . Fail: 5d10 radiant + 5d10 force + 2d10 per slot level above 3rd . Success: Half. Judgment of Dawn: The beam's path is treated as direct sunlight until the end of your next turn. A creature of evil alignment that fails the save is blinded and cannot regain hit points until the end of your next turn. Anti-Fortress: Non-artifact barriers, heavy fortifications, and magical darkness along the line are seared or suppressed at the DM’s discretion. Huge or larger creatures , living fortresses, creatures integrated into fortifications, and creatures with the Siege Monster trait have disadvantage on the Dexterity save against Promised Victory. Aftershock — Hero’s Fatigue: For 1 minute after firing: speed halved , disadvantage on attack rolls . A Lesser Restoration or Greater Restoration can end this early. Critical Glory (Unlocks at Level 15) ¶ On a critical hit against a fiend, undead, or shadow creature , add +2d8 radiant . The target must succeed on a CON save vs your spell DC or be blinded until the end of your next turn. Why You Probably Won’t Always Use Excalibur ¶ Beacon: Drawn blade = visible glow. You have disadvantage on Stealth checks and can’t benefit from being Invisible vs. creatures relying on sight. Divine Signature: Its holy aura can be sensed or scryed from afar by powerful foes. Selective Power: Radiant Edge only bites true evil. Knightly Temperament: Hates cheap shots and bullying; will loudly scold if you swing at weaklings or non-hostiles. Worthy Foe Bias: Prefers champions and monsters, not “cabbages.” Expect commentary. Attention Magnet: Open carry makes subtle plans harder; consider Muted Majesty or the Refraction Shroud when unlocked. Excalibur (stage whisper): “Sir Krunkulous… that goblin was already apologizing.” Avalon: The Everdistant Utopia (paired wondrous item) ¶ A rose-linen scabbard banded in summer-gold. Integrity % shows in the fuller when drawn (e.g., “Integrity 67% — Invisible Air: OFFLINE.” ). While worn and you are not wielding a shield , you gain +1 AC . Scabbard’s Mercy (1/short rest; automatic) ¶ If the creature holding the scabbard (including you) is still alive but below or would be reduced to below 0 hit points , that creature instead becomes stable at 0 hit points (unconscious; no death saves). You may give the scabbard to an ally—if they’re holding it, the effect can protect them instead. Muted Majesty (constant, togglable) ¶ Bonus Action while sheathed. Excalibur emits no light , reads as nonmagical to casual scans, and is hidden from most “detect item” divinations. If drawn while in this mode, then it is a regular longsword until the start of your next turn as it needs to power up from standby mode. Fairyward Pavilion (Unlocks at Level 13 ; 1/long rest) ¶ Casting Time: 1 minute Duration: 1 hour (no concentration) Range: 30 ft. (centered on Avalon) At your call, the world hushes and a secluded meadow blossoms into being: a 30-ft-radius sphere where warm sunlight streams from no visible sun and pink–violet blossoms drift in slow, weightless arcs. Petals skim the air like starlight fallen from the inner sea , and the distant outline of a lone tower seems to watch over the field’s edge. The scabbard must remain within 30 ft. of the center; if it leaves, the field ends. Bounded Field effects: Muffling Veil. Sound across the boundary is dulled; conversations inside can’t be clearly heard outside. One-Way Haze. From outside, the sphere appears as a sun-washed bower carpeted in flowers and gently drifting petals, heavily obscuring what lies within. From inside, you see out normally, with occasional visions of petal-showers and tiny fairy folk dancing at the periphery. Divination Dampers. Scrying sensors can’t appear inside, and creatures within can’t be targeted by divination . No Blinks, No Planes. Teleportation and planar travel can’t occur into or out of the field. Gentle Repulse. Hostile creatures with CR lower than your character level can’t willingly enter by nonmagical means. Hostile creatures of CR equal to or higher than your level must first succeed on a Charisma save against your spell save DC to enter. The field is difficult terrain for hostile creatures within it. Healing & solace within: Summer’s Mend. At the end of each of your turns , All living creatures in the field each regain 1d6 hit points. First Sip of Dawn. The first time a living creature enters the field during this casting , it recovers one 1st-level spell slot or removes one level of exhaustion . Sweet Balm of Avalon. All living creatures within the field have advantage on saves vs both magical and nonmagical ailments . Ongoing disease is suppressed while a creature remains in the field. Lore — Echo of the Garden: Once, Avalon sealed its chosen in a perfect sanctuary— a garden the world could not touch . That absolute defense has faded, but this gentler Pavilion lingers: sunlit petals, quiet air, and blessings that mend , like a memory of paradise glimpsed from the four corners of a weary battlefield.

They come from Fang Ro — Sheet ver7r11 ; the older Story ver7r3 is background material rather than a stat sheet. Variant Human Druid (Mógu Chóng Bài) 2 / Monk (Jiàn Shèng) 5 Alignment: Neutral Good • Background: Outlander AC: 17 • HP: 64 • Speed: 50 ft • Proficiency: +3 Spell save DC: 14 • Ki: 5 • Ki save DC: 14 💪 Ability Scores ¶ STR DEX CON INT WIS CHA 14 18 16 8 17 14 🎯 Skills ¶ Proficiency Legacy bonus Athletics +5 Intimidation +5 Nature +2 Perception +6 Survival +6 🛠 Legacy Class Features ¶ Wolf Hybrid Form: Fang's transformation from the Mógu curse. Wild Shape and Symbiotic Entity: Druidic transformations and fungal reinforcement. Halo of Spores: 1d4 damage on the legacy sheet. docs.text: 🛠 The Gadget Grotto 🛠 ¶ Archive audit notice: This handout was released before Session 077 and may contain older mechanics, names, links, or lore phrasing that still needs review. The table's latest ruling is authoritative. "Where ingenuity meets insanity!" Shop Description ¶ Deep beneath the cobbled streets and rusted pipelines of the city—hidden behind a series of mechanical locks—lies The Gadget Grotto : a subterranean emporium of invention and chaos. Part workshop, part black-market tech hub, and part mad scientist’s playground, it’s now courting investments from the E.A.R.S. ( Experimental Artifice & Research Syndicate ). This massive underground complex is lit by brass sconces, glowing blueprints, and crackling plasma coils. Cogs grind within the walls, and steampipes vent bursts of hissing vapor while mechanical arms scuttle overhead, adjusting precariously stacked shelves of half-finished contraptions, impossible blueprints, and clockwork creatures with questionable AI ethics . 🔐 Security Measures ¶ The JUDGE A sentient automaton guarding the entrance. Scans all visitors with its omniscient monocle eye. If someone fails its riddle-based authentication, they’re subjected to mildly humiliating punishments (e.g., gluing boots to the floor, floating for 5 minutes, or forced to speak in rhyme). Clockwork Swarm Sentinels Beetle-sized automatons patrolling shelves. Zap shoplifters with tiny electroshock pincers or inject mild sedatives for easy capture. Vault Access via DNA & Riddle Authentication A shifting metal puzzle box must be solved to open restricted schematics & weaponry. Anti-Duplication Field Prevents thieves from simply copying blueprints (except under incredibly convoluted circumstances). 🛒 Gadget Grotto Shop List ¶ 🔧 Prebuilt Gadgets (Ready to Use) ¶ Item Price Description Grappling Gear Gauntlet 60 gp A wrist-mounted grappling hook with steam-powered winch. Retracts with a hissing burst of pressure. ( Inspired by Attack on Titan & Inspector Gadget ). Spyglass Monocle 45 gp A collapsible monocle that zooms up to 5x and can shift to thermal vision. Occasionally plays classical music at inopportune moments. Clockwork Chameleon Cloak 120 gp A layered, gear-infused cloak that mimics its surroundings when still. Glitches if exposed to water. Tesla Knuckle Dusters 80 gp Brass knuckles that release a controlled lightning jolt when activated. Overuse may cause hair-raising side effects. Auto-Loader Bandolier 75 gp A magnetized ammo harness that reloads guns automatically. Occasionally spits bullets onto the floor. Multi-Tool Gauntlet 90 gp A leather gauntlet with tiny spring-loaded tools (lockpicks, screwdriver, flint striker, knife). Occasionally deploys the wrong tool at random. 📜 Schematics (Build Your Own) ¶ Item Price Description Schematic: "Bigger on the Inside" Cart 500 gp Turn a standard cart into an extraplanar, spacious laboratory. Each activation randomly expands into a new interior (library, forge, tea parlor, etc.). Schematic: Steam-Powered Wings 350 gp Attaches to a backpack, unfolding mechanical wings for short bursts of flight. Occasionally emits an annoying whistling noise. Schematic: The Muffler of Silence 200 gp A brass cone that creates a 30-ft zone of pure silence. Great for stealth, terrible for social interactions. Schematic: The Steam-Saw Staff 250 gp A clockwork-powered staff with a rotating sawblade on one end. Excellent for combat or overly aggressive woodworking. Schematic: The Smoke-Flinger Boots 180 gp Lets the user vanish in a puff of steam-smoke once per short rest. May also produce a whistling “kettle boil” noise. ⚠️ Experimental Tools (May Not Work as Intended) ¶ Item Price Description Omni-Spoon 10 gp Transforms into any utensil but randomly switches mid-bite, causing soup-salad-fork chaos. Tinker’s TNT Pen 50 gp Writes in explosive ink. Requires a command word to detonate selected text. Use with caution! Displacement Boots 125 gp Short-range teleportation (up to 15 ft.), but occasionally swaps you with a random nearby object. 🔥 Discount Gadgets (Slightly Defective) ¶ Item Price Description “Perfectly Normal” Hat 5 gp Looks completely normal—until someone comments on it. Then it bursts into flames for 6 seconds. Auto-Washing Gloves 10 gp Automatically clean your hands, but only during a handshake. Interdimensional Umbrella 15 gp Blocks rain but occasionally opens portals to unpredictable locations. Spring-Heeled Greaves 35 gp Add +5 ft. to your jump distance, yet sometimes launch you unexpectedly. 🧑‍🔬 Meet Picky Pauly ¶ “If it ain’t perfect, it ain’t good enough!” The caretaker and salesman of The Gadget Grotto . A small, wiry man with an ever-present look of scrutiny. Inspects every gadget like it personally offended him, and analyzes customers as though they’re malfunctioning devices. Picky Eater : “This soup is too symmetrical! It needs chaos!” Despite his exacting standards, he’s brilliant at modifying, upgrading, and repairing gadgets. If a player earns his respect (e.g., by fixing a flaw in one of his designs), he may offer them rare schematics or custom-built tools. 🔑 Special Deals & Services ¶ 🛠 Custom Modifications Pauly can enhance a gadget for an extra fee—but be ready for 20 minutes of him complaining first. 💰 Mystery Box Special (150 gp) A random gadget from the “restricted vault.” Could be incredible or utterly useless.

docs.text: Companions & Creatures ¶ Annie ¶ Small human, chaotic good Armor Class 11 Hit Points 15 (add 1d6 per level) Speed 20ft. STR DEX CON INT WIS CHA 7 (-2) 12 (+1) 10 (+0) 9 (-1) 8 (-1) 16 (+3) ___ - Condition Vulnerabilities fear - Skills Persuasion +1, Stealth +2 - Languages Common ___ Harmless. Annie does not provoke opportunity attacks for targets she hasn't attacked Annie are you OK? (Long Rest, Duration 5+lvl). This triggers if Mr. Snuggles drops below 5 Hit Points or she is persuaded by a PC. Annie gains temporary hit points equal to total and resistence to physical damage for the duration. Roll 1d6 each round: 1.Annie levitates 10 ft in the air for the duration 2.Roll on Wild Magic Surge Table, spells that target self target nearest ally instead 3.Annie duplicates the last spell that she saw casted, she chooses the target 4.Annie casts a first lvl spell of DMs choice 5.Annie casts Chaos Bolt on nearest enemy 6.For lvl rounds, Annie casts Call Lightning Actions ¶ Spellweaver(Recharge 6, Reaction). When 2 allies cast a spell during the same round that affects the same area it has a chance to create a side affect Amplify(Short Rest, Reaction). Annie touchs a nearby ally and increases the spell slot of a spell being cast Mr. Snuggles ¶ Large cutie, chaotic gossipy Armor Class 12 Hit Points 30(add 1d8 per level) Speed 40ft. STR DEX CON INT WIS CHA 15 (+2) 11 (0) 14 (+2) 6 (-3) 12 (+1) 9 (-1) ___ - Condition Immunities sleep, exhaustion - Senses passive Perception 14 - Languages Gibberish - Challenge 1 (200 XP) ___ Teddy Form. Unless Annie is being threatened, Mr. Snuggles remains in Teddy Bear Form. While in this form his AC is 10 and Hit Points is 5. False Appearance. After a long rest roll a d6, the effect lasts until your next long rest: 1. Nothing happens, you feel as if the curse is weakening. 2. You wake up to find you have stabbed yourself in your sleep somehow, 2d6 damage. 3. First time you are dealt damage in a combat encounter by a melee attack you must make a Wisdom Saving Throw(DC 14). On a fail, you spend your next action attempting to convince your attacker to hit you again and gain resistance to all physical damage. 4. You wake up with a back is covered in welts that toughen your skin. Decrease damage taken by 1d4 for the day. The welts make you vulnerable to Poison Damage. 5. You feel like you stepped on a nail but when you look nothing is there. Reduce movement speed by 10ft due to limp for the day. 6. You wake up and discover you have a painfully large hook body piecing on your head that sharpens your senses. Reduce max health by 1d10 and gain +2 to Consitution Saving Throws. docs.text: Legacy Magic Items ¶ Historical catalog: These are imported campaign records, not a guaranteed current inventory. A character name shows where the item was originally filed. Current player records and standalone item handouts are authoritative where linked. Current Player Records ¶ Bellafronte Dupree “Bells” Caracas Ella “Explosions” Emerald — legacy record Krunk Items Recorded Under Bells ¶ Open Bells’s current player record . Ring of Charm ¶ Wondrous item, uncommon 3 charges per day. You may cast Charm Person (DC 15), but you must shake the target’s hand with your ring hand. The target does not learn you tried to charm it on the first use, regardless of success or failure. Talking Skull ¶ Wondrous item, uncommon This skull has forgotten its name and seems to be constantly eyeing you. Once per day you can animate the skull, lighting up its eyes with a pale blue light. Roll a d6 and a d100. While animated, it speaks with you and will answer a question to the best of its ability if you correctly guess a riddle. Stasis Module Charm ¶ The current mechanics live in the canonical Bells — Stasis Module Charm handout. Elixir of Enhanced Eloquence ¶ Wondrous potion, rare (requires attunement) A potion that, when consumed, gives the drinker a silver tongue. It gives a permanent +1 to Charisma skill checks. It also allows the user to cast Comprehend Languages once per day without using a spell slot. Legacy text note: The original sentence ends after “not impacted…” without naming what does not affect the bonus. Use the benefits above as written unless the table establishes the missing limitation. Items Recorded Under Caracas ¶ Open Caracas’s current player record . Maul of Maelstroms ¶ Maul, uncommon (requires attunement) You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. The bonus damage is lightning damage. Once per long rest you can shout a battle cry and slam an enemy, dealing an extra 1d10 thunder damage. They must succeed on a DC 15 Strength saving throw or be knocked back 10 feet and prone. You feel a slight shock whenever you pick it up; the weapon seems to vibrate with energy. Gilly’s Bag of Beans ¶ Ownership note: The imported record lists “Caracas?”; confirm against the current sheet. Wondrous item, uncommon d8 Color Effect 1 Yellow Ipecac 2 Purple Eagle 3 Green Bear 4 Red Bull 5 Blue Cat 6 Grey Owl 7 Brown Fox 8 Black Unknown As a bonus action you may eat or give a bean. Most of these beans Enhance Ability , but several do other things. Make an Intelligence check (DC 12) to pick the correct bean. On a failure, roll a d8 and use that to select the color. The duration is 10 minutes. The party currently has 20 beans. Gilly warns only to eat one bean per person before taking a rest. Garland of Garlic ¶ Net, uncommon A magical garland of garlic laced with silver barbs. On a hit, it wraps around the vampire’s neck and prevents it from using its bite action. It cannot be removed or destroyed by a vampire regardless of shapechanging. It has the same properties as a Net , except it does not restrain. Bone Breaker ¶ Mace, uncommon (requires attunement) A large spiked mace that says “Bone Breaker, do not use!” hastily written across it. Base weapon: 1d6 bludgeoning, +1 piercing, +1 to hit, magical. Break Bones (Recharge 5–6): Melee attack. On a hit, the target must succeed on a Constitution save (DC 14) or have its AC reduced by 1 and speed reduced by 10 feet until healed. Hunger for Blood: At the start of combat the wielder must make a Wisdom save (DC 14). On a failure, you must Dash and Reckless Attack (Barbarian) an enemy within melee range of Bone Breaker. Bloodied Rage: While the wielder is bloodied in combat this weapon deals an extra 1d4 bludgeoning damage. At the start of their turn the wielder must make a Constitution save (DC 14) to avoid attacking the nearest creature (random if more than one is adjacent). Plasma Cutter of Limb Severance ¶ The current mechanics live in the canonical Caracas — Plasma Cutter of Limb Severance handout. Gloves of Archival Knowledge ¶ Wondrous item, rare (requires attunement) You have advantage on History checks to decipher an object’s origin. Once per long rest, the wearer can cast the Mending spell on a broken historical document or magical artifact (may require a DC check). Items Recorded Under Krunk ¶ Open Krunk’s current player record . Veil of Shadows ¶ Wondrous item, rare A large black amulet also known as the Shield of the Void. Once per day you can use a bonus action or reaction to speak this amulet’s command word, creating an aura that lightly obscures and gives resistance to all damage types until your next turn to everything in a 10-foot radius around you. Sword of Screams ¶ Longsword, uncommon When pulled from its scabbard, everyone within 60 feet is deafened for 1d4 turns. It has the same statistics as a longsword and is magical. While wielding this weapon you may ask the DM to play selected screamo or metal music. Ash’s Righteous Chainsaw Blade ¶ The current mechanics live in the canonical Krunk — Ash’s Righteous Chainsaw Blade handout. Historian’s Horologe ¶ Wondrous item, uncommon; does not require attunement This magical pocket watch allows its owner to transport back to a previously set position once per day. Former Character Records ¶ These items were recorded under former characters. Linked legacy ledgers preserve the last-known public information where an actual sheet survived. Eyes of the Eagle ¶ Historical owner: Ella “Explosions” Emerald Wondrous item, uncommon While wearing them, you have advantage on Perception and Investigation checks that rely on sight. In conditions of clear visibility, you can make out details of even extremely distant creatures and objects as small as 2 feet across. Helm of Invisibility ¶ Historical owner: Ella “Explosions” Emerald Wondrous item, uncommon This helmet makes the wearer’s head invisible. You may use this helm once per day to give yourself advantage on an Intimidation or Deception check. Kinesis Module ¶ Historical owner: Ella “Explosions” Emerald Wondrous item, uncommon (requires attunement) Kinesis Grab: As an action, you can cast Mage Hand . The spectral hand created by this spell is invisible. Kinesis Launch (Recharge after a Short Rest): Once per short rest, you can cast Catapult at 4th level without using a spell slot (6d8). The damage dealt by this ability can be modified by the item you choose to throw. The Kinesis Module, inspired by Dead Space , grants the wielder telekinetic abilities. This magical item is perfect for tactically minded characters who wish to manipulate their environment and use objects as weapons in creative ways. Boots of Elvenkind ¶ Historical owner: Vex Wondrous item, uncommon While you wear these boots, your steps make no sound, regardless of the surface you are moving across. You also have advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks that rely on moving silently. Necklace of Lightning Bolts ¶ Historical owner: Strawberry Wondrous guisarme, uncommon — legacy item type preserved as imported Once per turn, you can use an action to detach a bead. When you do, a 3rd-level Lightning Bolt spell (save DC 14) is created in the direction of your choice. You can detach multiple beads, or even the whole necklace, as one action. When you do so, increase the level of Lightning Bolt by 1 for each bead beyond the first. You may use this while wild shaped if the creature has enough manual dexterity. Sold or Unassigned Items ¶ Ring of the Gladiators ¶ Status: Sold by Krunk Wondrous item, common Explosive applause plays every time you critically hit with an attack or deliver a killing blow to an enemy. Add 1d6 to your next attack roll. A laugh track plays if the wielder critically fails an attack roll. Subtract 1d6 from your next attack roll. Chilling Halberd ¶ Status: Sold by Krunk Halberd, uncommon (requires attunement) You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon and can apply the Call of the Grave effect when you hit. Call of the Grave (Recharge 6): Add 1d6 necrotic damage. A ghostly skeletal hand attaches to the target, and it can’t regain hit points until the start of your next turn. Until then, the hand clings to the target. If you hit an undead target, it also has disadvantage on its next attack roll against you until the start of your next turn. Shadow Dagger ¶ Status: Sold Dagger, rare (requires attunement) You gain a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. Returning: Shadow Dagger returns to the wielder’s hand immediately after it is used to make a ranged attack. Backstabber: Roll an additional 1d4 damage when the target is flat-footed. Create Undead Minion (Long Rest): Once per long rest you may spend an action to stab the Shadow Dagger into a fresh corpse. The corpse becomes an undead minion and obeys your commands until it is destroyed or you use this ability again. High-CR creatures will be reduced to one. Demon Mask ¶ Status: Sold Wondrous item, uncommon This terrifying mask is crafted in the visage of a leering demon and grants a +1 item bonus to Intimidation checks. Leering Gaze (Long Rest): The mask casts the Fear spell with a DC of 14 (or spell bonus) on a single target that can see it. This doesn’t require concentration from the wearer. docs.text: Reward Spells ¶ Note: Reward spells require no spell slot unless specified. Crowlies Cromatic Sparks ¶ transmutation spell Casting Time: 1 action Range: 120 feet Components: V, M, S (bit of glitter) Duration: Up to 3 hours Uses: 1 per short rest This spell is similar to skywrite except it works a lot better at night since it's just fireworks without the noise. You can also write on buildings and clothing. The smaller the writing the longer it lasts. The color of the sparks is affected by the color of the glitter used. Level 5 : Writing on a surface now lasts 24 hours and you can weave intricate shapes into your writing. Wild Shrooms ¶ conjuration spell Casting Time: 1 action Range: 30 feet Components: V, M, S (dirt) Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute Uses: 1 per long rest As an action, while in the forest or underground you touch the dirt and call upon the Mycelium spirits to come to your aid! Suddenly a ring of mushrooms up to 20ft in diameter appears in the designated location. Anyone that walks within a foot of the ring is affected by the mushroom's spores. The size and effects of the mushrooms are determined by what kind they are. (best start studying those now...) Level 5 : Assuming you have been casting this, you are now proficient in mushroom knowledge and have a better idea of what kind of mushrooms you are calling forth. Animated Shroom ¶ conjuration spell Casting Time: 1 bonus action Range: 30 feet Components: V, M, S (dirt, mushroom spore) Duration: Up to 1 hour Uses: 1 per long rest As an action, you instantly grow and animate a mushroom that you control. The mushroom takes on the appearance and taste of whatever type of mushroom spore you used to animate it. The mushroom follows your instructions unless you tell it to do something stupid like jump off a cliff (it is intelligent after all). The mushroom is friendly and stays animated for 1 hour then reverts back into a regular mushroom. You can cast Animated Shroom on it again to reanimate and it will retain its memories from before. Stats (minus the sunlight sickness). https://5e.tools/bestiary/myconid-sprout-mm.html Level 7 : The mushroom gets stronger https://5e.tools/bestiary/myconid-adult-mm.html Back to Rules & Character Options

docs.text: Table Rules & Clarifications ¶ Character Alignment - Please track your character alignment using the Ethics and Morality chart . During the game your DM may require you to make an Alignment Check for heroic or evil deeds. Potions - Drinking a potion requires only a bonus action. Force feeding someone else is an action. Drinking the same potion multiple times in succession may require a Constitution saving throw. Flanking - Works the same as Pathfinder 2e . A creature is flat-footed (taking a –2 penalty to AC) to creatures that are flanking it. Lingering Injuries - These injuries will depend on the damage that caused the player to crit fail a saving throw or take damage that brings them below 0 Hit Points. Examples: Minor - Things like broken bones may cause a movement or attack disadvantage until healed during a long rest or use Lesser Restoration to remove the condition. Major - If a limb is destroyed beyond repair you may need to use a prosthetic until you find a cleric powerful enough to cast Regenerate. Curses - Some curses will require special material components in addition to the Remove Curse spell. Spell Material Components - Any spell component worth less than 100 gold or below level 4 is kept in a material pouch and never needs to be resupplied. Item Attunement - When you receive a new magic item that requires attunement you can choose to instantly attune the item if you have an attunement slot available. Attuned items that are traded between party members still require a Short Rest to attune the item to the new owner. Wild Shape Languages - In addtion to understanding languages they know, a wild shaped druid can understand and speak to beasts of the same kind it has turned into as if using the Speak with Animals spell. New Character - Generally, if a player character remains dead or missing for an extended length of time they become an NPC. Consult the DM if you wish to die or play another character. Rule Clarifications ¶ Skills with Different Abilities - We are using this variant rule. Please ask your DM if you have proficiency with a skill and would like to use a different ability for: https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/basic-rules/using-ability-scores#VariantSkillswithDifferentAbilities Healing Spirit - We are using the 2020 Errata for Healing Spirit. It can only heal a number of times equal to 1 + your spellcasting ability modifier: https://www.sageadvice.eu/2020/04/01/xanathars-guide-everything-errata/ Polymorph - While polymorphed you can still identify friend or foe but can be influenced by animalistic urges. You only understand the languages listed in the creature’s stat block. Back to Rules & Character Options

docs.text: Weapon Group Specializations ¶ Due to the rigorous daily practice it requires, you may only have one weapon group specialization at a time. You may retrain this using a week of downtime whenever you are in a friendly city. If you don't know if a weapon can be used with a specialization please ask your DM. Polearm Specialization: ¶ When you critically strike the target is moved up to 10 feet in a direction of your choice. This is forced movement. When you make an athletics check to shove a mounted foe you have advantage on any attempt to shove the rider off of its mount. Sword Specialization: ¶ When you critically strike the target is made off-balance by your attack, becoming flat-footed (-2 AC) to everyone until the start of your next turn. In place of an attack, you may use your sword to attempt to disarm an opponent of equal or smaller size by using an Athletics or Acrobatics check. Bow Specialization: ¶ If the target of the critical hit is adjacent to a surface, it gets stuck to that surface by the missile. The target is immobilized and must spend it's movement action making a DC 10 Athletics check to pull the missile free; it can’t move from its space until it succeeds. Reduce the AC provided by cover by one degree when attacking with a bow. Brawling Specialization ¶ When you critically strike the affected target’s speed is halved(minimum of 5ft) and it cannot take reactions until the start of your next turn. You have advantage on Attack rolls against a target you are Grappling. Axe Specialization ¶ When you critically strike, choose one creature adjacent to the initial target and within reach. You deal damage to that creature equal to the result of the weapon damage die you rolled. This amount isn’t doubled, and no other additional dice apply to this damage. You gain a +1 bonus to your attack roll if you already attempted to attack a different target this turn using this weapon. Club Specialization ¶ When you critically strike the affected target is knocked prone. You deal damage equal to your strength modifier when you make an athletics check to shove a target regardless of if you succeed. Dagger Specialization ¶ When you critically strike the affected target takes 1d8 persistent bleed damage. You gain an item bonus to this bleed damage equal to double the weapon’s item bonus to attack rolls. When you are wielding a dagger weapon, increase the base damage die size of that weapon by one step. Back to Rules & Character Options

docs.text: Ink Dragon Tattoo House ¶ Pain is included. Regret is billed separately. Consultation: 10 gp, credited toward any commissioned tattoo. Every symbol is translated before application. Every magical effect—and every known drawback—is written down before payment. No permanent magical work is performed on an intoxicated client, regardless of how persuasive his emergency sake may be. Prices are negotiable. Zhen accepts reasonable offers, useful barter, rare pigments, documented field testing, and interest-free installments. She will reduce the price before she reduces the safety. Art Ink — 10 to 500 gp ¶ Work Price Small linework, name, symbol, or uncomplicated mistake 10–50 gp Full-color crest, spirit animal, memorial, or scar-weaving design 50–250 gp Moonlit ink, slowly moving linework, harmless glow, or another cosmetic enchantment 150–500 gp Art Ink carries no combat power and does not count against magical-ink capacity. Cover-ups, removals, and work around old scars are quoted after inspection. Flash Ink — Temporary Magic ¶ Flash Ink lasts for its stated duration or until its single use is spent. It arrives charged, does not consume the wearer's magic, and does not recharge. A wearer can safely carry active Flash Ink designs equal to their proficiency bonus. Design Effect Shelf Life Price Second Opinion After making an Investigation, Insight, or tool check, reroll it and use the new result. The tattoo loudly explains what you did wrong either way. 7 days 75 gp Coward's Compass For 1 hour, the arrow points along the shortest traversable route to the nearest exit you could currently use. It cannot find hidden doors, cross planar boundaries, or distinguish a good exit from an embarrassing one. 7 days 100 gp Spring Hare After moving at least 15 feet, leap up to 20 feet horizontally or 10 feet vertically without a check. The landing causes no falling damage. 7 days 250 gp Borrowed Shadow For 10 minutes, detach your shadow and send it crawling up to 60 feet away. It can slip under ordinary doors and silently signal how many creatures it sees by raising ink-black fingers. You cannot see through it, and you cast no shadow while it is gone. 7 days 400 gp Dragon Sneeze One use of Dragon Sneeze (see below): a configurable elemental blast with the approximate power of a 3rd-level spell. 14 days 500 gp Two-Turn Thunderhead Spend your action on two consecutive turns charging the cloud. Taking damage before the second action spoils the charge. Once charged, fire a 30-foot line dealing 4d6 thunder damage on a failed Constitution save, half on success, and pushing failed targets 10 feet. 30 days 750 gp Koi Through the Wall Move through up to 10 feet of nonmagical wood, earth, or stone to an open space you have seen or can otherwise confirm. You cannot carry another creature. If no valid space exists, you remain where you started and the tattoo is still spent. You emerge prone and inexplicably wet. 30 days 1,000 gp Custom Flash Ink costs 50 to 1,000 gp . Unused Flash Ink fades harmlessly at the end of its shelf life. Dragon Sneeze ¶ As an action, scratch one of the dragon's four seasoning runes. The ink dragon races up your body, braces its tiny claws across your ribs, and magically overinflates your lungs. You then unleash a sneeze in either a 15-foot cone or a 30-foot-long, 5-foot-wide line , chosen when you activate it. Dragon Sneeze save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength or Constitution modifier. Choose Strength or Constitution when the tattoo is applied. The dragon supplies the element; the wearer supplies either violent respiratory commitment or lungs built like siege equipment. Each creature in the chosen area makes the rune's listed saving throw. On a failure, it takes 6d8 damage and suffers the listed rider. On a success, it takes half damage and suffers no rider. Seasoning Rune Target's Save Damage Failed-Save Rider and Duration Ember Chili Dexterity 6d8 fire The creature catches fire for up to 1 minute . At the start of each of its turns, it takes 1d8 fire damage. The burning ends when a creature uses an action to extinguish it, when it is thoroughly doused, or when magic extinguishes the flames. Unattended flammable objects in the chosen area ignite. Wintermint Constitution 6d8 cold Ice locks the creature in place, reducing its speed to 0 until the end of its next turn . On that turn, it may use an action to make a Strength (Athletics) check against the Dragon Sneeze DC, ending the effect early on a success. Storm Salt Dexterity 6d8 lightning The creature convulses with blue sparks and cannot take reactions until the end of its next turn . Any reaction it had already spent remains spent; the tattoo is powerful, not an accountant. Black Pepper Strength 6d8 thunder A Large or smaller creature is pushed 20 feet directly away and knocked prone. A Huge creature is pushed 10 feet but is not knocked prone. A Gargantuan creature is not moved. The movement is instantaneous; a prone creature remains prone until it stands normally. The sneeze instantly disperses mundane smoke, fog, and gas in the chosen area and flings unsecured Tiny objects 1d4 × 10 feet away without dealing damage. It is audible from 300 feet away. Everyone caught in it smells like the chosen seasoning for 1 hour , including creatures that succeeded on the save; Zhen insists this is how you know it worked. docs.text: As an action, scratch one of the dragon's four seasoning runes. The ink dragon races up your body, braces its tiny claws across your ribs, and magically overinflates your lungs. You then unleash a sneeze in either a 15-foot cone or a 30-foot-long, 5-foot-wide line , chosen when you activate it. Dragon Sneeze save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength or Constitution modifier. Choose Strength or Constitution when the tattoo is applied. The dragon supplies the element; the wearer supplies either violent respiratory commitment or lungs built like siege equipment. Each creature in the chosen area makes the rune's listed saving throw. On a failure, it takes 6d8 damage and suffers the listed rider. On a success, it takes half damage and suffers no rider. Seasoning Rune Target's Save Damage Failed-Save Rider and Duration Ember Chili Dexterity 6d8 fire The creature catches fire for up to 1 minute . At the start of each of its turns, it takes 1d8 fire damage. The burning ends when a creature uses an action to extinguish it, when it is thoroughly doused, or when magic extinguishes the flames. Unattended flammable objects in the chosen area ignite. Wintermint Constitution 6d8 cold Ice locks the creature in place, reducing its speed to 0 until the end of its next turn . On that turn, it may use an action to make a Strength (Athletics) check against the Dragon Sneeze DC, ending the effect early on a success. Storm Salt Dexterity 6d8 lightning The creature convulses with blue sparks and cannot take reactions until the end of its next turn . Any reaction it had already spent remains spent; the tattoo is powerful, not an accountant. Black Pepper Strength 6d8 thunder A Large or smaller creature is pushed 20 feet directly away and knocked prone. A Huge creature is pushed 10 feet but is not knocked prone. A Gargantuan creature is not moved. The movement is instantaneous; a prone creature remains prone until it stands normally. The sneeze instantly disperses mundane smoke, fog, and gas in the chosen area and flings unsecured Tiny objects 1d4 × 10 feet away without dealing damage. It is audible from 300 feet away. Everyone caught in it smells like the chosen seasoning for 1 hour , including creatures that succeeded on the save; Zhen insists this is how you know it worked.

docs.text: Jade Steam — Your First and Possibly Last Night Shift ¶ Session 078 · Temporary Staff Welcome Packet “Congratulations. You entered a spa and have progressed directly to unpaid training. The uniform is compulsory. Enthusiasm will be assessed separately.” — Madam Yu-Banya What the Hell Is Going On? ¶ After Deep Snoat's revelations and a round of questionable tattoo decisions, a bath sounded sensible. Then the tenth bell rang. The spa changed, the exit stopped being an exit, and your clothes were suddenly in another department. What the staff have told you: Someone arranged your overnight invitation, but the name is missing. Madam Yu-Banya says the sleeping lotus carried you safely through the change of shifts. The mortal entrance returns at dawn. Until your guest registration is sorted out, temporary employment keeps the bathhouse from classifying you as something it can put on a shelf. Gold is not accepted on the night shift. Service, promises, and certain personal intangibles are recognized currency. Your temporary staff agreement requires useful work until sunrise, with breaks. No blood signature or permanent surrender of your name is required. Read anything else before signing it. People You Have Been Introduced To ¶ Person What you know Madam Yu-Banya The night manager: crimson robes, towering silver hair, golden combs, and the expression of someone who has billed a thunderstorm for damages. She handles your temporary employment and insists the anonymous invitation is highly irregular. Mihiro A small Mian girl in a patched green work coat, oversized wooden sandals, and a red hair cord. She knows the service passages and has already demonstrated better survival instincts than management. She will accompany you, explain chores, and point out which instructions are meant literally. Maa and Paa — Mina and Hiro Mihiro's parents, currently goats while she works off their family debt. Maa inspects laundry; Paa eats paperwork. Mihiro would very much like her parents back. Nohbody A black-robed, white-masked spirit practicing scraps of overheard conversation. Mihiro says he copies the desires around him and becomes bigger and hungrier when fed. He seems unsure whether anyone will stay without being paid. She recommends kind company, help when he needs it, firm boundaries, and keeping your dumplings. Bobbin is with you, looking disproportionately qualified to operate the cleaning cart. Staff have asked him to stop referring to the night as “a hostile exfoliation.” Collect Your Kit — Five Staff Members ¶ Each of the five player characters receives the same uniform and one towel , then chooses a funny name tag, two utility items, and one cleaning weapon or casting tool below. Every kit also includes slippers, work gloves, a belt pouch, a red-thread focus badge, and a waterproof component sachet. Choices may repeat; the supply closet has duplicates. Bobbin and Mihiro have their own staff basics and do not take one of your five kits. Staff slot Name tag Towel Two utility items Cleaning weapon / casting tool 1 Choose below Issued Choose two Choose one 2 Choose below Issued Choose two Choose one 3 Choose below Issued Choose two Choose one 4 Choose below Issued Choose two Choose one 5 Choose below Issued Choose two Choose one These are temporary bathhouse loans , with no attunement. Their magic works only inside Jade Steam; return them before leaving. Outside combat you can exchange issued equipment at the cart. Exchanging never restores spent charges, and each character can carry only the listed allotment of enchanted loan equipment at once. Uniforms — Dress for the Job You Fear ¶ Everyone wears the same jade-green wrap robe, waterproof cream apron, and rubber-duck slippers . The apron reads TEMPORARY STAFF — PERMANENT LIABILITY . It resizes for your body, wings, horns, or other inconveniently heroic anatomy; the sash stays securely tied. Your only fashion choice is a name tag. Pick one below or invent your own; the title grants no extra powers or qualifications. Name tag Fine print The Bathromancer RAISE STANDARDS, NOT THE DEAD. The Sorcerer of Suds BORN WITH IT. WASHED WITH IT. The Warlock of Warsh MY PATRON SAYS DRY CLEAN ONLY. The Paladin of Porcelain SMITE THE MITE. The Cleric of Deep Cleaning BLESS THIS MESS. THEN REMOVE IT. The Steam-Punk LICENSED TO CARRY A BUCKET. Mop Fu Master BE LIKE SOAP. Union Representative ESSENTIAL, APPARENTLY. PAID, ALLEGEDLY. Uniform protection: AC 18. Do not add your Dexterity modifier or combine it with another base-AC calculation. The uniform cannot be further enchanted or upgraded. Separate AC bonuses from spells or features still apply normally. It counts as clothing, requires no armor proficiency, and does not prevent unarmored class features. “Management has already enchanted it against injury, embarrassment, and requests for a raise. Two out of three is acceptable.” Casters — Your Magic Still Works ¶ The red-thread badge and every issued casting tool can serve as a focus for your class's spells that use noncostly, unconsumed material components. The sachet supplies those mundane components too. A worn badge leaves your hands free, but you still need a free hand for somatic/material components unless a feature says otherwise. You may use the same hand holding a focus for a spell's material and somatic components as normal. You keep your prepared/known spells, spell slots, class features, tattoos, and worn jewelry. The uniform grants no bonus to spell attacks or spell save DCs . Components with a listed gold cost, or components the spell consumes, must still come from your belongings. Staff can bring your own required components from your locker on request; this does not conjure free diamonds or replenish supplies. A wizard's spellbook can likewise be retrieved for preparation or rituals. Your spell's normal requirements still apply. You can cast spells normally while carrying a cleaning implement. The tool attacks below are optional equipment powers, not extra spells, and do not automatically gain features that apply only to casting a spell or cantrip. Your Emergency Towel ¶ An enormous towel embroidered DON'T PANIC. IT ENCOURAGES THEM. Everyone receives one. Once per short rest, choose one use: Towel of Protection — Reaction: When you or a willing creature within 5 feet takes acid, cold, fire, necrotic, or psychic damage, reduce one instance of that damage by 2d8 . You must be able to reach the creature. Multiple towels cannot reduce the same damage instance. Please Hold Still — Action: End blindness on yourself or a willing creature within 5 feet caused specifically by nonmagical slime, soot, soap, or another removable surface coating. This does not cure disease, injury, magical blindness, or a spell. After use, it remains a perfectly good ordinary towel. Its magic recharges when its assigned wearer finishes a short or long rest; swapping towels does not grant extra uses. It also dries you, preserves your dignity, and silently judges your folding. Utility Cupboard — Choose Two ¶ Unless stated otherwise, each use takes an action and requires a free hand. These tools help solve physical problems; they do not automatically remove a curse or replace good judgment. Utility What it does Sponge of Unreasonable Absorbency Touch an unattended pool/spill to absorb up to 1 cubic foot of nonmagical liquid ; that is also its capacity. Squeeze it into a container to empty it. Cannot pull liquid from a creature, remove bodily fluids, absorb a magical effect, or turn stored liquid into a damaging spray. Wear the gloves for hazardous spills. Polter-Tongs Manipulate one unattended object of 10 lb. or less within 10 ft. that you can see, moving it up to 10 ft. Uses your hand's motion; cannot attack, pick locks, steal worn/held items, pass through barriers, or perform skilled work independently. Useful for suspicious teeth. Rubber Duck of Due Diligence Set it in liquid. For 1 minute it paddles at up to 10 ft. per round along the surface flow, quacking at visible obstructions. It cannot sense poison, magic, creatures, depth, or hidden passages. It has very strong opinions about drains but no special knowledge of them. OSHA-Approved Soap Three doses for the night. Coat one 5-ft. square within reach on solid ground for 1 minute , until washed away, or until someone wipes it up with an action. The first creature entering it on a turn makes a DC 15 Dexterity save or falls prone; at most once per creature per turn. It affects allies too and does not stack with itself. Evidence Before Exorcism Jar An airtight, nonmagical sample jar and tongs, capacity 1 quart . The jar tolerates ordinary corrosive cleaning chemicals; it is not immune to attacks or supernatural substances. No stasis, spirit imprisonment, or extradimensional storage. Label reads IF IT HAS A LAWYER, ASK FIRST . Squeegee of Clear Intentions Wipe up to 5 ft. square of reachable glass, tile, or metal clean of nonmagical surface condensation, grease, and grime. Does not erase writing, dissolve an object, or dispel a magical effect. It squeaks like a very disappointed violin. Inspector's Bubble Lens Once per short rest , after rolling an Investigation check to examine a visible physical mess, mechanism, or evidence, but before the result is declared, add 1d4 . Must spend at least an action examining it. No reading thoughts or seeing invisible creatures. Recharges for its assigned wearer, not by trading it around. Gloves of Absolutely Not Elbow-length work gloves. Handle filthy or ordinarily caustic objects safely when no damage is otherwise called for. Once per short rest, reaction: reduce acid damage to yourself by 1d8 + PB . Does not stack with an Emergency Towel against the same damage. The gloves visibly recoil before you touch anything especially disgusting. Cleaning Weapons and Casting Tools — Choose One ¶ Choose Strength, Dexterity, or one of your spellcasting abilities for an issued tool's attacks and save DC; use that same ability until you finish a short rest. At level 12, proficiency bonus is normally +4 . Tool attack bonus = proficiency bonus + chosen ability modifier. Tool save DC = 8 + proficiency bonus + chosen ability modifier. These are separate from your normal spell figures. All tools are magical; you are proficient with them. There is no hidden +1/+2 bonus. Tool Combat rules Household application Mop of Seven Ends Two-handed melee weapon, 10-ft. reach , 2d8 + modifier force . Once per turn on hit, push a Huge or smaller target 5 ft. , or clear one 5-ft. patch of slime in its space. Works with Extra Attack. Wringing the heads makes seven distinct noises of disgust. Sacred Plunger of Last Resort Two-handed melee weapon, 5-ft. reach , 2d10 + modifier bludgeoning . Critical on 19–20 against constructs or animated plumbing . Works with Extra Attack and features requiring a melee weapon. The handle reads IN CASE OF APOCALYPSE, BREAK SEAL . Ghost-Hose Nozzle Two-handed ranged weapon, range 60/120 ft. , 2d10 + modifier radiant . Once per turn on hit, reduce a Huge or smaller target's speed by 10 ft. until your next turn starts ; multiple hoses do not stack this reduction. Works with Extra Attack. Self-contained reservoir; no hose tether required. WHO YOU GONNA SOAP? Sponge Knuckles One-handed melee weapon, 5-ft. reach , 2d6 + modifier force . Works with Extra Attack. After a hit, you may harmlessly clean one nonmagical surface smear from the target; this does not remove conditions or defenses. Requires a hand to wield; not an unarmed strike or free-hand focus. Each punch makes a magnificent squeak. Hex & Shoulders Atomizer One-handed focus. Action: make one ranged spell attack using your tool attack bonus , range 60 ft. , dealing 3d8 + modifier radiant on a hit. Does not use Extra Attack or spend a spell slot. Removes flakes. Occasionally existential ones. Dustbuster of the Damned Two-handed focus. Action: one creature you see within 30 ft. makes a Strength save against your tool DC . Failure: 4d8 force and pulled 10 ft. toward you if Huge or smaller; success: half damage, no pull. Does not capture or contain the creature. The filter bag is marked SOULS SOLD SEPARATELY . Alternatively, ring to outline invisible creatures within 15 ft. until your next turn starts , removing invisibility's benefits; blocked by total cover. Alerts housekeeping, ghosts, and everyone trying to nap. Salt Scattergun Two-handed tool, three charges for the night . Action: 15-ft. cone , Dexterity save against your tool DC: 4d8 radiant , half on success. On failure, a target cannot benefit from invisibility until the end of its next turn. Please season responsibly. For an action-based tool power , take that action instead of casting a spell or using the Attack action; Extra Attack does not multiply it. Bonus actions and reactions remain subject to your normal features. Trading or replacing a charged tool never refills it: each character receives only one three-charge allotment for each charged tool type over the night. A brass trolley with six folding legs, mop racks, sample drawers, and a bell that prints workplace-incident slips. It follows the party whenever the route permits. Bobbin usually steers; Mihiro knows where to park it. It carries spare mundane towels, buckets, soap, chalk, salt, gloves, tongs, sealing paper, a 50-ft. rope, basic cleaning supplies, and component sachets. These are supplies, not unlimited alchemical ammunition or precious spell components. Item exchanges take a minute outside combat, and supplies cannot recharge powers already used. Between encounters it walks at 30 ft. speed , climbs ordinary stairs, and folds to fit a 3-ft.-wide passage . It cannot fly, teleport, open locked doors, swim safely through deep water, scout independently, or know a route nobody has shown it. If the party takes an inaccessible shortcut, leave it parked and carry the needed equipment; it can rejoin by a known accessible route. In combat, a character within 5 ft. may use a bonus action to direct it up to 30 ft. along a clear floor route . The cart can move this way only once per round , has no initiative or attacks, and cannot ram creatures. Taking one accessible mundane item uses your normal object interaction. It is a Medium object, AC 15, 40 HP ; at 0 HP its legs lock instead of exploding. Ten minutes of mundane repair restores it to working order with full HP. Repair requires a safe pause and cannot be repeated as combat healing. It does not grant automatic cover; use the actual positioning and ordinary cover rules. The Work Board ¶ Choose where to start. Mihiro accompanies you and Bobbin brings the cart. You are not required to finish all five jobs before an approved break or emergency reassignment. Card Assignment Management's helpful advice A — Linen Annex Seven Count and fold forty-nine robes; isolate the extra one. “If it folds you first, ring for assistance.” B — Honeymoon Suite / The Exorcise Room Clean the departing guests' spectacular mess and prepare the suite for another booking. “Start at the ceiling. You will understand why.” C — Long-Distance Guest Care Help bathe a mountain-lake patron who traveled an extraordinary distance for treatment. “Courteous. Gentle. Upwind.” D — Boiler-Crew Supper Deliver meals and feed the smallest workers as well as their supervisor. “Soot sprites are staff, not fuel.” E — Lost-Property Audit Check the cedar lockers and stop the paper birds rearranging ownership. Your belongings are stored there. “A bird carrying a receipt is still a bird.” Rules Worth Remembering ¶ Keep your red thread on and do useful work. Ask before taking a break. Honest mistakes and choosing a different job are not refusal of duty. Do not accept Nohbody's gold or feed his growing appetite. You may be kind without making a sale. Read the label before opening a valve, eating a snack, or promising anything in perpetuity. Your usual abilities still matter. Consider using it before the floor develops a legal defense. Questions about survival: Mihiro. Questions about invoices: Madam Yu-Banya. Questions about the smell: please stop asking.

docs.title: Jade Steam — Your First and Possibly Last Night Shift

docs.text: After Deep Snoat's revelations and a round of questionable tattoo decisions, a bath sounded sensible. Then the tenth bell rang. The spa changed, the exit stopped being an exit, and your clothes were suddenly in another department. What the staff have told you: Someone arranged your overnight invitation, but the name is missing. Madam Yu-Banya says the sleeping lotus carried you safely through the change of shifts. The mortal entrance returns at dawn. Until your guest registration is sorted out, temporary employment keeps the bathhouse from classifying you as something it can put on a shelf. Gold is not accepted on the night shift. Service, promises, and certain personal intangibles are recognized currency. Your temporary staff agreement requires useful work until sunrise, with breaks. No blood signature or permanent surrender of your name is required. Read anything else before signing it.
docs.title: What the Hell Is Going On?

docs.text: Person What you know Madam Yu-Banya The night manager: crimson robes, towering silver hair, golden combs, and the expression of someone who has billed a thunderstorm for damages. She handles your temporary employment and insists the anonymous invitation is highly irregular. Mihiro A small Mian girl in a patched green work coat, oversized wooden sandals, and a red hair cord. She knows the service passages and has already demonstrated better survival instincts than management. She will accompany you, explain chores, and point out which instructions are meant literally. Maa and Paa — Mina and Hiro Mihiro's parents, currently goats while she works off their family debt. Maa inspects laundry; Paa eats paperwork. Mihiro would very much like her parents back. Nohbody A black-robed, white-masked spirit practicing scraps of overheard conversation. Mihiro says he copies the desires around him and becomes bigger and hungrier when fed. He seems unsure whether anyone will stay without being paid. She recommends kind company, help when he needs it, firm boundaries, and keeping your dumplings. Bobbin is with you, looking disproportionately qualified to operate the cleaning cart. Staff have asked him to stop referring to the night as “a hostile exfoliation.”

docs.text: Everyone wears the same jade-green wrap robe, waterproof cream apron, and rubber-duck slippers . The apron reads TEMPORARY STAFF — PERMANENT LIABILITY . It resizes for your body, wings, horns, or other inconveniently heroic anatomy; the sash stays securely tied. Your only fashion choice is a name tag. Pick one below or invent your own; the title grants no extra powers or qualifications. Name tag Fine print The Bathromancer RAISE STANDARDS, NOT THE DEAD. The Sorcerer of Suds BORN WITH IT. WASHED WITH IT. The Warlock of Warsh MY PATRON SAYS DRY CLEAN ONLY. The Paladin of Porcelain SMITE THE MITE. The Cleric of Deep Cleaning BLESS THIS MESS. THEN REMOVE IT. The Steam-Punk LICENSED TO CARRY A BUCKET. Mop Fu Master BE LIKE SOAP. Union Representative ESSENTIAL, APPARENTLY. PAID, ALLEGEDLY. Uniform protection: AC 18. Do not add your Dexterity modifier or combine it with another base-AC calculation. The uniform cannot be further enchanted or upgraded. Separate AC bonuses from spells or features still apply normally. It counts as clothing, requires no armor proficiency, and does not prevent unarmored class features. “Management has already enchanted it against injury, embarrassment, and requests for a raise. Two out of three is acceptable.”
docs.title: Uniforms — Dress for the Job You Fear

docs.text: The red-thread badge and every issued casting tool can serve as a focus for your class's spells that use noncostly, unconsumed material components. The sachet supplies those mundane components too. A worn badge leaves your hands free, but you still need a free hand for somatic/material components unless a feature says otherwise. You may use the same hand holding a focus for a spell's material and somatic components as normal. You keep your prepared/known spells, spell slots, class features, tattoos, and worn jewelry. The uniform grants no bonus to spell attacks or spell save DCs . Components with a listed gold cost, or components the spell consumes, must still come from your belongings. Staff can bring your own required components from your locker on request; this does not conjure free diamonds or replenish supplies. A wizard's spellbook can likewise be retrieved for preparation or rituals. Your spell's normal requirements still apply. You can cast spells normally while carrying a cleaning implement. The tool attacks below are optional equipment powers, not extra spells, and do not automatically gain features that apply only to casting a spell or cantrip.
docs.title: Casters — Your Magic Still Works

docs.text: An enormous towel embroidered DON'T PANIC. IT ENCOURAGES THEM. Everyone receives one. Once per short rest, choose one use: Towel of Protection — Reaction: When you or a willing creature within 5 feet takes acid, cold, fire, necrotic, or psychic damage, reduce one instance of that damage by 2d8 . You must be able to reach the creature. Multiple towels cannot reduce the same damage instance. Please Hold Still — Action: End blindness on yourself or a willing creature within 5 feet caused specifically by nonmagical slime, soot, soap, or another removable surface coating. This does not cure disease, injury, magical blindness, or a spell. After use, it remains a perfectly good ordinary towel. Its magic recharges when its assigned wearer finishes a short or long rest; swapping towels does not grant extra uses. It also dries you, preserves your dignity, and silently judges your folding.

docs.text: Unless stated otherwise, each use takes an action and requires a free hand. These tools help solve physical problems; they do not automatically remove a curse or replace good judgment. Utility What it does Sponge of Unreasonable Absorbency Touch an unattended pool/spill to absorb up to 1 cubic foot of nonmagical liquid ; that is also its capacity. Wear the gloves for hazardous spills. Polter-Tongs Manipulate one unattended object of 10 lb. or less within 10 ft. that you can see, moving it up to 10 ft. Uses your hand's motion; cannot attack, pick locks, steal worn/held items, pass through barriers, or perform skilled work independently. Useful for suspicious teeth. Rubber Duck of Due Diligence Set it in liquid. For 1 minute it paddles at up to 10 ft. per round along the surface flow, quacking at visible obstructions. It cannot sense poison, magic, creatures, depth, or hidden passages. It has very strong opinions about drains but no special knowledge of them. OSHA-Approved Soap Three doses for the night. Coat one 5-ft. square within reach on solid ground for 1 minute , until washed away, or until someone wipes it up with an action. The first creature entering it on a turn makes a DC 15 Dexterity save or falls prone; at most once per creature per turn. It affects allies too and does not stack with itself. Must spend at least an action examining it. No reading thoughts or seeing invisible creatures. Recharges for its assigned wearer, not by trading it around. Once per short rest, reaction: reduce acid damage to yourself by 1d8 + PB . Does not stack with an Emergency Towel against the same damage. Heroic destinies may be checked at the desk. The staff did not notice the next room. Neither did you. Cannonballs are billed according to displaced water. If the tenth bell rings during your appointment, please proceed calmly to an exit that still exists. Tea may always be replaced with sake. Wisdom may not.

docs.text: 🧀 Kardarsha’s Curds & Curios — Arena Pop-Up Menu ¶ “Lactose? This one prefers lack-of-morals in his enemies.” All magical cheeses are single-use consumables (bonus action to eat a wedge or action to share a slice). Unless noted, effects last 1 minute and require attunement to nothing but bravery . Most effects are 1/short rest per creature (you can’t stack same cheese twice). Save DCs are 15 (or use your spell DC if higher when required). Everyday Wheels (Non-Magical, Delicious) ¶ Item Price Notes Arena Snack Board (assorted curds, crackers) 5 sp Hearty, feeds 2; gain 1d4 temp HP while spectating. Grilled Goudini 8 sp Melted gouda on toasted bread; advantage on the next Charisma (Performance) in the next hour (but your fingers are greasy). Brick of Courage (aged cheddar slab) 2 gp Short rest snack: one creature regains +1d4 extra HP from Hit Dice. Battle Bites (Quick Buffs with Small Bites Back) ¶ Cheese Price Effect (Pros) Side Effect (Cons) Muenstermind 25 gp For 1 min: add +1d4 to INT/WIS/CHA checks ; once to a save . Brain freeze: –2 to Initiative until next short rest. Pepperjack Unleashed 30 gp Bonus action: your next melee hit deals +1d6 fire . Hiccups: Disadvantage on Stealth for 1 min. Blue Fortify (veiny blue) 35 gp Gain resistance to bludgeoning for 1 min. Pungent aura: adjacent creatures (ally or enemy) must succeed DC 10 Con or have Disadvantage on Persuasion checks with them for 10 min. String Theory 30 gp Cast feather fall on self; once within 1 min, use a reaction to pull 10 ft toward a surface you can grab. Sticky: speed –5 ft for 1 min. Affinage Arcana (Magical Singles) ¶ Cheese Price Effect (Pros) Side Effect (Cons) Parmesan of Parry & Riposta 60 gp For 1 min: when a creature misses you, you can riposte for +1d8 slashing (1/round). Brittle: on a nat 1 attack, your weapon suffers –1 damage until repaired (mends after long rest or mending ). Brie of Brief Invisibility 90 gp invisibility on self (Concentration, 1 min) ; ends if you attack/cast. Rind-crumb trail: creatures tracking you have Advantage on the first Survival check after it ends. Gorgon-Zola 75 gp Bonus action glare at one target in 30 ft: DC 15 Con or Restrained by hardening curds until end of your next turn. If they save, you’re Stunned by their stink for 1 round ( end at your turn’s end ). Havarti Haste-ish 120 gp For 1 min: +10 ft speed , +1 AC , and one extra object interaction each turn; once during duration you can Dash as a bonus action . Whey crash: after it ends, you are Sluggish (can’t Dash) for 1 minute . Provo-Clone 150 gp Action: create an illusory duplicate (as mirror image , but only 1 image ) for 1 min. Doppelganger déjà vu: the first Insight check against you has Advantage for 10 min. Smoked Gouda-Luck 100 gp Gain 1 Luck die ( 1d6 ) to add to any d20 roll in the next hour. Ashy breath: until used, Disadvantage on Deception (smoke tells). Potent Plates (Once Per Long Rest, Shareable Slices) ¶ Cheese Price Effect (Pros) Side Effect (Cons) Camem-Bard 220 gp Share among up to 3 creatures: each gains Inspiration (one use) and can cast thaumaturgy 3/day for 24h. Chorus curse: you involuntarily hum; Stealth checks have –2 for 24h. Swiss of Second Windfall 250 gp As a reaction when reduced to 0 HP: drop to 1 HP instead and gain temp HP = your level . Triggers automatically within 24h of eating. Holes in memory: forget one minor detail (DM picks) for 24h. Cheddar Gate (folded sandwich) 260 gp Open/close one unattended nonmagical door/portcullis within 60 ft as if by knock (no sound). Crumb trail: leaves glowing crumbs; tracked easily for 10 min (DC 10 Perception). Burrata of Burrowing 280 gp Gain tremorsense 30 ft and can move through loose earth at half speed for 1 min. Mud gut: Disadvantage on Con saves vs. poison for 1 hour. Wildly Cursed Clearance (Sold “as-is”) ¶ Each wedge works once ; many are 1/short rest if you dare again. Eating a cursed cheese requires a DC 15 Wis save to anticipate the hiccup; on a success, you can choose to cancel the effect after it triggers. Cursed Cheese Price What It Does And The Catch… Roquefort of Roaring 10 gp As a bonus action, cause fear (DC 15 Wis) on one creature in 30 ft. You also roar— everyone within 10 ft must save or be startled (drop held item). Velveeternal Flame 15 gp Your next melee hit adds 1d8 fire and sheds bright light 20 ft for 1 min. You melt slightly: weapons hitting you in melee deal +1 fire to you during that minute. Feta Accompli 20 gp Once within 1 min, declare “ Feta accompli! ” to auto-succeed a check (not attacks/saves). Immediately after, the next check you make auto-fails . Curd of Holding 30 gp Store one Tiny object in the cheese; retrieve as an action. If you take thunder damage, it burps —random stored item ejects loudly (and smelly). Nachomancy Kit 25 gp Read your future in chips: ask one yes/no question as augury . Answer is always preceded by “ …if you don’t share .” If you didn’t share the nachos, result may be inverted (DM fun). Bleeuugh Cheese 5 gp Immediately end charmed or frightened on yourself. Also end any concentration you’re maintaining (because… bleeuugh).
