docs.text: Krunk “the Drunk” — Campaign Ledger ¶ Review draft. Best-effort transcription of Krunk's handwritten level-12 sheet and item cards, received September 2026. Questionable readings are collected under Needs Player Review instead of being treated as settled rules. Half-Orc Paladin 12 — Oath of Vengeance Background: Soldier (Officer) • Alignment: Neutral Good • Holy Symbol: The White Hand AC: 20 • HP Maximum: 107 • Speed: 30 ft • Initiative: +0 Proficiency Bonus: +4 • Spell Save DC: 16, or 18 with Excalibur • Spell Attack: +8, or +10 with Excalibur Hit Dice: 12d10 • Passive Perception: 11 Ability Scores ¶ STR DEX CON INT WIS CHA 18 (+4) 10 (+0) 15 (+2) 8 (−1) 12 (+1) 18 (+4) Carrying capacity: 270 lb • Push, drag, or lift: 540 lb Saving Throws ¶ Krunk's written totals include his Aura of Protection bonus. Strength Dexterity Constitution Intelligence Wisdom Charisma +8 +4 +10 +3 +9 +12 Krunk is proficient in Constitution saves through Resilient , and in Wisdom and Charisma saves through his class. Skills and Proficiencies ¶ Skill Bonus Notes Athletics +8 Proficient Animal Handling +5 Proficient; the sheet also notes vehicles here Insight +5 Proficient Medicine +5 Proficient Intimidation +8 Proficient; Menacing Persuasion +8 Proficient Weapons: Simple weapons and martial weapons Armor: All armor and shields Tools: Dice set Vehicles: Land vehicles Languages: Common and Orc, written in Dwarvish script Attack Reference ¶ Weapon Attack Damage Notes Excalibur, the Promised Dawn +2 +10 1d8 + 6 one-handed or 1d10 + 6 two-handed Versatile; once per turn against evil, add +4 radiant from Radiant Edge; see the full Excalibur handout Maul of Maelstroms +2 +10 2d6 + 4 bludgeoning plus 2 lightning Two-handed; attuned Heavy War Pick +8 1d10 + 4 piercing Confirmed homebrew heavy version Ash's Righteous Chainsaw Blade +2 +10 2d6 + 6 slashing Two-handed; attuned; see the original item handout Krunk has Extra Attack , so he attacks twice whenever he takes the Attack action. Weapon Group Specialization — Clubs ¶ Krunk uses Club Specialization : When Krunk critically strikes with a club-group weapon, the target is knocked prone. Whenever Krunk makes a Strength (Athletics) check to shove a target, he deals damage equal to his Strength modifier ( 4 ) whether the shove succeeds or fails. Core Features ¶ Darkvision. Krunk can see in darkness out to 60 feet. Menacing. Krunk is proficient in Intimidation. Relentless Endurance. Once per long rest, when reduced to 0 HP but not killed outright, Krunk drops to 1 HP instead. Savage Attacks. On a critical hit with a melee weapon, roll one additional weapon damage die. Resilient (Constitution). Krunk is proficient in Constitution saving throws. Great Weapon Master. Before making an attack with a heavy weapon he is proficient with, Krunk may take −5 to hit for +10 damage. A critical hit or reducing a creature to 0 HP can grant a bonus-action melee attack. Great Weapon Fighting. When Krunk rolls a 1 or 2 on a damage die for a two-handed or versatile melee weapon wielded with two hands, he may reroll that die and must use the new result. Divine Health. Krunk is immune to disease. Lay on Hands. Krunk has a pool of 60 HP per long rest. He may also spend 5 HP from the pool to cure one disease or neutralize one poison. Divine Sense — 5/long rest. As an action, Krunk detects celestials, fiends, and undead within 60 feet that are not behind total cover. Divine Smite. After hitting with a melee weapon, expend a spell slot for 2d8 radiant damage, plus 1d8 per slot level above 1st to a maximum of 5d8 , and another 1d8 against a fiend or undead. Improved Divine Smite. Krunk's melee weapon hits deal an extra 1d8 radiant damage. Aura of Protection. Krunk and friendly creatures within 10 feet add his +4 Charisma modifier to saving throws while he is conscious. Aura of Courage. Krunk and friendly creatures within 10 feet cannot be frightened while he is conscious. Relentless Avenger. After hitting with an opportunity attack, Krunk may move up to half his speed without provoking opportunity attacks. Channel Divinity ¶ Abjure Enemy. As an action, choose one creature within 60 feet. It makes a Wisdom save; fiends and undead have disadvantage. On a failure it is frightened for 1 minute and its speed becomes 0. On a success its speed is halved for 1 minute or until it takes damage. Vow of Enmity. As a bonus action, choose a creature within 10 feet. Krunk has advantage on attack rolls against it for 1 minute or until it drops to 0 HP or falls unconscious. Roleplaying Notes ¶ Traits: Fight the greater evil. Haunted by war and nightmares. His homeland was ravaged by war. Ideal: Independence. No mercy for the wicked. Bond: “I fight for the helpless by any means necessary.” Flaw: “My hatred is blind and unwavering.” Retribution comes before restraint. Currency and Major Purchases ¶ Price note: These are the shop's listed prices. Krunk purchased the tattoos at substantial discounts; the exact amounts paid were not recorded on the photographed sheet. Session Vendor Purchase Listed price Paid by Mechanical effect or statistics Notes 077 Ink Dragon Tattoo House Adventurer's Party Line — Budget Family Plan 140 gp Krunk Shared 25-word message and 25-word replies every 10 minutes Linked to Amerilis, Chao, Bobbin, and Caracas 077 Ink Dragon Tattoo House Dragon Sneeze — Dragon With Allergies 1,500 gp Krunk Once per short rest, 6d8 elemental damage in a 15-foot cone or 30-foot line While charged, any natural 1 Krunk rolls on any d20 triggers an accidental sneeze 077 Ink Dragon Tattoo House Lucifer's Last Run 2,000 gp Krunk Once per long rest, rush toward an ally who falls to 0 HP without provoking Costs a 1st-level spell slot or 1 Hit Die Permanent Upgrades and Custom Abilities ¶ Name Source Uses / recharge Rules summary Notes Adventurer's Party Line — Budget Family Plan Ink Dragon catalog Once every 10 minutes; shared cooldown Send 25 words to the group; each member may reply with 25 words Cannot mute, leave, or send privately Dragon Sneeze — Dragon With Allergies Ink Dragon catalog Once per short rest 6d8 damage in a 15-foot cone or 30-foot line; choose one of four seasoning runes While charged, any natural 1 on any d20 roll triggers a random sneeze; save DC uses Krunk's Strength or Constitution modifier Lucifer's Last Run Ink Dragon catalog Once per long rest Reaction to move up to speed toward an ally who falls to 0 HP without provoking Costs a 1st-level spell slot or 1 Hit Die Current Important Equipment ¶ Ash's Righteous Chainsaw Blade +2 ¶ Rare, two-handed; requires attunement by a paladin Grants +2 to attack and damage rolls. Deals 2d6 slashing damage before modifiers. Objects and creatures made of wood are vulnerable to damage from the weapon. On a critical hit against an undead creature, it deals an extra 2d8 fire damage. Chainsaw Roar. At the start of combat, Krunk may activate the roar. Everyone within 30 feet must succeed on a DC 14 Constitution save or be deafened until the end of their next turn. Maul of Maelstroms +2 ¶ Uncommon, two-handed; requires attunement Grants +2 to attack and damage rolls. The +2 damage bonus is lightning damage. Battle Cry. Once per long rest, Krunk may shout and slam an enemy for an extra 1d10 thunder damage. The target must succeed on a DC 15 Strength save or be pushed 10 feet and knocked prone. The weapon gives a slight shock when picked up and seems to vibrate with energy. Historian's Horologe ¶ Uncommon; does not require attunement This magical pocket watch allows its owner to teleport back to a previously set position once per day. Veil of Shadows — Shield of the Void ¶ Rare, requires attunement A large black amulet. Once per day, Krunk may use a bonus action or reaction and speak its command word— “FUCK NO!” —to create a lightly obscuring 10-foot aura. Until the start of his next turn, everything in the aura has resistance to all damage. Excalibur, the Promised Dawn ¶ Krunk currently carries and is attuned to Excalibur, the Promised Dawn , a +2 versatile longsword . With Strength +4, he attacks at +10 and deals 1d8 + 6 slashing one-handed or 1d10 + 6 slashing two-handed. Once per turn against a creature Excalibur deems evil, Radiant Edge adds +4 radiant damage . Excalibur's Spellcasting Enhancement: Krunk's spell save DC increases from 16 to 18 and his spell attack modifier increases from +8 to +10 while he wields Excalibur or keeps a hand on its hilt while it is sheathed, provided he is not wielding another weapon. A shield is allowed. Releasing the hilt or drawing another weapon ends the bonuses. Other Carried Gear ¶ The following low-magic and mundane equipment is transcribed from the current character sheet. Debts, Favors, and Ongoing Services ¶ Owed to / by Terms Status Notes Needs Player Review ¶ Spell figures: Krunk's base spell save DC 16 and spell attack +8 are calculated from Charisma 18 and proficiency +4; they are not written in dedicated boxes on the photographed page. While using Excalibur's spellcasting enhancement, they become DC 18 and +10 . Current HP: The sheet appears to show 69 current HP, but that is a changing session value and is intentionally not recorded as a permanent statistic. docs.text: Mian Lung ¶ Type: Province of the Republic of Leonia Historic name: The Jade Kingdom Location: Eastern coast of Leonia People: The Mian Provincial leader: Chancellor Jack E. Chan Known for: Soldiers, sword saints, river trade, old traditions Mian Lung is an old eastern realm inside a young republic. Its history predates Leonia, its people retain a strong identity of their own, and its soldiers form the backbone of the republic's armed forces. The name Mian Lung is commonly translated as “Distant from the Dragon.” Mian tradition says its people are ancient wanderers from a faraway kingdom called Shou Lung , “Receiver of the Dragon.” The journey is too old to verify and too good a story to stop telling. Land and People ¶ Mian Lung stretches along Leonia's eastern coastline. River valleys, wooded foothills, fishing villages, fortified settlements, and old city-states shape the province. Xuán Ji , the “Mysterious River,” is among its best-known regions. For generations, the noble Fang family supervised trade along its river and foothills. The Mian have a reputation for discipline, duty, skilled craftsmanship, and formidable martial traditions. Fishing, trapping, river trade, farming, forestry, and military service have all shaped life here. Urban expansion has also consumed forests and other natural resources, driving old nature spirits deeper into the wilds. Mian Lung has excellent roads to history and several potholes to modernity. Deuce Leem, Guardian of Xuán Ji ¶ Deuce Leem is a powerful water spirit traditionally said to guard the Xuán Ji. He seldom leaves the river, preferring to answer problems by flowing around them, through them, or—when the problem is an invading army—directly over them. During the War of Broken Chains, trapped Mian soldiers beat the old water drums and called for aid at Eclipse Ford. Deuce answered from Xuán Ji and strengthened the failing sluice flood that broke the New Moon Battalion. Lincohn handled the vampire officers; Deuce handled the water; generations of playwrights have handled the credit. Mian martial artists often repeat his best-known advice: “Be water, my friend.” Shrines depict him in dozens of contradictory fighting stances, but all agree that his hair looked excellent in the rain. Current Crisis: The Fires in Mian Lung ¶ Mian Lung is burning again. A new order called the Jǐn Bào , or “Golden Leopards,” claims it will restore balance through fire. Its leader, Master Zhaoyan , preaches purity and obedience to the flame. The results are less poetic than the speeches. Villages have vanished, temples have fallen silent, and the Mógu Chóng Bài have gone into hiding. Refugees describe rivers black with ash and feline shadows moving across rooftops at dawn. Fang Ro received a scroll sealed in red wax and bearing her name in Infernal. She recognizes the Jǐn Bào's rhetoric from earlier violence and believed she had already ended whatever movement inspired it. Fang has left the party and returned to Mian Lung to aid her homeland; Black Chao has joined the party in her absence. What the Jǐn Bào truly wants, whether the reports of feline shadows are literal, and who sent Fang's infernal message remain unknown. Mian Lung currently has more questions than answers and significantly more fire than either. From Jade Kingdom to Leonian Province ¶ About two hundred years ago, an earthquake in the Qlohsh Highlands unleashed an infernal army. A breakaway force marched east, destroyed settlements, and threatened Mian Lung before warnings could reach the province. Mian Lung fought that incursion as the independent Jade Kingdom. During the same broad era of regional danger, Armskirk, Torath, and Corvos formed their own mutual-protection pact. Their alliance became the Republic of Leonia; Mian Lung was not one of its founding members. After Leonia existed, the Jade Kingdom signed a separate mutual-defense treaty with the new republic. The two states cooperated against common threats, but Mian Lung remained sovereign. About one hundred years ago, the Jade-Lion Concord made Mian Lung a full province of Leonia. The agreement preserved the office of Chancellor and many local institutions while formalizing military service, taxes, food levies, and Mian representation in national government. Leonian historians call this “full inclusion.” Mian historians often call it “the second agreement, with considerably more fine print.” Government and Leonia ¶ Mian Lung is governed locally by Chancellor Jack E. Chan , who also represents the province before the Ringleader's government. The province retains older laws, customs, titles, and institutions so long as they do not conflict with the Leonian charter. Mian Lung pays substantial tax and food levies to the republic and supplies a large share of its professional soldiers. The Mian have honored those obligations for generations, though “honored” and “enjoyed” are very different verbs. The Nine Tables and One Ballot ¶ Mian Lung elects its Chancellor every six years through the Nine Tables and One Ballot . Prospective candidates must first earn endorsements from nine traditional constituencies: farmers, fishers, soldiers, artisans, merchants, scholars, temples, city wards, and rural clans. They then face a day-long public examination conducted at nine literal tables. The tests include interpreting law, balancing a granary ledger, settling a mock boundary dispute, planning a flood evacuation, and brewing tea while elderly spectators loudly explain how the previous candidate did it better. Anyone who survives all nine tables without fleeing, bribing an examiner, or declaring war on the audience earns a place on the ballot. The province then chooses its Chancellor by ranked-choice vote. This preserves the ancient principle that leaders should possess wisdom, patience, practical skill, and at least one afternoon they will never discuss again. The victor is inaugurated beneath an enormous golden dragon puppet carried by eighty volunteers. Tradition requires the dragon to bow before the new Chancellor. Tradition also forbids enlarging the palace doors, so the inauguration has taken place outside for 312 consecutive years. The Chancellor administers Mian Lung's provincial budget, granaries, roads, canals, civil defense, local courts, and civil appointments. The office may mobilize provincial forces during an immediate emergency, but sustained national deployment belongs to Leonia's Master of the Muster. At the Hall of Accord, the Chancellor occupies the separate Jade Seat rather than joining the six-member Barker Circle. The Jade Seat has a binding vote on changes to the Jade-Lion Concord, Mian taxes and food levies, deployment of Mian forces beyond the province, and national laws written specifically for Mian Lung. On other national business, the Chancellor may speak, advise, object, and produce an intimidating quantity of documentation, but does not cast a Barker vote. Chancellor Jack E. Chan ¶ Jack E. Chan is a former civil-defense organizer and treaty negotiator who would rather fix a problem himself than order someone else into danger. He is warm, practical, self-deprecating, and remarkably capable, though rarely dignified while demonstrating it. He has been known to catch falling scrolls, teacups, and pieces of furniture without interrupting a meeting. When violence is unavoidable, he favors improvised objects, rapid movement, and apologizing to whatever he breaks. He has an ancient and deeply personal feud with ladders. Chan supports the republic but argues that Leonia too often treats Mian Lung as a barracks and pantry rather than a full province. He wants fairer levies, greater provincial investment, and recognition for what the Mian contribute beyond military service. His greatest weakness is that he delegates poorly. Chan will exhaust himself protecting others long after a wiser leader would have asked for help. “Government is like a ladder: useful, necessary, and always falling toward the person least prepared to catch it.” The Martial State ¶ Military service is central to Mian Lung's public identity. In ordinary times, its forces range from local levies and trained infantry to cavalry, shi knights, and elite companies. During major incursions, conscription may be imposed. The most celebrated elite warriors are the jiàn shèng , or “sword saints.” They train from youth with the jiàn and horn bow, combining discipline, mobility, and an alarming ability to turn “unarmored” into a threat. The Night Tigers are an elite Mian company commanded by Heise Chao Ping , better known as Black Chao . The company earned its reputation surviving infernal attacks and later developed difficult war games designed to remove the undeserving, the soft, and anyone who thought training was going unusually well. The Fang and the Bái Láng ¶ The Fang of Xuán Ji were ennobled before Leonia existed. Their patriarch traditionally bore the title Gong , or Duke. During the first great infernal incursion, the Fang lands were overwhelmed until the neighboring Bái Láng , or “White Wolves,” came to their aid. The Bái Láng are yaoguài : natural shapeshifters with human, animal, and hybrid forms. They are not lycanthropes, do not spread their nature through bites, and are no more beholden to the moon than an ordinary wolf. Fang and Bái Láng families later intermarried, producing bloodlines touched by shapeshifting magic. That union was once considered holy. As Mian society became more urban and distant from the old spirits, mixed-blood Fang fell in social standing and were often treated as wild, unreliable, or “impure.” Many moved away from major settlements and worked as hunters, trappers, fishers, and farmers. The prejudice remains part of Mian Lung's history—and, in some places, its present. Faith and the Deep Places ¶ Beneath the foothills of Xuán Ji lie caves and hidden temples associated with the Mógu Chóng Bài , the “Cult of the Fungus.” Its spore druids protect underground places and preserve traditions overlooked by the growing city-states. The Mógu are neither a single cheerful mushroom club nor a single sinister cult. Like most religious communities, they include teachers, guardians, mystics, zealots, and at least one person who has made the meeting unnecessarily complicated. Fang Ro and Black Chao ¶ Fang Ro , also called Seiqua , was born in Xuán Ji to Tengfei and Lian. Descended from both Fang and Bái Láng bloodlines, she learned wilderness skills from her fisherman and trapper father, trained with the Mógu Chóng Bài, and later became a jiàn shèng in the Mian army. An infernal attack led by Ulysses Vex destroyed her village and killed her family. Fang Ro survived, but Vex severed her tongue with the hell-forged blade Gloomfire. Her pursuit of Vex eventually carried her away from Mian Lung and into the party's adventures. Black Chao is a Mian infantry leader and commander of the Night Tigers. He lost his left eye during the same campaign and survived to rebuild the company around its remaining veterans. Chao considers Fang Ro a little sister and sometimes calls her Heise Ro , or “Black Ro,” as a sign of kinship—even when disagreeing loudly with nearly every decision she makes. General Wei Shen , currently Leonia's Master of the Muster, is also Mian-born and remains deeply respected among the province's soldiers and veterans. Mian Lung Beyond the Province ¶ Generations of Mian merchants, sailors, artisans, soldiers, and laborers have settled elsewhere in Leonia. Their most visible community is Xiaolong , the “Little Dragon” district of Armskirk . Xiaolong's lantern festivals, tea houses, martial schools, bathhouses, herbalists, shrines, import halls, and food stalls make it a cultural bridge between Mian Lung and the Free Cities. Residents often consider themselves fully Leonian and proudly Mian, demonstrating that identity can do two things at once even when government paperwork cannot.

docs.text: The Pink Pony Inn ¶ Menu & House Guide ¶ The Pink Pony is a bardcore tavern, cabaret, and inn where a spaghetti western collided with a gay furry revue and ordered another round. Rose lanterns, swinging doors, live music, curtained booths, and dramatic performers make it one of Armskirk's finest places to draw attention without drawing steel. The house welcomes travelers, performers, queer locals, shifters, adventurers, and anyone prepared to respect the other guests, tip the talent, and make poor decisions entertainingly. Your Hosts ¶ Madam Maeve Mane — Proprietor: An impeccably dressed mare shifter and retired stage hostess. Maeve handles bookings, payroll, booth assignments, and the quiet removal of patrons who confuse hospitality with ownership. Butch Glassidy — Head Bartender: A broad bison shifter with polished horns, rolled sleeves, and the fastest pour in Armskirk's west end. Butch remembers every tab and can end an argument by serving the correct drink before anyone remembers ordering. The House Band & Performers: A rotating company of feline ribbon dancers, lupine stompers, avian aerialists, visiting musicians, and enthusiastic amateurs. They accept applause, coin, flowers, and useful gossip. Familiar Faces ¶ Clint Wetwood: An openly gay otter-shifter guide, owner of Wetwood's Brokeback Outfitters, enthusiastic Pink Pony regular, and full-time argument against subtlety. He is not technically one of the dancers. This distinction weakens as the evening continues. Deep Snoat: A discreet information broker associated with one of the curtained booths. Calling Snoat a gossip is like calling a crossbow a pointed suggestion. Appointments are not guaranteed, advertised, or improved by shouting. docs.text: Plasma Cutter of Limb Severance ¶ Archive audit notice: This handout was released before Session 077 and may contain older mechanics, names, links, or lore phrasing that still needs review. The table's latest ruling is authoritative. Owner: Caracas Weapon (ranged), uncommon (requires attunement) This ranged weapon, modeled after the plasma cutter from Dead Space, is designed for precision targeting of limbs. Damage: 1d8 radiant Properties: Range (40/120), ammunition (battery, 30 shots), light, two-handed Limb Targeting: When you make an attack with this weapon, you can choose to target a limb (arm, leg, wing, etc.) of a creature that has them. You have a -2 penalty to the attack roll, but on a hit, the attack deals an additional 1d4 radiant damage. Severing Beam: On a critical hit against a limb, the limb is severed if it is a type that can be severed, causing additional effects at the DM's discretion (like reduced movement speed for a severed leg). Battery: The weapon has 30 shots before its battery needs to be recharged or replaced. This weapon offers a unique tactical advantage, allowing characters to disable foes effectively at range.
docs.title: Caracas — Plasma Cutter of Limb Severance

docs.text: Republic of Leonia ¶ Type: Nation Government: Federal democracy Founding cities: Armskirk , Torath, and Corvos Province: Mian Lung Current capital: Armskirk Head of government: Ringleader Lincohn Abraham National symbol: The lion The Republic of Leonia lies in the far east of Suvaria. It is the youngest nation on the continent, although Leonian officials have already produced enough speeches, statues, and commemorative mugs to make it feel much older. Leonia did not exist before the alliance of Armskirk, Torath, and Corvos. About two centuries ago, the three sovereign free cities created a mutual-protection pact. That alliance gradually grew into shared laws, trade agreements, public institutions, and—after what historians politely call several energetic disagreements —the federal Republic of Leonia. The founding cities were fiercely independent and had no interest in trading three local rulers for one distant monarch. The republic was therefore built to preserve local identity while giving the cities a common defense and national government. Leonian politics has been arguing over where local freedom ends and federal authority begins ever since. Most citizens consider the arguing an essential public service. The Three Free Cities and Mian Lung ¶ Each city keeps its own customs and civic identity while participating in the government of the republic. Armskirk sits on the northwestern coast of Leonia's eastern peninsula. It is the current capital: a rain-polished city of government halls, markets, theaters, rail traffic, and confident public opinions. Torath is a mountain city of rail yards, arenas, performance halls, strong cheese, and the serene conviction that everyone else is pronouncing it wrong. Corvos is a coastal city of shipyards, lighthouses, aqueducts, and patient negotiators who consider silence a complete counteroffer. Mian Lung is an older eastern realm that remained separate when Leonia was founded. It later entered a mutual-defense treaty with the republic and became a full province roughly one hundred years ago while retaining a Chancellor and many local institutions. The national capital rotates among the three founding cities every twenty years. Mian Lung participates in the republic but is not part of the capital rotation. Armskirk currently has the privilege, responsibility, and municipal headache of hosting it. Government ¶ Leonian politics borrows its titles from the circus. This is not because government is a joke. It is because Leonians believe power should perform in public, face the crowd, and occasionally be pelted with fruit. The Ringleader is the republic's elected head of government. A Ringleader serves one five-year term and cannot immediately stand for another. The Barker Circle is the executive council. Its members administer the republic and explain its decisions to the public—sometimes in that order. The Jugglers oversee taxes, tariffs, budgets, and trade. They insist the name refers to balancing competing needs, not making public money disappear. The Stagehands oversee roads, rail, civic construction, and other public works. When everything functions, nobody sees them. When it does not, everybody suddenly becomes an engineer. The Audience is the citizen body from which the government draws its legitimacy. Citizens vote, petition, attend debates, cheer, heckle, and maintain the sacred democratic right to complain about the results. The Hall of Accord in Armskirk currently houses the national government. Its public chambers resemble an amphitheater more than a throne room: circular stages, packed galleries, speaking horns, banners, and enough acoustics to make a minor procedural objection sound like a declaration of war. Current Leadership ¶ Office Holder Public responsibility Ringleader Lincohn Abraham Head of government and defender of the republic's charter Vice-Ringleader Andruw Junction Administration, logistics, and coordination among the cities Master of the Muster General Wei Shen Defense, militias, emergency response, and Trials security Keeper of the Charter Magister Pica Draft Laws, records, archives, and official decrees Voice of the Republic Dolly Mannerly Ceremonies, public announcements, and civic messaging High Juggler Benny Frankquill Taxes, tariffs, budgets, treasury, and trade policy Chancellor of Mian Lung Jack E. Chan Provincial government and Mian representation before the Ringleader The Chancellor occupies Mian Lung's separate Jade Seat , not a seventh place in the Barker Circle. The seat carries a binding vote when national decisions alter the province's levies, military deployments, treaty rights, or the Jade-Lion Concord; otherwise the Chancellor advises the government with all the authority of a very old treaty and an extremely heavy binder. Ringleader Abraham has reached his term limit and is stepping down rather than seeking a way around it. In Leonia, voluntarily leaving office is considered either the highest form of civic virtue or proof that someone has finally read all the paperwork. The Trials of the Three Cities ¶ Every five years, Leonia chooses its next Ringleader through the Trials of the Three Cities . The Trials combine ritual competition, public spectacle, political campaigning, and civic judgment. Teams put forward a candidate for Ringleader and compete before the Audience. The exact sequence, scoring, and oldest rites are intentionally secretive. Some challenges test strength or skill; others test judgment, persuasion, teamwork, or the ability to remain dignified while the entire republic watches. Officials reveal rules when tradition requires it, which is a ceremonial way of saying at the last possible moment . The current Trials opened in Armskirk with a spectacular Super Clash Bros competition. The surviving teams now advance toward a public debate. Beyond that, contestants receive the same reassuring guidance given to generations before them: prepare for anything, trust the judges, and sign the waiver. The War of Broken Chains ¶ Twenty-five years ago, neighboring Mycoterra was still the Confederated Cap States : thirteen slaveholding states ruled from Richmire by vampire aristocrats. Their laws called slavery Royal Bond Service and sold feeding rights alongside labor contracts. This improved neither the slavery nor the vampires, although it produced considerably more paperwork. Enslaved Mycoterrans and abolitionists built their own liberation movement. Harriet Tubers guided families through the Underground Pipeway , Frederick Sporeglass rallied the country through speeches and newspapers, Ulysses S. Grantoad commanded the Army of the Free Caps, and William Tecumseh Shrooman broke Confederate supply lines during the March to the Green Sea. Young Leonian Lincohn Abraham joined the rebellion as a vampire hunter, wielding his silver-edged axe The Railsplitter against officers who treated death as a brief scheduling conflict. Mian Lung 's Jade Lantern Relief Company carried healers and engineers into the war, and its soldiers' water drums famously summoned Deuce Leem , guardian of Xuán Ji, at Eclipse Ford. The fighting passed through Fort Shroomter, Gettyspore, the Thwomp Trenches, and Eclipse Ford before Operation Breaking Dawn brought down Richmire and Blood Regent Toadstool. The new government abolished slavery, established citizenship, protected voting rights, and rebuilt the country as the Sporeign Dominion of Mycoterra . Mycoterrans remain quick to remind foreign admirers that they liberated themselves; Lincohn helped with the unusually persistent vampires. Mycoterra and the Open Ring ¶ The neighboring Sporeign Dominion of Mycoterra spent twenty years rebuilding after overthrowing the slaveholding vampire government that once ruled it. Five years ago, Mycoterra petitioned to become another Leonian province. Ringleader Abraham vetoed admission under the charter's Free Assent Clause after auditors found suspiciously uniform votes, matching council resolutions, and communities that inspectors could not interview privately. Critics call the veto an old soldier's prejudice; supporters call unanimous politics a contradiction wearing a very cheerful hat. This year's Open Ring Accord is the compromise. Mycoterra may sponsor the Redcap Resolutes for one Trials cycle, led by Marshal Marioni—a Mycoterran reformer who earned Leonian citizenship while rebuilding the Corvos floodworks. If Marioni wins, he may become Ringleader, but Mycoterra must still face a separate admission vote. Leonia has therefore addressed a major foreign-policy dispute in its traditional manner: public arguments, elaborate rules, and controlled property damage. Mian Lung and the Eastern Connection ¶ Mian Lung is Fang Ro's homeland, an eastern coastal province whose history predates the republic. Its merchants, craftspeople, immigrants, and soldiers have shaped Leonia for generations. Mian soldiers form the backbone of Leonian armed forces, while trade and migration have made their traditions part of daily life in the Free Cities. Armskirk's Xiaolong District , or “Little Dragon,” is the most visible expression of that relationship. Founded generations ago by people from Mian Lung, it remains a center for lantern festivals, tea houses, martial schools, bathhouses, artisans, imported goods, and food worth missing a train for. Fang Ro served among Mian Lung's warriors before traveling with the party. General Wei Shen and Black Chao also hail from Mian Lung, and their reputations carry considerable weight among soldiers and veterans in Leonia. Mian Lung is presently facing a wave of fires and disappearances blamed on the Jǐn Bào , or “Golden Leopards,” whose leader Master Zhaoyan preaches purity through flame. Fang Ro has returned home to confront the crisis while Black Chao travels with the party. The Golden Leopards' ultimate purpose remains unknown. Recent History ¶ The original Leonian pact was forged by Armskirk, Torath, and Corvos about two hundred years ago. Mian Lung was not a founding member. After the republic already existed, the independent Jade Kingdom signed a separate mutual-defense treaty with Leonia and remained a sovereign treaty partner for generations. Roughly one hundred years ago, the Jade-Lion Concord made Mian Lung a full province of Leonia. The Concord preserved the office of Chancellor and a place for Mian Lung in national government while formalizing military, tax, and food obligations. The fact that everyone still argues about which side gave up more is considered proof of a balanced treaty. The Lion Line, a recent joint rail venture with Tinkertown and EARS, has strengthened trade and travel between the republic's cities without turning Leonia into “the railroad nation”—a distinction its tourism office makes with surprising frequency. The capital rotates Corvos → Torath → Armskirk , then repeats; each move loses at least one ministry and several good chairs. Famous former Ringleaders include Louie the Fourteenth-Time , who built fourteen fountains and one working sewer; Vicky Regina , who wore black and doubled the national tea budget; and Otto von Biscuit , who unified the tariff code through pastries and threats.

docs.text: Subject: 🧭 The Seek Allies Arc Begins – Four Roads, One Destiny Archive audit notice: This handout was released before Session 077 and may contain older mechanics, names, links, or lore phrasing that still needs review. The table's latest ruling is authoritative. Greetings, Adventurers! Tinkertown breathes again, but the world beyond its steam-belching rails is far from still. The Eternal Engine is turning—but it won’t turn the tide alone. The Council of Chaos —an ancient pact of Suvaria’s darkest powers—has begun to stir. Whether they see you as a threat… or a pawn… remains unclear. But the ground beneath your boots is shifting. It’s time to Seek Allies. Near the start of the next session, you’ll choose your destination. Each path opens new possibilities—and carries its own risks. 🧁 1. King Curry’s Hidden Truths ¶ Aunt Jill Cookie , and the women and children of King Curry’s warren, were taken to a forced labor camp in the Yundabad Mountains , near the orc city of Cheddud Bha . Curry knows where—but not what’s being built. “It hums like thunder and eats the sky.” To reach it, you’ll cross lands where Sauron’s name is law , and shadows walk in daylight. Crude maps and escape routes scratched on old parchment Rumors of a fortress so large it blots out the sun A single warning: “Not even the shadows come back from that place.” 🧙‍♀️ 2. Invitation to Hügsnorts ¶ A bat-winged cat wearing a monocle delivers a glittering letter: “You are hereby invited to tea, tutelage, and perhaps a touch of destiny.” The School of Hexcraft & Hubbub has summoned Amaryllis . The drifting city of Brithombar hides behind layers of illusion—neutral in every war, or so they claim. But something hums beneath the stillness… like magic waiting to snap. The invitation won’t stop twitching A note on the back: “Don’t trust the headmaster’s reflection.” A chance to learn what others are preparing for—or hiding from 🔥 3. Fires in Ming Lung ¶ Fang Ro’s homeland burns again. A new order—the Jǐn Bào , or “Golden Leopards” —claims to bring balance through flame. Their leader, Master Zhaoyan , preaches purity and obedience to the fire. Villages vanish. Temples fall silent. The Mógu Chóng Bài have gone into hiding. But Fang has heard this rhetoric before—beneath screams and smoke. She ended it once… or thought she did. A scroll sealed in red wax bears Fang’s name in Infernal Refugees speak of feline shadows prowling rooftops at dawn The rivers of Mian Lung now run black with ash 🏯 4. The Trials of the Three Cities ¶ Every five years, the Republic of Leonia in the far east holds a ritual competition to choose the next Ringleader . That time has come. But something feels different this year. Relics stir beneath the arenas. Prophecies resurface. And some whisper the Council’s influence has already reached the Free Cities. The competition is being held in Armskirk this time. An old ally, Kardarsha the Kajiit , can get you inside the trials One challenge is called “The Walk Between Flames” —no one agrees what it means The winner shapes the cities’ future. The losers may not leave at all 🧭 Choose Your Path ¶ Each road could earn you allies—or make new enemies. The Council of Chaos is no longer watching from afar. They are moving. So must you. See you at the table, — Your DM Blake

docs.text: Signet of the Fallen Nine ¶ Archive audit notice: This handout was released before Session 077 and may contain older mechanics, names, links, or lore phrasing that still needs review. The table's latest ruling is authoritative. Wondrous item (ring), very rare (requires attunement by a non-good spellcaster; cursed) Provenance ¶ This signet is a lesser work of shadow—neither one of the Nine nor a Ring of Power in its own right, but forged to harmonize with them . Smiths loyal to the Dark Lord cast it in the fumes of Orodruin’s fires, quenching the band in the chill of Morgul water and setting a black glass gem cut from the same volcanic obsidian used to edge Morgul blades. In ages past, Khamûl the Easterling bore rings that answered the will of the One; this signet remembers that cadence. It is a tuning fork for wraithdom , designed to steady death magic, reveal the half-seen, and—over days—pull its wearer across the veil. Appearance ¶ A lean, iron-dark band with hammered facets that never reflect warmth. The inner rim bears hair-fine gouges like teeth marks ; under moonlight they crawl into legible sigils The stone is a lens of night. Stare long enough and you’ll notice pin-prick lights moving far beneath , as if watching you back. The Temptation of Power ¶ The ring grows stronger the longer it is worn continuously (attuned and on your person). Stage I — Dormant: Immediately on attunement. Stage II — Stirring: After 3 consecutive days worn. Stage III — Ascendant: After 7 consecutive days worn. If you remove the ring for 24 hours or receive remove curse , drop one stage (min I). Favor of the Eye (Doing Sauron’s Bidding) ¶ When you complete a task Sauron explicitly commands through the ring (DM adjudicates), you may claim his Favor within 24 hours: - Instantly set the ring to Stage III (Ascendant) for 24 hours. - Boon: Until the next day, the undead you control have advantage on their first attack each combat and you may cast Danse Macabre and Shadow of Moil without using a spell slot. Shared Properties (All Stages) ¶ Shadow Anchor (1/long rest). Reaction when you take damage: you may move up to 10 feet , then become Shadowform until the start of your next turn— you can move through creatures/objects as difficult terrain and have resistance to all damage except radiant and force . While in Shadowform you can’t cast spells, make attacks, or take reactions . If you end inside an object, take 1d10 force and are shunted to the nearest space. Sacred Bane. You have vulnerability to radiant . While on holy ground (e.g., hallow ), you have disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks . Stage I — Dormant ¶ Necromantic Aptitude I. +1 to spell attack rolls and damage with necromancy. Undead you control gain +1 to attack and damage rolls . Veil-Piercer I. Your darkvision increases by 30 ft. , and you can see through magical darkness . The Voice Whispers. Sauron can whisper to you —short, unmistakable messages the DM may deliver at any time (no action, any distance/plane). Stage II — Stirring ¶ (Includes Stage I benefits unless replaced.) - Necromantic Aptitude II. +2 to spell attack rolls and damage with necromancy. Undead you control gain +2 to attack and damage rolls . - Veil-Piercer II. While in dim light or darkness , you have see invisibility . - Grave Tether. When a creature drops to 0 HP from a necromancy spell you cast, gain temporary HP equal to your level/2 (once per turn, rounded up). - The Eye Turns. Sauron knows your general location (direction and within a few miles) while you wear the ring. - Taint of Shadow. You have disadvantage on Persuasion checks against good-aligned creatures and exude a faint, unsettling chill. Stage III — Ascendant ¶ (Includes Stage II benefits unless replaced.) - Necromantic Aptitude III. +3 to spell attack rolls and damage with necromancy. Undead you control gain +3 to attack and damage rolls . - Veil-Piercer III. Constant see invisibility ; in dim light/darkness you also gain blindsight 10 ft. - Wraith’s Command (1/short rest). Reaction: When a creature dies within 60 ft. , you may raise it as a Wight under your control for 10 minutes . It acts immediately after your turn, can’t create spawn , and counts against any control limits. When the duration ends, it crumbles to ash. - Sunlight Sensitivity. In direct sunlight, you have disadvantage on attack rolls and on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight. - The Hand Commands (Geas of the Nine). After completing a long rest while wearing the ring, make a DC 21 Wisdom saving throw . On a failure, you cannot remove the ring and you are affected by geas (no further save) until the next day with a command delivered through the ring. Every hour you directly disobey the command, you take 2d10 psychic damage , and the DM may impose disadvantage on saves vs. charm and fear until your next dawn. The effect ends early if you complete the command, or the ring is targeted by remove curse cast with a 7th-level slot or higher.

docs.text: ✈️ Skyhook Maneuver Gear ¶ Archive audit notice: This handout was released before Session 077 and may contain older mechanics, names, links, or lore phrasing that still needs review. The table's latest ruling is authoritative. Wondrous Item, Rare (requires attunement; can only be worn with Light Armor or no armor) 📝 Description: ¶ This sleek, gnomish-designed harness is crafted from polished brass fittings, sturdy leather straps, and compact steam pistons. Twin grappling hooks rest snugly in side-mounted holsters, attached to durable, clockwork-reinforced cables. ⚙️ Features: ¶ Vertical Grapple (Movement Action) : You fire a grappling hook up to 60 feet toward a solid surface, large object, or creature. You instantly pull yourself to that point or swing freely. Requires an Acrobatics or Athletics check (DC 13/8) to successfully maneuver. Boost Jets (Bonus Action; 3/Day) : Activate short-burst steam jets for an immediate 20-foot burst of speed . As part of this movement, you may make one melee attack with advantage . All three charges replenish after completing a long rest . Limited Steam Fuel : After every 10 uses of Vertical Grapple , the Skyhook Gear must be recharged. Spend 10 minutes refueling and maintaining the gear with basic supplies to restore its functionality. 🚨 Skyhook Mishap Table: ¶ When you fail an Acrobatics or Athletics check using Vertical Grapple , roll a d6 to determine the malfunction: d6 Mishap Result 1–3 Jammed: Gear jams and cannot be used again until the end of your next turn. 4–5 Misfire: You fall prone, but only lose the movement required to stand up again. 6 Tangled Cables: Your movement speed is reduced to zero until your turn ends as you untangle cables. 🎖️ Special Note for Fang Ro (Monk Character): ¶ Given Fang Ro's exceptional agility and speed as a Monk, the Skyhook Maneuver Gear complements and amplifies your natural mobility, enabling dramatic aerial combat, swift repositioning, and daring escapes. This gear aligns seamlessly with your playstyle, allowing rapid access to high vantage points and agile engagement in battle. Pratice makes perfect: After 3 days of dedicated practice, Fang Ro permanently reduces the Acrobatics DC for Vertical Grapple from 13 to 8 .

docs.text: Staff of Whispers of the Dark Lord ¶ Archive audit notice: This handout was released before Session 077 and may contain older mechanics, names, links, or lore phrasing that still needs review. The table's latest ruling is authoritative. Wondrous item (staff), legendary (requires attunement by a spellcaster) Appearance ¶ A gnarled blackwood shaft crowned by a dull, smoky crystal that seems to swallow light. Soft, sibilant whispers drift from its runes when you hold it. Faint spectral tendrils coil around the shaft, pulsing with each hushed word. Lore ¶ Forged deep beneath the dark spires of a forgotten fortress, the Staff of Whispers of the Dark Lord was born of both necromancy and treachery. Crafted by a sorcerer whose name was struck from history, the staff served as a vessel for imprisoning the soul of Gríma Wormtongue—a servant whose voice once toppled kings without ever raising a blade. Twisting in death as he did in life, Wormtongue’s spirit became bound to the staff’s smoky crystal, doomed to forever echo his master's will. Wherever the staff goes, so too does the breath of the Dark Lord, for it carries his voice to any who dare to listen.. Bound by foul magic, Wormtongue’s essence now writhes within the crystal, forever whispering Sauron’s will to any who dare wield it. Sentience ¶ Intelligence 12 | Wisdom 14 | Charisma 16 Alignment: Lawful Evil Personality: Duplicitous and sycophantic, its voice slithers into the wielder’s mind, promising power in return for loyalty to Sauron. Communication: Telepathic whispers in Common or Undercommon, audible only to the wielder. Properties while Attuned ¶ +1 bonus to spell attack rolls and to the saving-throw DCs of your spells. Umbral Rift (Recharge 6): As a bonus action, you may meld into a shadow or dim light, becoming invisible and intangible, then reappear from another shadow or dim light within 60 ft. As part of this movement, you leave behind a silent shadowy illusion of yourself at your point of origin. This decoy lasts until the start of your next turn. Creatures attempting to target you must succeed on a Wisdom (Perception) check against your spell save DC. On a failure, they mistakenly target the decoy, which vanishes harmlessly. Cloak of Flickering Gloom: While in dim light or darkness, you have advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks. Spell Usage (1/day each, cast at base level) ¶ You may cast each of the following spells once per day using your spellcasting modifier. Use the checkboxes to track usage. All extra spells cast using the Staff of Whispers require a somatic component , even if the spell normally does not. 1st Level - [ ] _Command - [ ] _Charm Person - [ ] _Dissonant Whispers 2nd Level [ ] _Enthrall [ ] _Suggestion [ ] _Gift for Gab 3rd Level - [ ] _Fear - [ ] _Enemies Abound - [ ] _Incite Greed Rewards for Obedience ¶ The staff hungers not only for loyalty, but for proof. If you commit vile acts at its urging—such as betraying your allies, defiling sacred sites, or murdering innocents—the staff rewards you by unlocking deeper powers. These spells are granted permanently once the required number of major evil deeds are completed. Use at your own peril. Deed-Based Spell Unlocks ¶ After 1st Major Deed Shadow of Moil , Compulsion (cast at base level, 1/day each) After 2nd Major Deed Synaptic Static , Geas (cast at base level, 1/day each) After 3rd Major Deed Otto’s Irresistible Dance , Mass Suggestion (cast at base level, 1/day each) These spells become available only if the staff deems your actions sufficiently evil. The DM determines if an act qualifies. The staff’s whispers may tempt, but the choices—and consequences—are yours. (May cause alignment shift and deity changes) Bond with the Dark Lord ¶ Sauron is always aware of the staff’s general location (within a mile) and its “mood” (calm, restless, hungry) unless the staff is warded by nondetection or similar divination-blocking magic. Through this bond, the staff can convey simple concepts back to Sauron—alerts, questions, or brief commands—as if feeling the pulse of its own malevolent will. Curse of Wormtongue’s Bond ¶ Attunement to the staff begins the moment a creature touches it. Upon first contact, the staff whispers directly into the mind of the holder, inviting them to claim its power. If the creature fails a DC 24 Wisdom saving throw the attunement process completes instantly, binding the two together. The staff can only be attuned to one creature at a time. It may choose to end its attunement to the current wielder at any time, removing all ill effects—though the former wielder is left with a vague, hollow desire to steal it back. Dark Obsession: At the end of each long rest, you must succeed on a DC 24 Wisdom saving throw or become obsessed until your next long rest ends. While obsessed: You will not allow anyone to attempt to destroy the staff. While weilding the staff you must use both hands. You cannot willingly let the staff leave your possession; if separated, you automatically use your movement on your next turn to retrieve it. Ally Protection: When you attempt to harm (including status effects) an ally or creature the staff “protects,” you must succeed on a DC 15 Wisdom saving throw. On a failure, the attack or harmful spell fizzles. If you fail three DC 15 Wisdom or Charisma saves against the staff's whispers in a single day, the staff’s intelligence silently casts suggestion on you (self‑only, 1‑hour duration) with no saving throw to resist. The wielder cannot willingly break or end attunement on their own; another creature must perform the curse-breaking magic. docs.text: A gnarled blackwood shaft crowned by a dull, smoky crystal that seems to swallow light. Soft, sibilant whispers drift from its runes when you hold it. Faint spectral tendrils coil around the shaft, pulsing with each hushed word.
docs.title: Appearance

docs.text: Forged deep beneath the dark spires of a forgotten fortress, the Staff of Whispers of the Dark Lord was born of both necromancy and treachery. Crafted by a sorcerer whose name was struck from history, the staff served as a vessel for imprisoning the soul of Gríma Wormtongue—a servant whose voice once toppled kings without ever raising a blade. Twisting in death as he did in life, Wormtongue’s spirit became bound to the staff’s smoky crystal, doomed to forever echo his master's will. Wherever the staff goes, so too does the breath of the Dark Lord, for it carries his voice to any who dare to listen.. Bound by foul magic, Wormtongue’s essence now writhes within the crystal, forever whispering Sauron’s will to any who dare wield it.
docs.title: Lore

docs.text: Intelligence 12 | Wisdom 14 | Charisma 16 Alignment: Lawful Evil Personality: Duplicitous and sycophantic, its voice slithers into the wielder’s mind, promising power in return for loyalty to Sauron. docs.text: +1 bonus to spell attack rolls and to the saving-throw DCs of your spells. Umbral Rift (Recharge 6): As a bonus action, you may meld into a shadow or dim light, becoming invisible and intangible, then reappear from another shadow or dim light within 60 ft. As part of this movement, you leave behind a silent shadowy illusion of yourself at your point of origin. This decoy lasts until the start of your next turn. Creatures attempting to target you must succeed on a Wisdom (Perception) check against your spell save DC. On a failure, they mistakenly target the decoy, which vanishes harmlessly. Cloak of Flickering Gloom: While in dim light or darkness, you have advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks.

docs.text: The staff hungers not only for loyalty, but for proof. If you commit vile acts at its urging—such as betraying your allies, defiling sacred sites, or murdering innocents—the staff rewards you by unlocking deeper powers. These spells are granted permanently once the required number of major evil deeds are completed. Use at your own peril.

docs.text: Stasis Module Charm ¶ Archive audit notice: This handout was released before Session 077 and may contain older mechanics, names, links, or lore phrasing that still needs review. The table's latest ruling is authoritative. Owner: Bellafronte Dupree “Bells” Wondrous item, uncommon (requires attunement) The Stasis Module Charm, inspired by the Stasis Module from Dead Space, is a small device that can momentarily slow time around a specific target. Charges: It holds 3 charges and regains 1d3 expended charges daily at dawn. Usage: As a reaction, you can expend one charge to cast the Slow spell (save DC 15) on a single target within 60 feet, without requiring concentration. The effect lasts the targets next turn. Flavor: The charm emits a brief blue light and a low hum when activated, and the targeted creature appears to move in slow motion. This item brings a tactical advantage, allowing the wielder to hinder a powerful foe or control the battlefield's tempo.

docs.text: Festival Schedule ¶ Archive audit notice: This handout was released before Session 077 and may contain older mechanics, names, links, or lore phrasing that still needs review. The table's latest ruling is authoritative. Talent Show (Rap Battle While Wrapping Presents) Igloo Building Contest Audience Participation Musical (feat. Vocal Vance) Tomorrow World Invention Displays Gnomish Opera Cheer Meister Vote Hanging Gems off the Clocktower & Founding of Tinkertown Story Detailed Festival Events ¶ Below are expanded descriptions for Events 2–8, complete with skill checks , funny/punny moments , and scene-setting vignettes. Tinkertown’s colorful citizens all play a part, and you’ll find plenty of ways to engage your Level 11 party in DnD 5e. 2. Talent Show: “Rap & Wrap” Battle ¶ Location : A makeshift stage near Brews and Blues . Garland and giant candy canes decorate the platform, and a modest crowd of gnomes and dwarves eagerly awaits the show. Scene Setting ¶ Paper streamers float on the evening breeze, and holiday lights cast dancing patterns on the stage. A tiny gnome in peppermint-striped pants steps up to the mic, adjusting his candy-cane microphone. “Step right up, fold that paper tight, spit your rhymes—show your holiday might! We’re about to rap while we wrap, If you flop, watch your gifts unwrap!”* Mechanics & Skill Checks ¶ Contestants must rap (Performance check, CHA-based) and wrap (Sleight of Hand or simple DEX-based) simultaneously. Base DC 14 for moderate success. DC 18+ yields a big crowd reaction and a small prize (e.g., a Potion of MistleToe which makes your breath smell like peppermint for 24 hours, or a handful of special cookies from Munster Mart ). Rap Lines Examples ¶ “I’m a gift-wrappin’ wizard, yo you betta believe, Twistin’ bows, droppin’ flows, got a trick up my sleeve. I’ll box this present tight like a gnome in a crate, Keep your eyes on me, ‘cuz I’m the illest in the state!” “Tape, tape, tape—gonna stick it in place, Ribbon so bright, it lights up the space. My bars so cold, I’m chillin’ the beat, While my paper corners sharper than a blacksmith’s heat!” A Tinkertown local, wearing a tinsel chain, waves the crowd to chant along, “Wrap it, rap it, wrap it, rap it!” 3. Igloo Building Contest ¶ Location : A fenced-off snowy yard just past Francis’s Furniture . Huge blocks of packed snow are piled high, along with gnomish ice saws that hum with faint mechanical energy. Scene Setting ¶ Chunks of fresh snow glisten in the winter sun. Gnomes in thick mittens dart between snow piles, shaping frosty bricks with weirdly advanced ice saws. The air resonates with crisp frost and echoing laughter. Mechanics & Skill Checks ¶ Strength (Athletics) DC 15 to carve or haul large snow blocks. Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) DC 15 to fashion precise snow bricks or decorate edges. Arcana or Tinker’s Tools (DC 15) for magical details (e.g., color-shifting icicles or functional snow doors). Notable Competitors ¶ Gnomer Simpson attempts to help. He frequently ends up napping inside half-built igloos. “Mmm… donut Igloo.” Miss Gnomer of the Tinkertown Times snaps pictures, threatening to print embarrassing fails on the front page. Winning Prize : - A satirical “ Igloo’d to Perfection ” ribbon—shaped like an upside-down ice cube. - Some frozen cheddar bites from Munster Mart as a comedic snack. 4. Audience Participation Musical feat. Vocal Vance ¶ Location : A cozy corner stage behind Dresselmeyer’s Emporium . Vocal Vance: The “Weird Al”-Style Accordion Singer ¶ He’s a flamboyant gnome with an accordion bedazzled in LED lights. Sings parodies of popular Tinkertown tunes—“ Teeny Cog Rhapsody ,” “ Like a Gnome Stone ,” etc. Scene Setting ¶ A hush falls as a spotlight illuminates Vance, decked in polka-dotted robes. The clack of his accordion resounds, bouncing off the glistening cogs overhead. “Allow me to polka your fancy!” he cries, before launching into an outrageous parody ballad about misfired inventions. Audience Participation ¶ Vance invites volunteers to wave glowing wands (Minor Illusion wands) and sing backup vocals. Performance (CHA) DC 12 for a decent showing. If a PC wants a star cameo, they can do a short comedic duet with Vance (DC 15). If successful, participants get showered with confetti and a cameo mention in Vance’s next “GnomeTube” performance. 5. Tomorrow World Invention Displays (Hosted by Pat Pat) ¶ Location : An open-air expo area near Pat Pat’s Patent Office train car. Setting & Flavor ¶ Crowds cluster around makeshift stands displaying half-finished gadgets and cunning contraptions. The aroma of burning metal wafts from a corner where a gnome vigorously polishes clockwork wings. Pat Pat, sporting a flamboyant bowler hat and a wide grin, calls out: “Got an idea? Register it with Pat Pat—where your invention meets its future!” Pat Pat’s Bulletin Board ¶ Showcases the “ Idea of the Week ”: Calvin Cookie’s Cookie Gun. Everyone’s abuzz with talk of “edible ammo” and “dessert-based deterrence.” Displays ¶ Hover-Hat Helios A metallic top hat with mini-propellers. Demonstrator claims it can levitate the user up to 10 ft for short durations. But a DC 14 Arcana check reveals frequent engine sputters… Thermal Coil Boots Self-heating footwear. DC 12 Investigation check to note they overheat occasionally, scorching floors. Squeakless Dynamo A “silent” generator that ironically makes more noise than a standard one. Cog-to-Go Portable Kitchen A foldout stove with multiple gear-driven attachments—chopping, stirring, etc. Ideal for dwarven feasts on the go. Optional Skill Checks - Intelligence (Investigation or Tinker’s Tools) DC 14 to grasp how each invention works. - PCs can pitch their own invention to Pat Pat for comedic effect or potential future plot hooks. 6. Gnomish Opera ¶ Location : A modestly grand but temporary Opera House car near the Clocktower. Plush seats inside are decorated with swirling gear motifs. Scene Setting ¶ Cascading curtains of velvet shimmer under an array of mechanical chandeliers. Gnome performers in elaborate steampunk costumes take the stage. The score is in “i minor,” an odd tonal key that resonates with arcane undertones. Performance ¶ The Opera weaves a tale of forbidden love between an inventor and a faulty automaton. Dramatic solos include mechanical clanks for percussion. Any PC who wants to cameo as an opera extra can make a Performance (CHA) DC 15 to convincingly hit the notes or gracefully navigate the stage’s trapdoors. “Hold me, my clockwork heart, for I spin with longing in the gloom of parted gears…” The audience dabs away tears at the tragic refrain. 7. Cheer Meister Vote ¶ A nod to How the Grinch Stole Christmas. The Cheer Meister is chosen for their “Holiday Spirit and Great Gusto!” Scene Setting & Mechanics ¶ A public vote by secret ballot (some may bribe or trick the process). The winner receives: The Gaudy Crown of Jubilation – An obnoxious magic crown that glows bright green. Side effect : Once worn, it sporadically amplifies the wearer’s voice at random intervals (DM’s discretion). Coupon Book – Filled with 101 random coupons for Tinkertown shops. Ranges from “Buy 1 Get 1 Half Off” at SoSo Mart to “Free Cheese Sample at Munster Mart” to “One Complimentary Clockwork Carriage Ride” . Skill checks: PCs can attempt Persuasion (CHA) DC 15 or Performance (CHA) DC 15 to rally support for a chosen candidate. Alternatively, Sleight of Hand (DEX) DC 14 could be used for comedic tampering with ballots—though that might get them in trouble. Mayor Cobblebot officiates, exclaiming, “We crown thee, Cheer Meister of Tinkertown!” as the crown’s glow intensifies to near-blinding. A wave of giggles and applause follows the new Cheer Meister’s random voice echo. 8. Hanging Gems off the Clocktower & Founding of Tinkertown Story ¶ Location : The Tinkertown Clocktower stands tall at the center, gear-laden spire visible from across the rolling city. Scene Setting ¶ Soft snow drifts downward as an elder gnome steps forward, carrying a crystalline gem. The flickering lamplights cast shards of color across the crowd. Families hush, eyes locked on the Clocktower’s pinnacle. A hush of reverence falls… Short Founding Story ¶ “A century ago,” begins Ezmirelda Emerald , her voice echoing across the hush, “Our ancestors, the EARS —Experimental Augmentation Research Society—found themselves in Gnormandy, bound by tyrannical rules. Some caved, becoming GEARS , slaves to corporate whim. But others believed in freedom to invent . So they created the first hex track —a repeating runic pattern that let the very ground become our rails. Tinkertown was born from their unwavering spirit. We set off, our homes rolling behind us, forging fresh horizons daily. We learned that true invention blossoms only when unshackled—an idea that no government can chain. To honor that birth, we hang these gems upon the Clocktower, each a symbol of hope, creativity, and unstoppable progress .” At that final word, Ezmirelda climbs a ladder (or a gear-lift), affixes the gem, and a warm glow envelops the tower momentarily. Applause erupts, and a wave of communal pride ripples through Tinkertown. Final Note ¶ While the party won’t have time to attend every event in depth, these expanded scenes give you plenty of roleplay hooks , skill checks , and comedic moments to incorporate. NPCs like Pat Pat, Gnomer Simpson, Ezmirelda Emerald , and others each add their personal flair, so feel free to seed side quests or foreshadow bigger plot points (like the engine theft ) across these festivities. Enjoy the holiday cheer—and keep an eye out for suspicious giant mice lurking in the shadows!
docs.title: Tinkertown Winter Festival Program

docs.text: Soft snow drifts downward as an elder gnome steps forward, carrying a crystalline gem. The flickering lamplights cast shards of color across the crowd. Families hush, eyes locked on the Clocktower’s pinnacle. A hush of reverence falls…
docs.title: Scene Setting

docs.text: “A century ago,” begins Ezmirelda Emerald , her voice echoing across the hush, “Our ancestors, the EARS —Experimental Augmentation Research Society—found themselves in Gnormandy, bound by tyrannical rules. Some caved, becoming GEARS , slaves to corporate whim. But others believed in freedom to invent . So they created the first hex track —a repeating runic pattern that let the very ground become our rails. Tinkertown was born from their unwavering spirit. We set off, our homes rolling behind us, forging fresh horizons daily. We learned that true invention blossoms only when unshackled—an idea that no government can chain. To honor that birth, we hang these gems upon the Clocktower, each a symbol of hope, creativity, and unstoppable progress .” At that final word, Ezmirelda climbs a ladder (or a gear-lift), affixes the gem, and a warm glow envelops the tower momentarily. Applause erupts, and a wave of communal pride ripples through Tinkertown.
docs.title: Short Founding Story

docs.text: While the party won’t have time to attend every event in depth, these expanded scenes give you plenty of roleplay hooks , skill checks , and comedic moments to incorporate. NPCs like Pat Pat, Gnomer Simpson, Ezmirelda Emerald , and others each add their personal flair, so feel free to seed side quests or foreshadow bigger plot points (like the engine theft ) across these festivities. Enjoy the holiday cheer—and keep an eye out for suspicious giant mice lurking in the shadows!
