docs.text: Francis’s Furniture ¶ Archive audit notice: This handout was released before Session 077 and may contain older mechanics, names, links, or lore phrasing that still needs review. The table's latest ruling is authoritative. Nestled in a whimsically oversized train car, Francis’s Furniture is a rainbow jumble of couches, chairs, and cabinets—some plush, some peculiar, all hand-picked by Francis himself. A flamboyant gnome in a paisley vest, Francis prides himself on curating items “fit for the maddest hatters and the most sensible of halflings alike.” You’ll see chairs that float, tables that dance, and ottomans that purr. If you’re seeking the ordinary or the extraordinary, you’ve come to the right place! Non-Magical Furnishings ¶ Item Description Price (gp) Mushroom Ottoman A plush, toadstool-themed footrest. Surprisingly comfy, but otherwise mundane. 15 gp Curious Clockwork Rocker A rocking chair with little whirring gears for decoration. It makes soft ticking sounds in time with your rocking. 30 gp Polka-Dot Pouf A bright cushion for casual seating. Durable, stain-resistant cover. Perfect for any festive corner of your home or workshop. 20 gp Flip-Flap Folding Chair This metal folding chair snaps open and closed with a satisfying “flip-flap.” Sturdy enough for gnomes and dwarves. 10 gp Spiral Stair Shelf A spiral-shaped wooden shelf that’s great for displaying your tinker tools (or small trinkets). 45 gp Laughing Loveseat No actual magic here, but the upholstery is embroidered with smiling faces and bright motifs. Comfortably seats two small folk or one medium-sized visitor. 50 gp Magical Furnishings ¶ Note : All magical furniture items here require attunement only if the item specifically states it (DM’s discretion). Otherwise, they function as described. Item Description Price (gp) Color-Shifting Chaise A plush, fainting-couch style seat that can change its color or pattern with a tap (no action required). Great for dramatic entrances. 150 gp Hopscotch Footstool Once per day, standing on this footstool allows the user to cast Jump on themselves (no components needed). 300 gp Mirror-Mirror Vanity A gilded vanity with a mirror that can cast Minor Illusion (1/day) to perfect your appearance—or distract an unwary foe. 350 gp Dancing Dresser Once per day, as an action, you can speak a command word to animate the dresser for up to 1 hour. It behaves like an Animated Object under your control. 750 gp Chimera Couch A sofa stitched together with various fabrics. Once per long rest, any creature that completes a short rest on it regains an extra 1d6 hit points. 1,000 gp Teleporting Tea Table This dainty table can teleport itself (and anything on it, up to 50 lbs) up to 30 feet once per day, so long as you can see the destination space. 1,200 gp Slumbering Sofa of Solace Attunement Required . Whenever a creature attuned to this sofa completes a long rest on it, they gain the benefit of a Lesser Restoration spell once per day. 1,500 gp Topsy-Turvy Armoire Opening the doors can flip its contents upside-down (harmlessly) once per day. The novelty effect can also impose Disadvantage on Sleight of Hand checks against it. 2,000 gp Necessities and Nuances ¶ Run by Nelly Nimbleneedle , a soft-spoken yet sharp-witted gnome with an eye for detail, Necessities and Nuances is the beating heart of Tinkertown’s daily life. Much like a classic mom-and-pop store, they stock everything from humble hygiene products to experimental potions—just the thing to keep a gnome’s gears running smoothly. Step inside, and you’ll see shelves stacked with everyday must-haves, plus a few extraordinary oddities that could only have been dreamed up in this whimsical, rolling town. Everyday Essentials and Novelties ¶ Item Description Price Tampons (10 pack) Called “Flo-Stop” by locals. Simple, disposable, essential for travelers and townsfolk alike. 5 sp Toilet Paper (1 roll) Soft, cloud-like tissues embossed with subtle gear patterns—because gnomes never forget style. 1 sp Gnome-Grown Shampoo A gentle, floral formula said to keep hair lush and grease-free—especially handy for grease monkey inventors. 2 sp Squeaky-Clean Soap A lavender-scented bar that leaves a faint shimmer on your skin—popular before fancy Tinkertown soirées. 1 sp Gnomish Tooth Powder A small tin of fizzy tooth powder that “scrubs away plaque like a mechanic on a stubborn cog.” 8 cp Clockwork Comb A durable, collapsible comb with tiny, non-magical gears—folds neatly into your pouch. 1 gp Everyday Bandages Simple linen wraps with gear-pattern adhesives. Perfect for minor cuts and scrapes. 5 cp (per roll) “Arcane Aspirin” A mild pain-relief potion. Soothes headaches, minor aches, and that “inventor’s muscle cramp.” 5 gp Antacid Tonic Bubbly brew for easing indigestion (especially after too many cheese experiments at Munster Mart). 3 gp Gnomicilin Ointment A salve akin to antibiotic cream—promotes faster healing of small wounds (1 extra hit point per Short Rest if applied). 10 gp Tabaxi Balm An imported soothing cream for sore muscles—rumored to be from faraway lands. Provides advantage on checks to recover from Exhaustion (1 use). 15 gp Soothe & Snooze Draft A gentle draught that makes you tired and helps clear congestion 8 gp Gear-Etched Journal Blank pages. The cover depicts tiny interlocking cogs. Rumored to occasionally make soft ticking sounds when you write. 5 gp Tinkerbell’s Tissues Box of lightly enchanted tissues that flutter a bit like fairy wings as you pull them out. Good for sneezes or wiping goggles. 5 sp “Gnome Alone” Board Game A comedic puzzle game where you set mechanical traps to catch imaginary intruders—popular at Tinkertown family gatherings. 8 gp Hitchhiker’s Gnome to the Galaxy (Pamphlet) A witty, abridged pamphlet about far-off worlds, emphasizing “Don’t Panic… just Tinker!” 2 gp Magical Miscellany & “Medicinals” ¶ Item Description Price Bubble & Brew Hair Wash A playful shampoo that changes hair color for 24 hours (user’s choice). Great for festivals or disguises. 25 gp Clockwork Vapor Rub Rub on your chest to relieve congestion. When used, tiny clockwork gears spin across your skin, providing a faint mechanical hum that eases breathing for up to 8 hours. 30 gp Restoration Ration A single dose biscuit loaded with vitamins and mild curative magic—restores 1d4+1 HP. Each biscuit is embossed with the E.A.R.S. insignia. Limit 3 per customer per week. 12 gp Gnome ‘n Tonic A mild euphoric brew that grants +1 Charisma checks for 1 hour. Causes mild giggling and hiccups. 50 gp Fairy Flicker Eye Drops Grants Darkvision 30 ft for 1 hour. If the user already has Darkvision, it extends the range by 30 ft. 100 gp Invisibalm A small jar of translucent ointment. Applying it to a single object (up to 1 cubic foot) renders it invisible for 10 minutes or until it’s moved by a living creature. 20 gp Engineheart Elixir A bright red potion that stabilizes a dying creature automatically once within 1 hour of drinking. Popular among Tinkertown’s daredevils. 100 gp Merry Mender Mushrooms Dried mushrooms that, when steeped in hot water for 1 hour, act as a Lesser Restoration spell. Each bag contains enough for 2 servings. 100 gp SoSo Mart ¶ The SoSo Mart chain has spread across the land faster than a flock of griffons on half-price wing night—promising “savings, or so-so they say.” Every location looks the same: a huge warehouse-like interior with bright, garish signage insisting that everything is “Cheaper Here!” Run by the perpetually bland Manager Manny Monotone , this branch in Tinkertown towers over its modest neighbors, complete with a mechanical sliding door that greets you with a tinny “Welcome to SoSo Mart.” They advertise a 20% discount for members , but the membership fees are steep, and the fine print is very fine. Advertising Slogan : “You could pay more elsewhere … but that would be so so silly, wouldn’t it?” Everyday Essentials ¶ Item Description Price SoSo Brand Tampons (10 pack) Basic, no-frills design. Cardboard applicator squeaks sometimes. Often on sale “Buy 2, get the 3rd for 10% off.” 6 sp SoSo Brand Toilet Paper (1 roll) Thin, scratchy, and emblazoned with the SoSo Mart logo. You suspect it’s recycled from rejected magical scrolls. 2 sp SoSo-Fro Shampoo The cheapest shampoo around, known for leaving hair vaguely smelling like old daisies. 3 sp SoSo-Pro Condoms Guaranteed for “Satisfactory” performance. Comes in a plain wrapper with no indication of what they are made from. 1 gp (3 pack) Junk Food: “SoSo Crispies” A bag of suspiciously crunchy “grain puffs” coated in sweet dust. Slight chemical aftertaste. 1 sp per bag Candy: “ChocoGnome Bars” Contains “real cocoa flavor (3%).” Wrapped in bright foil, popular among sugar-craving adventurers on a budget. 5 cp each Energy Drink: “Gnogurt Surge” A vaguely yogurt-flavored fizzy drink. Provides a quick sugar rush—then a sugar crash. 8 cp each SoSo Bandages Low-quality bandages. Peel off easily, offering minimal coverage. 3 cp (per roll) Tinkertown Tourist Tee A cheaply printed shirt with “I <3 Tinkertown” on it. 5 sp Discounted Magical Items ¶ Item Description Price SoSo Brand “Blinking Lantern” A lantern that claims to cast Light (cantrip-level) but flickers unpredictably. 10% chance each hour it extinguishes itself and must be re-lit. 50 gp Mediocre Magical Mop When used to clean, it casts Prestidigitation to slightly freshen an area. However, each use might produce random colors or faint odors for 1 minute. 60 gp Wand of Minor Malfunction This wand should cast Minor Illusion once per day, but there’s a 25% chance it misfires, producing a random comedic effect (DM’s choice). 125 gp Uninspired Umbrella Functions as an Umbrella of Feather Fall (once per day). Has a 20% chance to snap shut mid-descent , causing falling damage for the user. 150 gp SoSo Self-Repair Kit Supposed to cast Mending (cantrip) on small objects 3/day. Often takes five times as long and has a 20% chance of failure, using up a daily charge. 200 gp Mystic Magnifier A monocle that grants Advantage on Investigation checks for 10 minutes, once a day. Sometimes spontaneously fogs up, negating the advantage. 250 gp Hovering Halberd (Damaged) This halberd can levitate itself for 1 minute (1/day). 15% chance it drops out of the air mid-use, possibly landing on your foot (1d4 damage). 300 gp Store Highlights ¶ 20% Discount Membership For a flat 50 gp annual fee, sign a “few” pages of magically binding contract, and all items qualify for the discount. Warning : Breaking membership terms might incur “substantial magical penalties.” Uniformed Staff Manager Manny Monotone lurks near the registers, urging patrons to upgrade to the “Super SoSo Membership.” Staff rarely seem enthusiastic; must be the corporate training. Happy shopping (or so-so shopping)! Remember, at SoSo Mart: “If it ain’t cheap, we’ll make it cheaper… eventually.” Full Metal Racket ¶ Run by Sergeant Ironbeard , a gruff dwarf veteran who paces around the shop barking orders at imaginary recruits, Full Metal Racket is Tinkertown’s one-stop depot for all things armament. Clad in a dented breastplate etched with slogans like “Gnome Mercy,” he firmly believes the town is “always one subterranean ambush away” from total disaster. Though he scoffs at “puny gnome gear,” he grudgingly stocks smaller-sized weapons and armor, too. Step into his cramped train-car workshop, and expect an earful of tough love—and maybe some top-notch arms if you can handle the rant. Mundane Weapons and Armor ¶ Item Description Price Short Sword A standard steel blade favored by gnomes for its manageable size. Sergeant Ironbeard rolls his eyes at its “tiny jab,” but it gets the job done. 10 gp Long Sword Heavy, robust steel for medium-sized creatures. The dwarf calls it “barely adequate.” 15 gp Heavy War Pick 2 handed 1d10, Vicious Weapon: add an extra 1d10 on critcal hit. Sturdy, with a reinforced haft, ideal for splitting rocks or heads. 1 gp Gnomish Spike Trap (kit) A collapsible set of spikes that can be laid on the floor to deter intruders. Covers a 5 ft. square. Ironbeard says “if it’s small, it’s sneaky.” 5 gp Gnomeflint Pistol A rudimentary black-powder firearm with a -1 to attack rolls. Deals 2d12 piercing damage (range 20/40). Requires a full action to reload. Ironbeard calls it a “boomstick for babies.” 120 gp Light Crossbow A reliable range option. Ironbeard says, “If you can’t handle real recoil, at least handle this.” 25 gp Handaxe Perfect for close quarters or throwing. The dwarf uses one to shave his whiskers. 5 gp Padded Armor Basic quilted armor, comfortable but not too protective. Sergeant Ironbeard sneers, “Might as well wear a pillow.” 5 gp Leather Armor Standard light armor, popular among gnome scouts. “Softies,” mutters Ironbeard. 10 gp Chain Shirt Medium armor that clinks and clanks. Gnomes like the partial coverage without the weight—Ironbeard just roars, “Grow a spine!” 50 gp Breastplate A metal front plate offering decent protection. If it’s good enough for the dwarf, it’s good enough for you—though he says, “you’ll never fill it out.” 400 gp Splint Armor Heavy metal plates strapped over chain. Ironbeard’s favorite pre-war style. “Now, this is real armor,” he bellows. 200 gp Gnome Helm A smaller, lightweight steel cap with a flip-down visor that looks like a cog. Ironbeard calls it “that tinker bucket.” 15 gp Magical Weapons & Armor ¶ Item Description Price Sarge’s +2 Battleaxe A dwarven-forged axe etched with Ironbeard’s personal motto: “Born to Brawl.” Grants a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls . 600 gp Tinkershot Muzzleloader (+2) This improved muzzleloader deals +2 to attack and damage rolls . Deals 3d12 piercing damage (range 60/120). Requires a full action to reload. Ironbeard grudgingly admits the gnome-smiths “didn’t screw it up this time.” Comes with a small stabilizing bipod for extra style. 800 gp Drill Sergeant’s “Shock Stick” A +1 spear that, once per combat, can cast Shocking Grasp upon hitting a target (lightning arcs for 1d8 extra damage). “Wake ’em up, soldier!” – Ironbeard. 500 gp Guardian’s Gearplate (+1) A +1 breastplate crafted with intricate gear motifs. Ironbeard calls it “fashion nonsense,” but it’s unexpectedly quiet, giving Advantage on Stealth checks in dimly lit areas. 1,200 gp Tunnelbane Helm A dwarven helm that grants Darkvision 30 ft. (if you already have Darkvision, it extends it by 30 ft). In addition, once per day, you can sense tremors within 30 ft. for 1 minute. 500 gp Gnomeguard Exo-Suit (Half Plate) A half plate lined with hidden springs and cogs. Grants the wearer Advantage on Strength (Athletics) checks to jump or climb . Ironbeard grudgingly calls it “Clever. For a gnome.” 300 gp “Boom Bulwark” Shield A +1 steel shield inscribed with a runic blast symbol. Once per long rest, when you’re hit with a melee attack, you can use a reaction to push the attacker back 10 ft. (Con save negates). 1,000 gp Additional Shop Flavor ¶ Sergeant’s Rants : Expect an earful of “YOU CALL THAT A WEAPON?” whenever you browse anything but the heavy gear. Trench-Safe Guarantee? : Ironbeard claims everything sold here is “battle-tested” …though you might notice some items have never seen real conflict. All Sales Final : Return policy? “War waits for no one, so neither do we!” The Wonderarium ¶ Formerly Fredrick Fizzlebang’s Fireworks , this bright and bustling bazaar is owned by the one and only Fredrick Fizzlebang —a gnome with a spark in his eye and a perpetual wisp of smoke drifting from his rumpled top hat. While Fredrick’s passion for pyrotechnics remains, the rebranded Wonderarium now features all manner of trinkets, oddities, and potions that dazzle (and sometimes backfire) in classic gnomish fashion. Step inside for an explosion of colors, tinkling bell sounds, and the faint smell of singed hair. There is a small platform out front for fireworks demonstrations. Watch from a safe distance… or not. Mundane Trinkets & Fireworks ¶ Item Description Price Gnomish Glow Rod A foot-long glass rod that emits a soft, warm light in a 10 ft. radius. Perfect for reading blueprints after dark. 10 gp Tick-Tock Pocket Watch A small watch that plays an upbeat jingle on the hour. Non-magical but oh-so-charming. 15 gp Mystery Music Box Hand-cranked music box with a random tune every time (roll a d6 for a new melody). A crowd-pleaser or mild annoyance—depending on your luck. 20 gp Clockwork Trinket Animal Tiny wind-up figures of mice, squirrels, or birds. They scurry/peck for 1 minute before winding down. 8 gp Fireproof Mittens Non-magical, thick mittens sewn with special flame-resistant thread. Designed for blacksmiths—and reckless fireworks handlers. 30 gp Fizzlebang’s “Rainbow Rockets” A pack of three small fireworks shooting out vibrant, glittery sparks in the colors of the rainbow. Beautiful, but loud enough to wake half of Tinkertown. 10 gp Snap, Crackle, and BOOM! A trio of more powerful fireworks that produce dazzling lights in a 30 ft. radius and deafening thunder (Con save DC 13 or be deafened for 1 round). 25 gp Illusory Incense Stick Burns for 1 hour, creating minor illusions in the smoke (as the Minor Illusion cantrip, once every 10 minutes). 30 gp Confetti Grenade When thrown (range 20/60 ft), explodes into multicolored confetti. Creatures in a 5 ft. radius must succeed on a DC 12 Dexterity save or be “Confetti-Covered.” 8 gp Discounted Items and Rarer Marvels ¶ Item Description & Side Effects Price Bonkers Bottle Rocket A single-use mini-firework that should ignite a brilliant spark. Side Effect : 25% chance it misfires, dealing 1d4 fire damage to the holder. 5 gp Random Sparkler When lit as an action, this sparkler can cast Confusion (DC 15 Wisdom Save). Side Effect : The sparkler might affect the user instead of the intended target (50% chance). Duration: 1 minute. 60 gp Sneeze Powder Sachet Creates a 5 ft. cloud of powder that forces creatures in the area to make a DC 12 Con save or spend their next action sneezing. Side Effect : In strong wind, the user can also be affected. 30 gp Phoenixfeather Firework (1-shot) Launches a flaming bird of light that deals 8d6 fire damage in a 10 ft. radius (Dex save DC 14 for half). Leaves behind harmless red-hot embers resembling phoenix down. 150 gp Lens of Long Sight A monocle that grants Advantage on Perception checks in bright light while viewing opjects over 30ft away. Can be mounted on a ranged weapon to increase its range by 20ft. 300 gp Spell-Splinter Boomstick (Firework Wand) A wand (5 charges) that can cast Fire Bolt (1 charge) or Burning Hands at 4th level (2 charges). Regains 1d4 charges daily at dawn. 300 gp Sprocket’s Spark Shell (Consumable) Once thrown, it creates a 15 ft. diameter Faerie Fire effect (DC 15 Dex save). If the target fails, they glow in bright sparks. Side Effect : Loud whistling, alerting nearby creatures. 100 gp Whirligig Skylens A polished brass monocle that can telescope outward. Once per day , you can see up to 1 mile with perfect clarity for 1 minute, as though using the Clairvoyance spell (visual only). A faint tick-tock echoes in your ear while in use. 500 gp Clockwork Bounce Boots A pair of steam-powered boots with small pistons. Once per short rest , you can activate them to triple your long jump distance for 1 round. However, they make a loud “BOING!” noise, drawing attention within 60 ft. 700 gp Gnomish Camouflage Cloak A cloak woven with threads that shift color to match surroundings. Grants Advantage on Stealth checks in urban or subterranean environments. Side Effect : In bright sunlight, it occasionally glitches with flickering patterns, imposing a -1 penalty. 600 gp Pocket-Portal Pipe A small, ornate smoking pipe. Once per day as an action , when you exhale the smoke, it opens a pair of, 2 ft. diameter temporary portal linking two points of your choice within 60 ft. The portal lasts 5 minutes or until something blocks it. 800 gp Gnomeporter Beanie A beanie with a tiny, spinning propeller. Attunement required. Up to 3 times per day , as a bonus action, you can teleport up to 15 ft. to an unoccupied space you can see. Emits a constant whirring noise while worn. 1,000 gp Munster Mart ¶ Once a humble stall hawking a few wedges of cheese, Munster Mart has grown into Tinkertown’s favorite fromagerie, famed for its robust dairy selection and Marbury Munster’s flamboyant mustache. The shop smells of toasted cheese, fresh bread, and the faint whiff of brine from cured meats. Impossibly tall shelves (for a gnome, at least) showcase artisanal cheeses, whimsical charcuterie boards, and, for the daring, a few “enchanted edibles.” Lately, Marbury Munster has been eyeing his new rival— Kardarsha , a male Kajiit traveling merchant (and boat-wagon entrepreneur), backed by Ella’s recent investment. Will Munster Mart maintain its cheesy crown, or will Kardarsha’s curiosities lure customers away? Cheese and Meat Selections ¶ Item Description Price Classic Munster Wheel A semi-soft, pungent cheese with a distinctive tang. The store’s namesake. 2 gp / lb Gnome-Feta Crumble Lightly salted crumbles perfect for salad toppers or mini pastries. 1 gp / lb “Brie-lliant” Spread A creamy, melt-in-your-mouth brie with a mild flavor—kids (and halflings) love it. 3 gp / lb Blue Gear-Vein A strong blue cheese that has swirling “veins” resembling cogs. Slightly metallic aftertaste, beloved by Tinkertown inventors. 4 gp / lb Pepperjack-of-all-Trades Spicy pepper-infused cheese. Rumored to “jumpstart” your taste buds—just watch out for the jalapeño surprise. 5 gp / lb Smoked Cog-Ham A tender ham smoked over gear-shaped coals, giving a subtle mechanical aroma (gnomes love the novelty). 2 gp / lb Gear-Turn Bacon Strips Crispy, spiral-cut bacon that mimics a turning gear. Satisfyingly crunchy. 3 gp / lb Mini Artisan Baguettes Small, crusty baguettes sized for gnome hands. Freshly baked daily. 1 sp each “Rye’d and True” Loaf A hearty rye bread with a swirl pattern. Perfect for sandwiches, soaking up soups, or creating canapés. 5 sp each Clockwork Croissants Flaky pastries shaped like tiny cogs. A local favorite at breakfast—melt some brie on top for pure bliss. 1 gp (3 pcs) Gearhead Charcuterie Board (serves 2) A wooden board carved to look like interlocked gears. Comes with cheese slices, cured ham, olives, and pickled onions. 6 gp “Tinker & Taste” Platter (serves 4) A larger board with assorted cheeses (Brie-lliant, Gnome-Feta, Blue Gear-Vein), smoked sausages, fruit preserves, and breadsticks. 10 gp Mini “Mouse Trap” Board (1-person snack) A playful single-serving board with tiny cheese cubes and dried meats. Includes a small mechanical clamp that looks like a mousetrap. 3 gp Magical & Enchanted Edibles ¶ Item Description Price Mystic Muenster A glowing wedge that grants +1 to Constitution saves for 1 hour after consumption. Side Effect : You emit a faint sulfurous cheesy aroma. 70 gp Singing Swiss Slice When eaten, you can cast Message (cantrip) until your next long rest. Side Effect : You occasionally sing (softly) in squeaky, mouse-like tones for the duration. 40 gp Polymorph Parmesan A potent cheese that allows 1 self cast of Polymorph with a CR limit of 1 and duration of an hour. Side Effect : If you fail a DC 12 Con save, you briefly sprout mouse ears for 10 minutes. 80 gp Ethereal Edam Grants Etherealness (as the 7th-level spell) until the end of your next turn. Side Effect : Roll a d6; on a 1, the user experiences a mild “cheese coma,” falling asleep for 1 round after returning. 80 gp Tinkergold Truffle A rare fungus-enriched cheese rumored to be grown in mushroom farms beneath Tinkertown. Heals 3d8+3 HP once, and grants Advantage on the next tool-related check in the next 10min (Smith’s, Tinker’s). 100 gp Blacksmith’s Brie of Strength Eating a bite of this pungent brie temporarily grants +2 STR (to a max of 22) for 10 minutes. Side Effect : Mild hallucination of floating cheese wheels around your head. 40 gp Store Highlights ¶ Marbury’s Mustache : Painted on signs, boxes, and jars throughout the shop. Some say it’s more famous than the cheese itself. Taste Before You Buy : Sample trays available, but a watchful gnome staff member ensures you don’t take too many freebies. TinkerTown Twist : Gnome engineering meets dairy artistry; mini clockwork fans keep cheeses fresh, mechanical mice roam the floor as part of Munster’s “advertisement.” Come for the cheese—stay for the cultured conversation (and mild cheese puns). Munster Mart promises Tinkertown’s tastiest treats—just keep an eye out for Kardarsha’s roving wagon of wonders! Deep Rock Galactic Corporation ¶ A battered storefront welded onto a rumbling train car, Deep Rock Galactic Corporation is the tough-as-stone mining hub of Tinkertown. Run by the no-nonsense dwarf Karl , the shop greets you with its rallying cry: “Rock and Stone!” A dusty dwarf helmet is perched on a rusty hook outside, and the interior is lit by flickering lanterns strung from the rafters. Miners of all races pass through, lured by rugged gear, arcane digging gadgets, and Karl’s famed one-liners (“If it ain’t dwarven, it ain’t worth dirt!”). Gnomes flock here too, bringing their flair for engineering to the grit of underground expeditions. Mundane Mining Gear ¶ Item Description Price Rock-Solid Pickaxe A sturdy steel pickaxe engraved with the Deep Rock logo. Perfect for mining metal ores and cracking through stubborn stone. 5 gp Driller’s Hand Spade A short-handled shovel. Fits snugly into backpacks. Useful for loosening soil quickly. 2 gp Sturdy Headlamp (Lantern) A metal headband fitted with a swiveling lantern. Illuminates 15 ft. bright light, 15 ft. dim. Requires oil refills. 5 gp “Crash & Bash” Hammer A thick-headed sledgehammer. Favored for demolishing small walls or punishing pesky boulders. 3 gp Mechanical Pulley Kit A portable pulley system that can lift up to 200 lbs. Gnomes refine the gears, ensuring minimal squeak—except under extreme load. 12 gp Rock & Stone Ration Pack Hard biscuits and jerky recommended for 2 days in the mines. Dwarves consider this “comfort food,” gnomes just call it “chewy.” 5 sp Flare Canister A small canister that burns bright for 1 minute, lighting up a 30 ft. radius. Perfect for safely spelunking. 1 gp Miner’s Mustache Wax A wax that can style facial hair into robust dwarven curls or cogs for gnome beards. No mechanical benefit, but a morale booster for sure. 1 sp Sweet Ale of the Tunnel Karl’s personal brew. Drinking grants +2 on CON saves against cold environments for 1 hour. Side Effect : A chance of mild drunkenness (DC 10). 4 gp Glowshroom Powder Add to any torch or lantern to create colored flames for 1 hour. Gnomes love using it to “show off.” 5 sp Magical & Specialized Mining Tools ¶ Item Description Price Driller’s Dream Pick (+1) A +1 pickaxe that deals an additional 1d6 damage against elemental or stone constructs . Once per short rest, you can cast Mold Earth (cantrip) to shift a 5 ft. cube of dirt. 200 gp Handy Dwarven Laser-Cutter A handheld device that casts Scorching Ray (3nd level) once per short rest. Anything made of stone or rock is vulnerable to this damage. Often used to slice through ore veins. Gnomes added a safety toggle—Karl removed it. 200 gp Rockcracker Supply Pod Summon a supply pod from a pocket demension underground (only works while touching the ground). Be sure to tell DM god what you are hoping will be in the pod. May collapse weak tunnel ceilings. 300 gp Farglow Flares (3-pack) Each flare emits Daylight (3rd level) in a 20 ft. radius for 10 minutes. Once lit, they can’t be extinguished early. Perfect for battling subterranean nasties. 80 gp Platform Gun Use to create 10by10 platforms that can be attached to any wall within 60ft. Has 4 charges per short rest. Favored by gnome spelunkers tired of puny rope-ladders. 600 gp Earth-Biter Drill Arm A mechanized gauntlet that grants a Burrow speed of 10 ft. through soft earth or clay once per day for up to 1 minute. Perfect for forging new tunnels—or escaping them. 1,100 gp Deep Rock Rune-Emitter A device that casts Stone Shape (4th level) 3 times per day, letting you sculpt 5 cubic feet of stone. Karl uses it for quick fortifications. 1,000 gp Karl’s Kinetic Smasher ( +2 Maul ) A finely crafted +2 one handed maul that deals 1d6 thunder damage on hit. Once per long rest, you can cast Thunderwave (2nd level) from the weapon (DC 15). Must shout “Rock and Stone!” 2,000 gp Store Highlights ¶ Karl’s War Stories : He’ll often regale customers with tales of “the Drop Pod crash of ’39” or “that time a swarm nearly shaved me beard!” Rock and Stone : The shop motto, yelled every time you buy something important. It’s said to bring good luck in the mines. Gnome vs. Dwarf Rivalry : Gnome-made devices are sometimes more advanced, but dwarven gear is rugged and reliable. Karl tosses friendly jabs at “gnome tinkering.” “No Returns” Policy : Karl’s store is strictly no-refunds—after all, “The mine don’t give you second chances!” Whether you’re a pickaxe-wielding dwarf or a gadget-happy gnome, Deep Rock Galactic Corporation stands ready to equip you for spelunking, monster-bashing, and treasure-hunting. Remember: Rock and Stone! Brews and Blues ¶ Tucked away in a cozy corner of Tinkertown’s rolling streets, Brews and Blues is a dimly lit pub run by the mischievous twin gnomes Artie and Bartie . Nearly identical in height, voice, and even their smug grins. Their bar’s motto is: “When the tinkering stops, the drinking starts.” Downstairs, patrons gather for hearty bar food, to sip creative cocktails, and to lose themselves in the gentle hum of gnomish blues tunes. Upstairs lies the Rumor Mill , a literal milling machine used in the brewing process (for crushing specialty grains), which churns so loudly that private conversations become whispers in the din. Perfect for rumor-seekers and rumor-makers alike. Drinks Menu ¶ Drink Description Price Simple Suds A light, crisp ale brewed from local grains. Easy on the pocket and the palate. 4 sp Gnome-Brewed Lager Smooth lager served in pint-sized steins with engraved cogs. Refreshing with a slightly nutty aftertaste. 8 sp Whirligig Whiskey A fiery whiskey said to “spin your gears.” Burns going down, but warms you up in Tinkertown’s cooler nights. 5 gp Steel-Toed Stout Extra-dark stout with subtle chocolate notes. Especially popular among dwarves, who claim it “kicks like a mule.” 6 sp Fizzlebang’s Fizzy Non-alcoholic. A sweet carbonated juice with a hint of lemon. Perfect for designated tinkers. 3 sp Magical Specialties ¶ Drink Description Price “Midnight Mechanism” A smoky black concoction with swirling silver specks. Grants Darkvision (30 ft.) for 1 hour. Side Effect : mild paranoia about squeaking gears. 13 gp “Cog-Fog Cocktail” A swirling glass that, once sipped, casts Blur on the drinker for 1 minute (DC 13 to maintain concentration). Side Effect : 1 minute of minor dizziness. 25 gp “Clockstopper Cordial” Temporarily grants +5 to initiative rolls for the next hour. Side Effect : your internal sense of time is stuck and you are unable to hold your action for the duration. 10 gp Artie & Bartie’s “Blue Bummer” The signature brew that makes you feel down and sleepy . Mechanically, you gain 1 level of exhaustion (mild) but also a advantage on Wisdom (Insight) checks for 1 hour—your senses sharpen ironically before sleepiness sets in(your Insight is not impacted by exhaustion). 8 gp Bar Food & Snacks ¶ Food Item Description Price Gnome-Sized Sliders (3 pack) Tiny buns stuffed with seasoned mince—perfect for small hands (or nibbling for bigger folk). 5 sp Cog-Cut Fries Spiral-cut potato wedges dusted with tangy gear-themed seasoning. Crisp on the outside, fluffy inside. 3 sp Vegetarian Gear Salad A mix of fresh greens, sliced cucumbers, and miniature “gear-shaped” croutons. Topped with a zesty gnomish dressing. 4 sp Mushroom Ragout Pie Hearty pastry filled with savory mushrooms, onions, and gravy. Popular among Tinkertown’s veggie-lovers. 6 sp Cheesy Clock-Tower Platter An assortment of local cheeses from Munster Mart , served with crackers. Inspired by Tinkertown’s famous Clocktower. 8 sp The Rumor Mill ¶ Up the squeaky stairs is the Rumor Mill —an actual milling contraption used for refining specialty grains in small experimental brew batches. The grinding noise provides perfect cover for hushed conversations. Here, you can glean or spread rumors. Some tidbits float freely among the barflies; others cost a little coin or require a bit of persuasion. Quick Notes ¶ Artie & Bartie : Identical twins except for one difference. They’ll gladly serve “Blue Bummer” to calm you down if Tinkertown’s hustle gets too intense. The Rumor Mill : Pay a coin, roll a Persuasion check, or buy a drink or two—chances are you’ll glean some juicy secrets in the noisy upstairs. Performers : Brews and Blues often features traveling bards, occasionally playing gnomish blues ballads about mechanical heartbreak and stolen steam-powered hearts. Enjoy the ambiance, nurse a drink (maybe not too many “Blue Bummers”), and maybe walk away with some new intel—if the milling machine doesn’t drown out your eavesdropping first

docs.text: Archive audit notice: This handout was released before Session 077 and may contain older mechanics, names, links, or lore phrasing that still needs review. The table's latest ruling is authoritative. Nestled in a whimsically oversized train car, Francis’s Furniture is a rainbow jumble of couches, chairs, and cabinets—some plush, some peculiar, all hand-picked by Francis himself. A flamboyant gnome in a paisley vest, Francis prides himself on curating items “fit for the maddest hatters and the most sensible of halflings alike.” You’ll see chairs that float, tables that dance, and ottomans that purr. If you’re seeking the ordinary or the extraordinary, you’ve come to the right place!

docs.text: Run by Nelly Nimbleneedle , a soft-spoken yet sharp-witted gnome with an eye for detail, Necessities and Nuances is the beating heart of Tinkertown’s daily life. Much like a classic mom-and-pop store, they stock everything from humble hygiene products to experimental potions—just the thing to keep a gnome’s gears running smoothly. Step inside, and you’ll see shelves stacked with everyday must-haves, plus a few extraordinary oddities that could only have been dreamed up in this whimsical, rolling town.
docs.title: Necessities and Nuances

docs.text: Item Description Price Tampons (10 pack) Called “Flo-Stop” by locals. docs.text: The SoSo Mart chain has spread across the land faster than a flock of griffons on half-price wing night—promising “savings, or so-so they say.” Every location looks the same: a huge warehouse-like interior with bright, garish signage insisting that everything is “Cheaper Here!” Run by the perpetually bland Manager Manny Monotone , this branch in Tinkertown towers over its modest neighbors, complete with a mechanical sliding door that greets you with a tinny “Welcome to SoSo Mart.” They advertise a 20% discount for members , but the membership fees are steep, and the fine print is very fine. Advertising Slogan : “You could pay more elsewhere … but that would be so so silly, wouldn’t it?”
docs.title: SoSo Mart

docs.text: Item Description Price SoSo Brand Tampons (10 pack) Basic, no-frills design. Cardboard applicator squeaks sometimes. Provides a quick sugar rush—then a sugar crash. 8 cp each SoSo Bandages Low-quality bandages. Has a 20% chance to snap shut mid-descent , causing falling damage for the user. 150 gp SoSo Self-Repair Kit Supposed to cast Mending (cantrip) on small objects 3/day. Sometimes spontaneously fogs up, negating the advantage. 250 gp Hovering Halberd (Damaged) This halberd can levitate itself for 1 minute (1/day). 15% chance it drops out of the air mid-use, possibly landing on your foot (1d4 damage). 300 gp
docs.title: Discounted Magical Items

docs.text: 20% Discount Membership For a flat 50 gp annual fee, sign a “few” pages of magically binding contract, and all items qualify for the discount. Warning : Breaking membership terms might incur “substantial magical penalties.” Uniformed Staff Manager Manny Monotone lurks near the registers, urging patrons to upgrade to the “Super SoSo Membership.” Staff rarely seem enthusiastic; must be the corporate training. Happy shopping (or so-so shopping)! Remember, at SoSo Mart: “If it ain’t cheap, we’ll make it cheaper… eventually.”
docs.title: Store Highlights

docs.text: Run by Sergeant Ironbeard , a gruff dwarf veteran who paces around the shop barking orders at imaginary recruits, Full Metal Racket is Tinkertown’s one-stop depot for all things armament. Clad in a dented breastplate etched with slogans like “Gnome Mercy,” he firmly believes the town is “always one subterranean ambush away” from total disaster. Though he scoffs at “puny gnome gear,” he grudgingly stocks smaller-sized weapons and armor, too. Step into his cramped train-car workshop, and expect an earful of tough love—and maybe some top-notch arms if you can handle the rant.
docs.title: Full Metal Racket

docs.text: Item Description Price Short Sword A standard steel blade favored by gnomes for its manageable size. Sergeant Ironbeard rolls his eyes at its “tiny jab,” but it gets the job done. 10 gp Long Sword Heavy, robust steel for medium-sized creatures. The dwarf calls it “barely adequate.” 15 gp Heavy War Pick 2 handed 1d10, Vicious Weapon: add an extra 1d10 on critcal hit. Sturdy, with a reinforced haft, ideal for splitting rocks or heads. 1 gp Gnomish Spike Trap (kit) A collapsible set of spikes that can be laid on the floor to deter intruders. Covers a 5 ft. square. Ironbeard says “if it’s small, it’s sneaky.” 5 gp Gnomeflint Pistol A rudimentary black-powder firearm with a -1 to attack rolls. Deals 2d12 piercing damage (range 20/40). Requires a full action to reload. Ironbeard calls it a “boomstick for babies.” 120 gp Light Crossbow A reliable range option. Ironbeard says, “If you can’t handle real recoil, at least handle this.” 25 gp Handaxe Perfect for close quarters or throwing. The dwarf uses one to shave his whiskers. 5 gp Padded Armor Basic quilted armor, comfortable but not too protective. Sergeant Ironbeard sneers, “Might as well wear a pillow.” 5 gp Leather Armor Standard light armor, popular among gnome scouts. “Softies,” mutters Ironbeard. 10 gp Chain Shirt Medium armor that clinks and clanks. Gnomes like the partial coverage without the weight—Ironbeard just roars, “Grow a spine!” 50 gp Breastplate A metal front plate offering decent protection. If it’s good enough for the dwarf, it’s good enough for you—though he says, “you’ll never fill it out.” 400 gp Splint Armor Heavy metal plates strapped over chain. Ironbeard’s favorite pre-war style. “Now, this is real armor,” he bellows. 200 gp Gnome Helm A smaller, lightweight steel cap with a flip-down visor that looks like a cog. Ironbeard calls it “that tinker bucket.” 15 gp

Deals 3d12 piercing damage (range 60/120). Requires a full action to reload. docs.text: Sergeant’s Rants : Expect an earful of “YOU CALL THAT A WEAPON?” whenever you browse anything but the heavy gear. Trench-Safe Guarantee? : Ironbeard claims everything sold here is “battle-tested” …though you might notice some items have never seen real conflict. All Sales Final : Return policy? “War waits for no one, so neither do we!”
docs.title: Additional Shop Flavor

docs.text: Formerly Fredrick Fizzlebang’s Fireworks , this bright and bustling bazaar is owned by the one and only Fredrick Fizzlebang —a gnome with a spark in his eye and a perpetual wisp of smoke drifting from his rumpled top hat. While Fredrick’s passion for pyrotechnics remains, the rebranded Wonderarium now features all manner of trinkets, oddities, and potions that dazzle (and sometimes backfire) in classic gnomish fashion. Step inside for an explosion of colors, tinkling bell sounds, and the faint smell of singed hair. There is a small platform out front for fireworks demonstrations. Watch from a safe distance… or not.
docs.title: The Wonderarium

Perfect for reading blueprints after dark. 10 gp Tick-Tock Pocket Watch A small watch that plays an upbeat jingle on the hour. A crowd-pleaser or mild annoyance—depending on your luck. 20 gp Clockwork Trinket Animal Tiny wind-up figures of mice, squirrels, or birds. Designed for blacksmiths—and reckless fireworks handlers. 30 gp Fizzlebang’s “Rainbow Rockets” A pack of three small fireworks shooting out vibrant, glittery sparks in the colors of the rainbow. docs.text: Once a humble stall hawking a few wedges of cheese, Munster Mart has grown into Tinkertown’s favorite fromagerie, famed for its robust dairy selection and Marbury Munster’s flamboyant mustache. The shop smells of toasted cheese, fresh bread, and the faint whiff of brine from cured meats. Impossibly tall shelves (for a gnome, at least) showcase artisanal cheeses, whimsical charcuterie boards, and, for the daring, a few “enchanted edibles.” Lately, Marbury Munster has been eyeing his new rival— Kardarsha , a male Kajiit traveling merchant (and boat-wagon entrepreneur), backed by Ella’s recent investment. Will Munster Mart maintain its cheesy crown, or will Kardarsha’s curiosities lure customers away?
docs.title: Munster Mart

docs.text: Item Description Price Classic Munster Wheel A semi-soft, pungent cheese with a distinctive tang. The store’s namesake. 2 gp / lb Gnome-Feta Crumble Lightly salted crumbles perfect for salad toppers or mini pastries. 1 gp / lb “Brie-lliant” Spread A creamy, melt-in-your-mouth brie with a mild flavor—kids (and halflings) love it. 3 gp / lb Blue Gear-Vein A strong blue cheese that has swirling “veins” resembling cogs. Slightly metallic aftertaste, beloved by Tinkertown inventors. 4 gp / lb Pepperjack-of-all-Trades Spicy pepper-infused cheese. Rumored to “jumpstart” your taste buds—just watch out for the jalapeño surprise. 5 gp / lb Smoked Cog-Ham A tender ham smoked over gear-shaped coals, giving a subtle mechanical aroma (gnomes love the novelty). 2 gp / lb Gear-Turn Bacon Strips Crispy, spiral-cut bacon that mimics a turning gear. Satisfyingly crunchy. 3 gp / lb Mini Artisan Baguettes Small, crusty baguettes sized for gnome hands. Freshly baked daily. 1 sp each “Rye’d and True” Loaf A hearty rye bread with a swirl pattern. Perfect for sandwiches, soaking up soups, or creating canapés. 5 sp each Clockwork Croissants Flaky pastries shaped like tiny cogs. A local favorite at breakfast—melt some brie on top for pure bliss. 1 gp (3 pcs) Gearhead Charcuterie Board (serves 2) A wooden board carved to look like interlocked gears. Comes with cheese slices, cured ham, olives, and pickled onions. 6 gp “Tinker & Taste” Platter (serves 4) A larger board with assorted cheeses (Brie-lliant, Gnome-Feta, Blue Gear-Vein), smoked sausages, fruit preserves, and breadsticks. 10 gp Mini “Mouse Trap” Board (1-person snack) A playful single-serving board with tiny cheese cubes and dried meats. Includes a small mechanical clamp that looks like a mousetrap. 3 gp

Side Effect : You occasionally sing (softly) in squeaky, mouse-like tones for the duration. 40 gp Polymorph Parmesan A potent cheese that allows 1 self cast of Polymorph with a CR limit of 1 and duration of an hour. Side Effect : If you fail a DC 12 Con save, you briefly sprout mouse ears for 10 minutes. 80 gp Ethereal Edam Grants Etherealness (as the 7th-level spell) until the end of your next turn. Side Effect : Mild hallucination of floating cheese wheels around your head. 40 gp
docs.title: Magical & Enchanted Edibles

docs.text: Marbury’s Mustache : Painted on signs, boxes, and jars throughout the shop. Some say it’s more famous than the cheese itself. Taste Before You Buy : Sample trays available, but a watchful gnome staff member ensures you don’t take too many freebies. TinkerTown Twist : Gnome engineering meets dairy artistry; mini clockwork fans keep cheeses fresh, mechanical mice roam the floor as part of Munster’s “advertisement.” Come for the cheese—stay for the cultured conversation (and mild cheese puns). Munster Mart promises Tinkertown’s tastiest treats—just keep an eye out for Kardarsha’s roving wagon of wonders!
docs.title: Store Highlights

docs.text: A battered storefront welded onto a rumbling train car, Deep Rock Galactic Corporation is the tough-as-stone mining hub of Tinkertown. Run by the no-nonsense dwarf Karl , the shop greets you with its rallying cry: “Rock and Stone!” A dusty dwarf helmet is perched on a rusty hook outside, and the interior is lit by flickering lanterns strung from the rafters. Miners of all races pass through, lured by rugged gear, arcane digging gadgets, and Karl’s famed one-liners (“If it ain’t dwarven, it ain’t worth dirt!”). Gnomes flock here too, bringing their flair for engineering to the grit of underground expeditions.
docs.title: Deep Rock Galactic Corporation

docs.text: Item Description Price Rock-Solid Pickaxe A sturdy steel pickaxe engraved with the Deep Rock logo. Perfect for mining metal ores and cracking through stubborn stone. 5 gp Driller’s Hand Spade A short-handled shovel. Fits snugly into backpacks. Useful for loosening soil quickly. 2 gp Sturdy Headlamp (Lantern) A metal headband fitted with a swiveling lantern. Illuminates 15 ft. bright light, 15 ft. dim. Requires oil refills. 5 gp “Crash & Bash” Hammer A thick-headed sledgehammer. Favored for demolishing small walls or punishing pesky boulders. 3 gp Mechanical Pulley Kit A portable pulley system that can lift up to 200 lbs. Gnomes refine the gears, ensuring minimal squeak—except under extreme load. 12 gp Rock & Stone Ration Pack Hard biscuits and jerky recommended for 2 days in the mines. Dwarves consider this “comfort food,” gnomes just call it “chewy.” 5 sp Flare Canister A small canister that burns bright for 1 minute, lighting up a 30 ft. radius. Perfect for safely spelunking. 1 gp Miner’s Mustache Wax A wax that can style facial hair into robust dwarven curls or cogs for gnome beards. No mechanical benefit, but a morale booster for sure. 1 sp Sweet Ale of the Tunnel Karl’s personal brew. Drinking grants +2 on CON saves against cold environments for 1 hour. Side Effect : A chance of mild drunkenness (DC 10). 4 gp Glowshroom Powder Add to any torch or lantern to create colored flames for 1 hour. Gnomes love using it to “show off.” 5 sp
docs.title: Mundane Mining Gear

docs.text: Item Description Price Driller’s Dream Pick (+1) A +1 pickaxe that deals an additional 1d6 damage against elemental or stone constructs . Once per short rest, you can cast Mold Earth (cantrip) to shift a 5 ft. cube of dirt. 200 gp Handy Dwarven Laser-Cutter A handheld device that casts Scorching Ray (3nd level) once per short rest. Anything made of stone or rock is vulnerable to this damage. Often used to slice through ore veins. Gnomes added a safety toggle—Karl removed it. 200 gp Rockcracker Supply Pod Summon a supply pod from a pocket demension underground (only works while touching the ground). Be sure to tell DM god what you are hoping will be in the pod. May collapse weak tunnel ceilings. 300 gp Farglow Flares (3-pack) Each flare emits Daylight (3rd level) in a 20 ft. radius for 10 minutes. Once lit, they can’t be extinguished early. Perfect for battling subterranean nasties. 80 gp Platform Gun Use to create 10by10 platforms that can be attached to any wall within 60ft. Has 4 charges per short rest. Favored by gnome spelunkers tired of puny rope-ladders. 600 gp Earth-Biter Drill Arm A mechanized gauntlet that grants a Burrow speed of 10 ft. through soft earth or clay once per day for up to 1 minute. Perfect for forging new tunnels—or escaping them. 1,100 gp Deep Rock Rune-Emitter A device that casts Stone Shape (4th level) 3 times per day, letting you sculpt 5 cubic feet of stone. Karl uses it for quick fortifications. 1,000 gp Karl’s Kinetic Smasher ( +2 Maul ) A finely crafted +2 one handed maul that deals 1d6 thunder damage on hit. Once per long rest, you can cast Thunderwave (2nd level) from the weapon (DC 15). Must shout “Rock and Stone!” 2,000 gp
docs.title: Magical & Specialized Mining Tools

docs.text: Karl’s War Stories : He’ll often regale customers with tales of “the Drop Pod crash of ’39” or “that time a swarm nearly shaved me beard!” Rock and Stone : The shop motto, yelled every time you buy something important. It’s said to bring good luck in the mines. Gnome vs. Dwarf Rivalry : Gnome-made devices are sometimes more advanced, but dwarven gear is rugged and reliable. Karl tosses friendly jabs at “gnome tinkering.” “No Returns” Policy : Karl’s store is strictly no-refunds—after all, “The mine don’t give you second chances!” Whether you’re a pickaxe-wielding dwarf or a gadget-happy gnome, Deep Rock Galactic Corporation stands ready to equip you for spelunking, monster-bashing, and treasure-hunting. Remember: Rock and Stone!
docs.title: Store Highlights

docs.text: Tucked away in a cozy corner of Tinkertown’s rolling streets, Brews and Blues is a dimly lit pub run by the mischievous twin gnomes Artie and Bartie . Nearly identical in height, voice, and even their smug grins. Their bar’s motto is: “When the tinkering stops, the drinking starts.” Downstairs, patrons gather for hearty bar food, to sip creative cocktails, and to lose themselves in the gentle hum of gnomish blues tunes. Upstairs lies the Rumor Mill , a literal milling machine used in the brewing process (for crushing specialty grains), which churns so loudly that private conversations become whispers in the din. Perfect for rumor-seekers and rumor-makers alike.
docs.title: Brews and Blues

docs.text: Drink Description Price Simple Suds A light, crisp ale brewed from local grains. Easy on the pocket and the palate. 4 sp Gnome-Brewed Lager Smooth lager served in pint-sized steins with engraved cogs. Refreshing with a slightly nutty aftertaste. 8 sp Whirligig Whiskey A fiery whiskey said to “spin your gears.” Burns going down, but warms you up in Tinkertown’s cooler nights. 5 gp Steel-Toed Stout Extra-dark stout with subtle chocolate notes. Especially popular among dwarves, who claim it “kicks like a mule.” 6 sp Fizzlebang’s Fizzy Non-alcoholic. A sweet carbonated juice with a hint of lemon. Perfect for designated tinkers. 3 sp
docs.title: Drinks Menu

docs.text: Drink Description Price “Midnight Mechanism” A smoky black concoction with swirling silver specks. Grants Darkvision (30 ft.) for 1 hour. Side Effect : mild paranoia about squeaking gears. 13 gp “Cog-Fog Cocktail” A swirling glass that, once sipped, casts Blur on the drinker for 1 minute (DC 13 to maintain concentration). Side Effect : 1 minute of minor dizziness. 25 gp “Clockstopper Cordial” Temporarily grants +5 to initiative rolls for the next hour. Side Effect : your internal sense of time is stuck and you are unable to hold your action for the duration. 10 gp Artie & Bartie’s “Blue Bummer” The signature brew that makes you feel down and sleepy . Mechanically, you gain 1 level of exhaustion (mild) but also a advantage on Wisdom (Insight) checks for 1 hour—your senses sharpen ironically before sleepiness sets in(your Insight is not impacted by exhaustion). 8 gp
docs.title: Magical Specialties

docs.text: Food Item Description Price Gnome-Sized Sliders (3 pack) Tiny buns stuffed with seasoned mince—perfect for small hands (or nibbling for bigger folk). 5 sp Cog-Cut Fries Spiral-cut potato wedges dusted with tangy gear-themed seasoning. Crisp on the outside, fluffy inside. 3 sp Vegetarian Gear Salad A mix of fresh greens, sliced cucumbers, and miniature “gear-shaped” croutons. Topped with a zesty gnomish dressing. 4 sp Mushroom Ragout Pie Hearty pastry filled with savory mushrooms, onions, and gravy. Popular among Tinkertown’s veggie-lovers. 6 sp Cheesy Clock-Tower Platter An assortment of local cheeses from Munster Mart , served with crackers. Inspired by Tinkertown’s famous Clocktower. 8 sp
docs.title: Bar Food & Snacks

docs.text: Up the squeaky stairs is the Rumor Mill —an actual milling contraption used for refining specialty grains in small experimental brew batches. The grinding noise provides perfect cover for hushed conversations. Here, you can glean or spread rumors. Some tidbits float freely among the barflies; others cost a little coin or require a bit of persuasion.
docs.title: The Rumor Mill

docs.text: Artie & Bartie : Identical twins except for one difference. They’ll gladly serve “Blue Bummer” to calm you down if Tinkertown’s hustle gets too intense. The Rumor Mill : Pay a coin, roll a Persuasion check, or buy a drink or two—chances are you’ll glean some juicy secrets in the noisy upstairs. Performers : Brews and Blues often features traveling bards, occasionally playing gnomish blues ballads about mechanical heartbreak and stolen steam-powered hearts. Enjoy the ambiance, nurse a drink (maybe not too many “Blue Bummers”), and maybe walk away with some new intel—if the milling machine doesn’t drown out your eavesdropping first

docs.text: Order of Events ¶ Archive audit notice: This handout was released before Session 077 and may contain older mechanics, names, links, or lore phrasing that still needs review. The table's latest ruling is authoritative. 1️⃣ Three-Legged Ice Skating Race 🏃‍♂️ ( Speed & Agility ) → Leads directly into 2️⃣ Mechanical Bobsled Race 🛷 ( Engineering & Control ) → Finishes at 3️⃣ Snow Slingshot Siege ❄️ ( Strategy & Accuracy! ) Why These Work as a Triathlon ¶ Momentum Carries Over : The faster you finish one event, the sooner you begin the next . Team Roles Matter : Different skills shine— athletics for skating, dexterity for bobsledding, intelligence for siege-building . Each event has its own chaos but connects seamlessly—leading to last-second turnarounds! 🏆 Spectator Experience & Commentary Tracks ¶ The Great Tinkertown Winter Triathlon isn’t just for competitors—it’s one of the biggest spectator events of the year! A pair of gnomish sports commentators —legendary announcers Riff Gearwhistle and Clank Cogsworth —provide play-by-play analysis, comedic banter, and exaggerated reactions to every twist and turn of the race. Event 1: The Three-Legged Ice Skating Race ¶ ⛸️ Team Coordination Meets Sheer Chaos! The first event of The Great Tinkertown Winter Triathlon is a classic gnomish spin on ice racing— literally . Competitors must tie one leg to their partner’s , strap on skates that may or may not have been recently tested , and make their way across an icy obstacle-laden course without wiping out! Rules & Structure ¶ Each team of six must pair up into three sets of two for the race. Pairs will tie one leg together and attempt to skate as fast as possible across the course. Once they cross the finish line , they untie themselves and jump straight into their pre-built bobsled for Event 2 . The faster they finish, the sooner they start the bobsled race! 🎙️ Three-Legged Ice Skating Race Commentary ¶ Situation Riff Gearwhistle's Take Clank Cogsworth's Response Start of the race “And they’re off! Look at those gnomes go—like a bunch of caffeinated chipmunks on ice!” “Or like poorly-oiled automatons about to tip over—oh! And there goes our first fall! ” Slipping on the ice “Whoa! That’s what we call a Tinkertown Tango! ” “Oh, it’s a full send—hope they enjoy snow for dinner!” Wind tunnel struggles “The wind is really picking up! Some of these teams are about to learn what flying gnomes look like!” “We should start handing out air mileage rewards!” Finish line moments “It’s a neck-and-neck finish! Who will cross the line first?!” “Forget the skates, just dive for it!” The Ice Course Layout ¶ The race spans 300 feet of icy terrain , broken into four treacherous sections: Section Description Mechanics & DCs 1. The Slippery Start (0-50 ft.) The first stretch is pristine but deceptively slick ice. Racers must find their rhythm fast or risk slipping immediately! Acrobatics (DC 10): Success = Normal movement. Fail = Skid in place, lose 5 feet. 2. The Snowy Patches (50-150 ft.) Patches of light snow mounds make the surface uneven, forcing teams to weave carefully or risk getting tripped up. Dexterity (DC 12): Success = Navigate cleanly. Fail = Stumble, lose 10 feet. 3. The Wind Tunnel (150-250 ft.) Strong gusts from enchanted snow fans blast racers unpredictably, sending them veering sideways or spinning out. Strength (DC 12): Success = Push through. Fail = Get pushed back 5-10 feet. 4. The Mogul Gauntlet (250-300 ft.) A final series of small icy ramps and dips threaten to launch the unprepared. Acrobatics (DC 14): Success = Land smoothly. Fail = Faceplant at the finish line (but still move forward). 💡 DM Option: Allow teamwork mechanics —one partner can use their roll to help the other if they’re proficient in Acrobatics! Bonus Hazards & Spectator Chaos ¶ The Gnomish Pep Band 🎺: Over-enthusiastic musicians line the track, occasionally blasting out a discordant tune that might cause distraction ( DC 10 Constitution save or momentary loss of focus ). Wild Penguins (or Mechanical Equivalents?) 🐧: Someone let loose a flock of confused snowy birds that periodically slide across the track, forcing emergency dodges ( DC 13 Dexterity save or collision ). Loose Magic Snowballs ❄️: Random “stray” enchanted snowballs occasionally bounce onto the track, leaving patches of slippery or sticky ice . 🏁 Finishing the Race: - The first teams to cross gain priority access to their bobsleds in Event 2 . - Slower teams must scramble into their sleds seconds behind , putting them at a small disadvantage! Event 2: The Mechanical Bobsled Race ¶ 🛷 Speed, Stability, and Tinkertown Engineering! The second event tests raw speed, teamwork, and craftsmanship as teams pilot their pre-built bobsleds down an icy, winding course . However, these sleds have no built-in propulsion —meaning gravity, weight distribution, and steering skill determine victory! Bobsled Construction Rules ¶ Each team of six had time before the race to design and build their sled using non-magical materials . Sleds must be piloted by four teammates at a time ( two will rotate out and join for the next event ). Teams were allowed to build for either speed, stability, or gimmicks , affecting how well they perform on the track! 💡 Strategy Choices: | Build Focus | Effect | |----------------|-----------------------------| | Speed-Focused Build 🏎️ | Bonus to initial momentum, but steering is harder . | | Stability-Focused Build 🏗️ | Handles turns well, but might lag behind in acceleration. | | Weird Gnome Engineering™ Build 🤪 | Could be brilliant… or explode. DM rolls secretly. | 🎙️ Mechanical Bobsled Race Commentary ¶ Situation Riff Gearwhistle's Take Clank Cogsworth's Response Sleds launch from the start “And we’re off! Look at those sleds FLY—some intentionally, some... not so much.” “If a sled flips before the first turn, does it really count as a race?” Near wipeout in a turn “Ohhh, that was a CLOSE one! That sled was nearly a permanent part of the track!” “Might need to rename this the Bobsled Wreckage Derby! ” Rough landing from a jump “Oof! That’s gotta rattle your screws!” “Not to worry, folks—gnomes bounce! ” Finish line chaos “It’s too close to call! Someone’s sled is literally falling apart but STILL moving!” “That’s what we call winning through duct tape and hope! ” The Icy Track Layout ¶ The bobsled run is a 500-foot course featuring sharp turns, unexpected jumps, and environmental hazards . Successful teams must balance speed and control while navigating obstacles. Section Description Mechanics & DCs 1. The Drop (0-100 ft.) The first 50-foot near-vertical slope launches sleds into high speeds FAST. Athletics (DC 12) to brace or lose control. 2. The Frostbite Chicane (100-250 ft.) A sharp set of twists force teams to steer carefully or risk a wipeout. Dexterity (DC 14) to steer safely. 3. The Mogul Madness (250-350 ft.) Ice humps and gaps shake sleds, testing suspension. Poor builds might crack here! Tinker’s Tools (DC 13) for durability checks. 4. The Avalanche Curve (350-450 ft.) A steep banking turn requires perfect balance—or you flip! Acrobatics (DC 15) to keep upright. 5. The Final Stretch (450-500 ft.) The fastest section— raw speed vs. last-second steering! Final Dexterity (DC 12) OR Strength (DC 14) for a last-second push! Bonus Hazards & Mayhem ¶ Gnomish "Air Fans" Malfunction 🍃: Automated fans meant to reduce wind resistance occasionally fire randomly , boosting or spinning sleds out ( DC 13 Dexterity save ). Tumbling Snow Golems ⛄: A runaway sentient snowball somehow found its way onto the track. A team must dodge it or get slowed down ( DC 14 Acrobatics check ). Sabotage or Defensive Tactics? 🤔: Teams can lean into their build strategy to mess with rivals—use extra weight to bump opponents off course ( contested Strength check ) or fake a steering malfunction ( Deception vs. Insight ). 🏁 Finishing the Race: - First to finish = First to start building their siege launcher in Event 3! - Slower teams get a delayed start , meaning less time to build and launch! Event 3: The Snow Slingshot Siege ¶ 🎯 Precision, Power, and a Dash of Chaos! The final event of the Great Tinkertown Winter Triathlon tests not just speed, but ingenuity! After hurtling through the Three-Legged Ice Skating Race and Mechanical Bobsled Race , teams immediately enter a fortified arena where they must construct and use a massive snow-launching contraption to knock down targets before their opponents do! Teams must build their siege weapon from provided materials , then fire at six magical targets to claim victory. Faster teams from the previous event get a head start on construction. 🏁 First team to destroy all their targets wins the Triathlon! 🏗️ Phase 1: Construction (Time-Based Head Start) ¶ Each team must construct a snow-launching device: Slingshot (Quick-firing, but lower power). Catapult (Good range, moderate accuracy). Trebuchet (Most powerful, but slowest to reload). Faster bobsled teams get a head start based on their finish order : 🥇 1st place in bobsled race = 10-minute head start 🥈 2nd place = 5-minute head start 🥉 3rd place or later = No delay, start immediately 🔧 Building Mechanics ¶ Teams describe their design and assign roles. Each player contributes one skill check (or helps another). Three key elements determine launcher quality : Skill Check Effect Intelligence (Tinker’s Tools, Arcana, or Investigation) DC 13+ Design stability – Reduces chance of misfires. Dexterity (Sleight of Hand or Tinker’s Tools) DC 14+ Fine-tuning aim – Improves accuracy on target shots. Strength (Athletics or Raw Construction) DC 12+ Power & durability – Prevents breaking under stress. 🎲 DM Note: If the team rolls exceptionally well (all rolls DC 18+), their launcher gains a +1 bonus on all attack rolls. If they fail multiple checks (more than 2 failures), it starts wobbly and has a 10% chance of misfiring on every shot. 🎙️ Snow Slingshot Siege Commentary ¶ Situation Riff Gearwhistle's Take Clank Cogsworth's Response First team starts building “And the first team is already assembling their siege weapon! Looks like… uh… a slingshot? A trebuchet? A gnome’s bad dream?” “Whatever it is, it better work! ” Team struggles with launcher “Ooooh, that does NOT look stable. That’s not a siege weapon, that’s an art installation waiting to collapse! ” “Maybe they’re aiming for style points? ” Perfect shot on a hard target “BOOM! What a hit! That target never saw it coming! ” “Neither did I! I was too busy watching the OTHER team’s slingshot catch fire!” Final shot for the win “They line up the shot… they FIRE… IT HITS!” “WE HAVE OUR WINNERS! And only minor injuries this time!” 🎯 Phase 2: Target Practice (Firing the Siege Weapon!) ¶ Once built, teams must fire at 6 magical targets to win. Each turn: 1. A player loads the launcher (no check required). 2. A player aims & fires (Attack Roll required). 3. The shot hits or misses based on target AC. Target Type AC Special Rule Wooden Dummy (Basic Target) 12 Simple, stationary, easy to hit. Enchanted Floating Gear 14 Floats erratically, requires Dex Save (DC 12) on hit to confirm direct impact . Defensive Ice Wall 16 Requires a Strength-based attack to break through. Animated Snowman 14 Moves 5 feet after every hit , forcing new angles. Bouncing Bell Target 18 Disadvantage on attack rolls unless using a powerful launch method . Final “Grand Clocktower” Target 20 Must be hit twice to fully destroy! 💡 Tactical Options: - Fast-firing Slingshot : More chances to hit, but may struggle with armored/moving targets. - Steady Catapult : Balanced power and accuracy. - Heavy Trebuchet : Devastating force, but takes 2 rounds to reload . 🔧 Adjustments & Fixes: - A team member can spend a round fixing issues if their launcher misfires (DC 12 Intelligence or Tinker’s Tools). - Teams can switch shooters if one is struggling. 🚨 Winning Condition: First team to destroy all 6 targets wins the Triathlon! 🎭 Bonus Chaos & Special Mechanics ¶ To keep the event dynamic and unpredictable , the following random events may occur: Random Event (Roll d6) Effect 1 - Slippery Ice Patch Someone slips near the launcher! Next shooter rolls Dex Save DC 13 or has Disadvantage . 2 - Referee Interference A gnomish referee runs onto the field screaming “Foul!” before realizing their mistake. Delays one shot. 3 - Sudden Blizzard Visibility drops! All attack rolls made at Disadvantage until the storm passes (1d3 rounds). 4 - Mechanical Malfunction A random team’s launcher misfires , shooting backward instead of forward (must be reset). 5 - Rival Sabotage! Another team’s gnome assistant sneaks up and loosens a hinge —if unnoticed, next shot is wildly inaccurate . (Perception DC 14 to catch them!) 6 - Surprise Extra Target! A new floating “bonus target” (AC 15) appears! Hitting it grants a +1 to all future attack rolls. 🏆 Why This Works as the Final Event ¶ Speed matters, but so does skill – Rushing through earlier events gets you a head start, but a poorly built launcher could ruin your chances. Different team members shine in different areas – Intelligence for design, Dexterity for aiming, Strength for power. Spectator-friendly excitement – Misfires, random magic mishaps, and comeback moments keep the crowd entertained! A tense, neck-and-neck ending – Since teams fire at different speeds and accuracy varies, no one is ever truly out of the race until the final shot! Final Order of Events in The Great Tinkertown Winter Triathlon ¶ 1️⃣ Three-Legged Ice Skating Race ⛸️ ( Agility & Coordination ) → Teams rush to their bobsleds. 2️⃣ Mechanical Bobsled Race 🛷 ( Speed & Engineering ) → Finish order determines Siege building time. 3️⃣ The Snow Slingshot Siege ❄️ ( Strategy, Teamwork, & Accuracy ) → First team to destroy their targets wins! 🥇 1st-3rd Place Prizes ¶ No Tinkertown festival is complete without over-the-top prizes , some practical, some… not so much. 🥇 1st Place - The Grand Champions ¶ 🏆 Title: Tinkertown Triathlon Titans! 🎁 Prize Rewards: - The Golden Gear Trophy 🏆 (An oversized, gaudy, gold-painted mechanical gear that spins on its own. Engraved with the team’s name.) - 250 gp each - A custom "Tinkertown Winter Triathlon Badge" ( Can be attatched to the bottom of shoes where it Grants +10 ft. speed on ice. ) - 1 Free Magical Item from the Wonderarium (DM’s choice of rare trinket or consumable). - Honorary Parade Float in the Next Festival (Their team gets their own parade float next year, complete with an animatronic version of them!) - A lifetime supply of free fries at Brews & Blues. 🍟 ( Fine print: "Lifetime" means until Artie & Bartie get tired of them. ) 🥈 2nd Place - The Almost Champions ¶ 🏅 Title: Silver-Gear Sprinters! 🎁 Prize Rewards: - The Silver-Cog Medals ( Slightly dented, but made with love. ) - 150 gp each - A “Second Best” Enchanted Spoon ( Can magically stir drinks on command. Bartie swears it’s useful. ) - 50% off coupon for Munster Mart’s cheese board platters. 🥉 3rd Place - The "Hey, At Least We Finished" Award ¶ 🥉 Title: The Resilient Runners! 🎁 Prize Rewards: - The Bronze Wrench Trophy ( For "enduring mechanical hardship with grace and panic." It squeaks when turned. ) - 75 gp each - A free round of drinks at Brews & Blues. 🍻 (Limit: No more than 2 Blue Bummers in one night.) - A "Slightly Used" Sled from the Race. ( May or may not be fixable. Congratulations! ) 🎭 Extra Fun Awards ¶ Because Tinkertown loves a good laugh , additional “honorary” awards are handed out: 🏅 "Best Wipeout" – Given to the team with the most spectacular crash during the race. 🏅 "Most Over-Engineered Sled" – For the team that made a sled so complicated it was practically a mobile house. 🏅 "The Tinker Award" – For the team that built the most creative (or absurd) snow-launching contraption. 🏅 "Audience Favorite" – Voted on by the crowd! The most beloved team gets a custom-made Tinkertown plushie in their honor. 🏁 Closing Ceremony ¶ As the winners are announced , fireworks from The Wonderarium explode above, bathing the festival in shimmering lights. Artie & Bartie lead a Victory Toast at Brews & Blues , where competitors celebrate (or drown their sorrows) . Meanwhile, rumors are already swirling about what wild challenges next year’s Triathlon will bring… 🎆 “Another Tinkertown Triathlon in the books! Now, let’s drink until we forget how bad we were at ice skating!” 🎆
