docs.text: The Gnomish Pep Band 🎺: Over-enthusiastic musicians line the track, occasionally blasting out a discordant tune that might cause distraction ( DC 10 Constitution save or momentary loss of focus ). Wild Penguins (or Mechanical Equivalents?) 🐧: Someone let loose a flock of confused snowy birds that periodically slide across the track, forcing emergency dodges ( DC 13 Dexterity save or collision ). Loose Magic Snowballs ❄️: Random “stray” enchanted snowballs occasionally bounce onto the track, leaving patches of slippery or sticky ice . 🏁 Finishing the Race: - The first teams to cross gain priority access to their bobsleds in Event 2 . - Slower teams must scramble into their sleds seconds behind , putting them at a small disadvantage!
docs.title: Bonus Hazards & Spectator Chaos

docs.text: 🛷 Speed, Stability, and Tinkertown Engineering! The second event tests raw speed, teamwork, and craftsmanship as teams pilot their pre-built bobsleds down an icy, winding course . However, these sleds have no built-in propulsion —meaning gravity, weight distribution, and steering skill determine victory!
docs.title: Event 2: The Mechanical Bobsled Race

docs.text: Each team of six had time before the race to design and build their sled using non-magical materials . Sleds must be piloted by four teammates at a time ( two will rotate out and join for the next event ). Teams were allowed to build for either speed, stability, or gimmicks , affecting how well they perform on the track! 💡 Strategy Choices: | Build Focus | Effect | |----------------|-----------------------------| | Speed-Focused Build 🏎️ | Bonus to initial momentum, but steering is harder . | | Stability-Focused Build 🏗️ | Handles turns well, but might lag behind in acceleration. | | Weird Gnome Engineering™ Build 🤪 | Could be brilliant… or explode. DM rolls secretly. |
docs.title: Bobsled Construction Rules

docs.text: Situation Riff Gearwhistle's Take Clank Cogsworth's Response Sleds launch from the start “And we’re off! Look at those sleds FLY—some intentionally, some... not so much.” “If a sled flips before the first turn, does it really count as a race?” Near wipeout in a turn “Ohhh, that was a CLOSE one! That sled was nearly a permanent part of the track!” “Might need to rename this the Bobsled Wreckage Derby! ” Rough landing from a jump “Oof! That’s gotta rattle your screws!” “Not to worry, folks—gnomes bounce! ” Finish line chaos “It’s too close to call! Someone’s sled is literally falling apart but STILL moving!” “That’s what we call winning through duct tape and hope! ”
docs.title: 🎙️ Mechanical Bobsled Race Commentary

docs.text: The bobsled run is a 500-foot course featuring sharp turns, unexpected jumps, and environmental hazards . Successful teams must balance speed and control while navigating obstacles. Section Description Mechanics & DCs 1. The Drop (0-100 ft.) The first 50-foot near-vertical slope launches sleds into high speeds FAST. Athletics (DC 12) to brace or lose control. 2. The Frostbite Chicane (100-250 ft.) A sharp set of twists force teams to steer carefully or risk a wipeout. Dexterity (DC 14) to steer safely. 3. The Mogul Madness (250-350 ft.) Ice humps and gaps shake sleds, testing suspension. Poor builds might crack here! Tinker’s Tools (DC 13) for durability checks. 4. The Avalanche Curve (350-450 ft.) A steep banking turn requires perfect balance—or you flip! Acrobatics (DC 15) to keep upright. 5. The Final Stretch (450-500 ft.) The fastest section— raw speed vs. last-second steering! Final Dexterity (DC 12) OR Strength (DC 14) for a last-second push!
docs.title: The Icy Track Layout

docs.text: Gnomish "Air Fans" Malfunction 🍃: Automated fans meant to reduce wind resistance occasionally fire randomly , boosting or spinning sleds out ( DC 13 Dexterity save ). Tumbling Snow Golems ⛄: A runaway sentient snowball somehow found its way onto the track. A team must dodge it or get slowed down ( DC 14 Acrobatics check ). Sabotage or Defensive Tactics? 🤔: Teams can lean into their build strategy to mess with rivals—use extra weight to bump opponents off course ( contested Strength check ) or fake a steering malfunction ( Deception vs. Insight ). 🏁 Finishing the Race: - First to finish = First to start building their siege launcher in Event 3! - Slower teams get a delayed start , meaning less time to build and launch!
docs.title: Bonus Hazards & Mayhem

docs.text: 🎯 Precision, Power, and a Dash of Chaos! The final event of the Great Tinkertown Winter Triathlon tests not just speed, but ingenuity! After hurtling through the Three-Legged Ice Skating Race and Mechanical Bobsled Race , teams immediately enter a fortified arena where they must construct and use a massive snow-launching contraption to knock down targets before their opponents do! Teams must build their siege weapon from provided materials , then fire at six magical targets to claim victory. Faster teams from the previous event get a head start on construction. 🏁 First team to destroy all their targets wins the Triathlon!
docs.title: Event 3: The Snow Slingshot Siege

docs.text: Each team must construct a snow-launching device: Slingshot (Quick-firing, but lower power). Catapult (Good range, moderate accuracy). Trebuchet (Most powerful, but slowest to reload). Faster bobsled teams get a head start based on their finish order : 🥇 1st place in bobsled race = 10-minute head start 🥈 2nd place = 5-minute head start 🥉 3rd place or later = No delay, start immediately
docs.title: 🏗️ Phase 1: Construction (Time-Based Head Start)

docs.text: Teams describe their design and assign roles. Each player contributes one skill check (or helps another). Three key elements determine launcher quality : Skill Check Effect Intelligence (Tinker’s Tools, Arcana, or Investigation) DC 13+ Design stability – Reduces chance of misfires. Dexterity (Sleight of Hand or Tinker’s Tools) DC 14+ Fine-tuning aim – Improves accuracy on target shots. Strength (Athletics or Raw Construction) DC 12+ Power & durability – Prevents breaking under stress. 🎲 DM Note: If the team rolls exceptionally well (all rolls DC 18+), their launcher gains a +1 bonus on all attack rolls. If they fail multiple checks (more than 2 failures), it starts wobbly and has a 10% chance of misfiring on every shot.
docs.title: 🔧 Building Mechanics

docs.text: Situation Riff Gearwhistle's Take Clank Cogsworth's Response First team starts building “And the first team is already assembling their siege weapon! Looks like… uh… a slingshot? A trebuchet? A gnome’s bad dream?” “Whatever it is, it better work! ” Team struggles with launcher “Ooooh, that does NOT look stable. That’s not a siege weapon, that’s an art installation waiting to collapse! ” “Maybe they’re aiming for style points? ” Perfect shot on a hard target “BOOM! What a hit! That target never saw it coming! ” “Neither did I! I was too busy watching the OTHER team’s slingshot catch fire!” Final shot for the win “They line up the shot… they FIRE… IT HITS!” “WE HAVE OUR WINNERS! And only minor injuries this time!”
docs.title: 🎙️ Snow Slingshot Siege Commentary

docs.text: Once built, teams must fire at 6 magical targets to win. Each turn: 1. A player loads the launcher (no check required). 2. A player aims & fires (Attack Roll required). 3. The shot hits or misses based on target AC. Target Type AC Special Rule Wooden Dummy (Basic Target) 12 Simple, stationary, easy to hit. Enchanted Floating Gear 14 Floats erratically, requires Dex Save (DC 12) on hit to confirm direct impact . Defensive Ice Wall 16 Requires a Strength-based attack to break through. Animated Snowman 14 Moves 5 feet after every hit , forcing new angles. Bouncing Bell Target 18 Disadvantage on attack rolls unless using a powerful launch method . Final “Grand Clocktower” Target 20 Must be hit twice to fully destroy! 💡 Tactical Options: - Fast-firing Slingshot : More chances to hit, but may struggle with armored/moving targets. - Steady Catapult : Balanced power and accuracy. - Heavy Trebuchet : Devastating force, but takes 2 rounds to reload . 🔧 Adjustments & Fixes: - A team member can spend a round fixing issues if their launcher misfires (DC 12 Intelligence or Tinker’s Tools). - Teams can switch shooters if one is struggling. 🚨 Winning Condition: First team to destroy all 6 targets wins the Triathlon!
docs.title: 🎯 Phase 2: Target Practice (Firing the Siege Weapon!)

docs.text: To keep the event dynamic and unpredictable , the following random events may occur: Random Event (Roll d6) Effect 1 - Slippery Ice Patch Someone slips near the launcher! Next shooter rolls Dex Save DC 13 or has Disadvantage . 2 - Referee Interference A gnomish referee runs onto the field screaming “Foul!” before realizing their mistake. Delays one shot. 3 - Sudden Blizzard Visibility drops! All attack rolls made at Disadvantage until the storm passes (1d3 rounds). 4 - Mechanical Malfunction A random team’s launcher misfires , shooting backward instead of forward (must be reset). 5 - Rival Sabotage! Another team’s gnome assistant sneaks up and loosens a hinge —if unnoticed, next shot is wildly inaccurate . (Perception DC 14 to catch them!) 6 - Surprise Extra Target! A new floating “bonus target” (AC 15) appears! Hitting it grants a +1 to all future attack rolls.
docs.title: 🎭 Bonus Chaos & Special Mechanics

docs.text: Speed matters, but so does skill – Rushing through earlier events gets you a head start, but a poorly built launcher could ruin your chances. Different team members shine in different areas – Intelligence for design, Dexterity for aiming, Strength for power. Spectator-friendly excitement – Misfires, random magic mishaps, and comeback moments keep the crowd entertained! A tense, neck-and-neck ending – Since teams fire at different speeds and accuracy varies, no one is ever truly out of the race until the final shot!
docs.title: 🏆 Why This Works as the Final Event

docs.text: 1️⃣ Three-Legged Ice Skating Race ⛸️ ( Agility & Coordination ) → Teams rush to their bobsleds. 2️⃣ Mechanical Bobsled Race 🛷 ( Speed & Engineering ) → Finish order determines Siege building time. 3️⃣ The Snow Slingshot Siege ❄️ ( Strategy, Teamwork, & Accuracy ) → First team to destroy their targets wins!
docs.title: Final Order of Events in The Great Tinkertown Winter Triathlon

docs.text: No Tinkertown festival is complete without over-the-top prizes , some practical, some… not so much.
docs.title: 🥇 1st-3rd Place Prizes

docs.text: 🏆 Title: Tinkertown Triathlon Titans! 🎁 Prize Rewards: - The Golden Gear Trophy 🏆 (An oversized, gaudy, gold-painted mechanical gear that spins on its own. Engraved with the team’s name.) - 250 gp each - A custom "Tinkertown Winter Triathlon Badge" ( Can be attatched to the bottom of shoes where it Grants +10 ft. speed on ice. ) - 1 Free Magical Item from the Wonderarium (DM’s choice of rare trinket or consumable). - Honorary Parade Float in the Next Festival (Their team gets their own parade float next year, complete with an animatronic version of them!) - A lifetime supply of free fries at Brews & Blues. 🍟 ( Fine print: "Lifetime" means until Artie & Bartie get tired of them. )
docs.title: 🥇 1st Place - The Grand Champions

docs.text: 🏅 Title: Silver-Gear Sprinters! 🎁 Prize Rewards: - The Silver-Cog Medals ( Slightly dented, but made with love. ) - 150 gp each - A “Second Best” Enchanted Spoon ( Can magically stir drinks on command. Bartie swears it’s useful. ) - 50% off coupon for Munster Mart’s cheese board platters.
docs.title: 🥈 2nd Place - The Almost Champions

docs.text: 🥉 Title: The Resilient Runners! 🎁 Prize Rewards: - The Bronze Wrench Trophy ( For "enduring mechanical hardship with grace and panic." It squeaks when turned. ) - 75 gp each - A free round of drinks at Brews & Blues. 🍻 (Limit: No more than 2 Blue Bummers in one night.) - A "Slightly Used" Sled from the Race. ( May or may not be fixable. Congratulations! )
docs.title: 🥉 3rd Place - The "Hey, At Least We Finished" Award

docs.text: Because Tinkertown loves a good laugh , additional “honorary” awards are handed out: 🏅 "Best Wipeout" – Given to the team with the most spectacular crash during the race. 🏅 "Most Over-Engineered Sled" – For the team that made a sled so complicated it was practically a mobile house. 🏅 "The Tinker Award" – For the team that built the most creative (or absurd) snow-launching contraption. 🏅 "Audience Favorite" – Voted on by the crowd! The most beloved team gets a custom-made Tinkertown plushie in their honor.
docs.title: 🎭 Extra Fun Awards

docs.text: As the winners are announced , fireworks from The Wonderarium explode above, bathing the festival in shimmering lights. Artie & Bartie lead a Victory Toast at Brews & Blues , where competitors celebrate (or drown their sorrows) . Meanwhile, rumors are already swirling about what wild challenges next year’s Triathlon will bring… 🎆 “Another Tinkertown Triathlon in the books! Now, let’s drink until we forget how bad we were at ice skating!” 🎆
